text:
`GDeflate` decoder reads past the end of its input page (`multiple_decompress_fuzzer`)

`multiple_decompress_fuzzer` found a heap-buffer-overflow read in the `GDeflate` decoder on master ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?REF=master&sha=1df150bae26c5a8149409e27964d577e3c4ac7cd&name_0=NightlyFuzzers&name_1=libFuzzer%20tests), [input](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/REFs/master/1df150bae26c5a8149409e27964d577e3c4ac7cd/nightlyfuzzers/libfuzzer_tests/multiple_decompress_fuzzer/crash-00a28ab7523a854c2df0ad1b1b6ac4d58643e540)):

```
READ of size 4 ... 1 bytes after 30-byte region
#2 deflate_decompress_default contrib/gdeflate/lib/gdeflate_decompress_template.h:289
#4 Chunk::decompress src/Compression/CompressionCodecGDeflate.cpp:93
#7 CompressionCodecMultiple::doDecompressData src/Compression/CompressionCodecMultiple.cpp:256
```

Cause: `ENSURE_BITS` (`contrib/gdeflate/lib/gdeflate_decompress_template.h:61-67`) refills a stream with `get_unaligned_le32(in_next)` and never compares `in_next` with `in_end`; only the stored-block path does (lines 439, 445). The stream start alone refills all 32 streams, 128 bytes, so any page shorter than that is read past its end, and `Chunk::decompress` passes the exact page size. `NVIDIA/libdeflate` branch `gdeflate` is still at the pinned `8ba9502`, so there is no upstream fix. Master only: the codec came with #127422 and is not on 26.10.

Fix: return `LIBDEFLATE_BAD_DATA` from `ENSURE_BITS` when fewer than 4 bytes remain before `in_end` (one line). A valid page should never hit it, since the encoder reserves exactly the packets the decoder refills (`deflate_add_bits`); I will confirm that with round trips at every level and add a guard-page regression test here.

Blocker: `contrib/gdeflate` points at `NVIDIA/libdeflate` directly, and `ClickHouse/libdeflate` (same fork network) has no `gdeflate` branch, so I have nowhere to send the patch.

@thevar1able, A or B?
- A: you create a `gdeflate` branch in `ClickHouse/libdeflate` from `NVIDIA/libdeflate@8ba9502`; I open the one-line PR there, then a PR here that repoints `contrib/gdeflate` and adds the test.
- B: I send the patch to `NVIDIA/libdeflate` first.

text:
Lightweight `UPDATE`s made on 26.8+ silently disappear after a rollback to 26.6: v2 patch parts are detached as `broken-on-start` (`Invalid version of SourcePartsSetForPatch: 1`)

After a rollback from 26.8 (or newer) to 26.6, every patch part written by a lightweight `UPDATE` on the new version fails to load, is moved to `detached/` as `broken-on-start`, and all queries return the pre-update values without any error. The only trace is in the server log: `Part .../patch-...-all_3_3_0_2/ is broken and needs manual correction. Reason: Code: 117. DB::Exception: Invalid version of SourcePartsSetForPatch: 1. (INCORRECT_DATA)`. Upgrading back to 26.8 does not bring the update back, because the part stays detached: it has to be found in `system.detached_parts`, renamed and re-attached by hand (`ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH PART`), and any new data written to the updated rows on 26.6 in the meantime would be overwritten by it.

26.8 switched lightweight updates to the v2 patch part format (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182, reverted in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116005, re-landed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116007 and backported to `26.8` in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116373). The new `MergeTree` setting `patch_parts_version` defaults to `v2`; `PatchPartIndex::writeBinary` writes `static_cast<UInt8>(MergeTreePatchPartsVersion::V2)`, i.e. byte `1`, as the first byte of `source_parts.dat`, followed by the sorting key text, and the patch part itself is sorted by the table's sorting key instead of `(_part, _part_offset)`. 26.6 only knows the v1 layout: `SourcePartsSetForPatch::readBinary` (`src/Storages/MergeTree/PatchParts/SourcePartsSetForPatch.cpp` in `26.6`) throws on any version other than `0`, and the part loader turns that into a detached broken part. `26.6` (latest 26.6.1.2475 included) has no backport of the v2 reader. The 26.8 changelog lists the change as backward incompatible and asks to keep `patch_parts_version = 'v1'` or an old `compatibility` during a rolling upgrade, but says nothing about rollback, and the failure mode (silent loss of acknowledged updates) is much worse than a loud error.

26.10 and master (26.11) also write v2 and read each other's patch parts; rollback 26.10 -> 26.8, 26.11 -> 26.10 and 26.11 -> 26.8 keep the updates. Only 26.6 and older are affected.

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d)
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "
    CREATE DATABASE d ENGINE = Atomic;
    CREATE TABLE d.t (id UInt64, v Int64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id
        SETTINGS enable_block_number_column = 1, enable_block_offset_column = 1;
    INSERT INTO d.t SELECT number, 0 FROM numbers(10)"
clickhouse-26.8 local --path $d -q "UPDATE d.t SET v = 1 WHERE id = 3; SELECT sum(v) FROM d.t"
# 1
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "SELECT sum(v) FROM d.t; SELECT name, reason FROM system.detached_parts WHERE database = 'd'"
# 0
# broken-on-start_patch-c3fd57639ae527f3a846f39739ab3236-all_3_3_0_2	broken-on-start
clickhouse-26.8 local --path $d -q "SELECT sum(v) FROM d.t"
# 0 (still lost after upgrading again)
```

What does work on the 26.8 side: a server-level `compatibility` below 26.8 (`clickhouse-26.8 local --compatibility=26.6`, or `compatibility` in the default profile) makes 26.8 write v1 patch parts, and 26.6 applies them. `ALTER TABLE ... APPLY PATCHES` before the rollback also keeps the data, because the update is then in the base part (26.6 still detaches the stale patch part, harmlessly). The table-level `SETTINGS patch_parts_version = 'v1'` is not a way out: 26.6 then refuses to attach the table with `Unknown setting 'patch_parts_version': for storage MergeTree (UNKNOWN_SETTING)`.

Expected: an acknowledged lightweight `UPDATE` is never silently lost. Proposed fix, in order of preference: (1) backport to `26.6` the ability to read v2 patch parts (the read and apply path of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116007), so 26.8 LTS can be rolled back to 26.6; (2) if that is too large, at least make 26.6 fail loudly instead of detaching: keep the patch part in place and refuse to read or merge the affected partitions (or load the table) with a clear error that names the version mismatch, so the update is never silently missing and comes back on its own after upgrading again; (3) document in the 26.8 changelog that rollback below 26.8 requires `compatibility` below 26.8 for the whole time the new version runs, or `APPLY PATCHES` before the rollback. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/116276 (the same error and silent loss for patch parts from the master builds of the first v2 attempt).

Lightweight updates are `BETA` (`enable_lightweight_update`, enabled by default) in 26.6 and 26.8, and need `enable_block_number_column = 1` and `enable_block_offset_column = 1` on the table. A server running 26.8 with a server-level `compatibility` below 26.8 writes v1 patch parts, which 26.6 reads.

Found by the upgrade/rollback harness, `26.6 -> 26.8 -> 26.6`.

@groeneai please fix this.

text:
Parts with any skip index written by 26.8+ are unreadable and unmergeable on 26.6 after a rollback: `Unknown format (1) of packed data (UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION)`

Any data part that 26.8 or newer writes for a table with at least one skip index (even a single `minmax`) cannot be used by 26.6 after a rollback: `count()`, every `SELECT` with a `WHERE` (also on the primary key, also with `use_skip_indexes = 0`), every merge, and the rows of `system.parts` / `system.columns` for that table fail with `Code: 287. DB::Exception: Unknown format (1) of packed data. (UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION)`. Only a full scan without a filter still works. The failure is not only in index analysis: `IMergeTreeDataPart::calculateColumnsAndSecondaryIndicesSizesOnDiskUnlocked` opens the archive to compute column sizes, which the planner asks for on almost every query. Merges stay blocked until the server is upgraded again, so the partition keeps accumulating parts. No data is lost: the table works again after upgrading back to 26.8.

The packed skip-index archive `skp_idx.packed` was added in 26.6 behind `packed_skip_index_max_bytes` (default 0) with archive index format version 0 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105321). In 26.7, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109272 added a per-file `uncompressed_size` field to the archive index and made the skip-index writer always use the new format version 1 (`PackedFilesIO::VERSION_WITH_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE`, `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk.cpp`, the `finalize` call of `skip_indices_packed_writer`); `statistics.packed` and packed part storage keep writing version 0. In 26.8, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111816 enabled packing by default (`packed_skip_index_max_bytes = 1 MiB`), so from 26.8 on practically every part with a skip index carries a version 1 archive. The 26.6 reader (`PackedFilesReader::readIndex` in `src/IO/PackedFilesReader.cpp`) rejects anything above `PackedFilesIO::VERSION = 0`; it cannot just skip the new field, because each index entry is now 8 bytes longer. `26.6` (latest 26.6.1.2475 included) has no backport of the reader change. The 26.8 changelog entry for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111816 states that the new parts "stay fully readable on older versions", which is not true for 26.6.

26.8 and 26.10 read each other's archives (both use format version 1, `MAX_VERSION = 1`), and master (26.11) archives read fine on 26.10 and 26.8. Only 26.6 is affected.

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d)
clickhouse-26.8 local --path $d -q "
    CREATE DATABASE d ENGINE = Atomic;
    CREATE TABLE d.t (id UInt64, v UInt64, INDEX i v TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id;
    INSERT INTO d.t SELECT number, number FROM numbers(1000)"
ls $d/store/*/*/all_1_1_0/ | grep skp_idx          # skp_idx.packed, first byte 0x01
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "SELECT * FROM d.t WHERE id = 5 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0"
# Code: 287. DB::Exception: Unknown format (1) of packed data. (UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION)
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "SELECT count() FROM d.t"
# Code: 287. DB::Exception: Unknown format (1) of packed data. (UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION)
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "INSERT INTO d.t SELECT number, number FROM numbers(10); OPTIMIZE TABLE d.t FINAL"
# Code: 287. DB::Exception: Unknown format (1) of packed data. (UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION)
clickhouse-26.6 local --path $d -q "SELECT sum(v) FROM d.t"
# 499545 (a full scan without a filter still works)
```

The 26.8 side can avoid it: with a server-level `compatibility` below 26.8 (`clickhouse-26.8 local --compatibility=26.6`, or `compatibility` in the default profile on a server) the `MergeTree` default becomes `packed_skip_index_max_bytes = 0`, parts get the standalone `skp_idx_<name>.idx2` / `.cmrk4` files, and 26.6 reads them. A session-level `SET compatibility = '26.6'` does not help, because `MergeTree` settings come from the server-level default profile. Parts already written with a version 1 archive stay unreadable on 26.6.

Expected: a 26.8 part with a skip index is readable on 26.6, as the changelog promises. Proposed fix: backport the read side of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109272 to `26.6` (accept index format version 1 in `PackedFilesReader::readIndex` and read, or skip, the `uncompressed_size` field). It is a few lines and does not change what 26.6 writes. Also correct the 26.8 changelog entry.

A server-level `compatibility` below 26.8 restores `packed_skip_index_max_bytes = 0` and avoids the problem; a session-level `compatibility` does not.

Found by the upgrade/rollback harness, `26.6 -> 26.8 -> 26.6`.

@groeneai please fix this.

text:
Wide parts with a `Geometry` column written before 26.8 are unreadable after the upgrade: `Stream g.MultiPoint.size0 ... is not found`

### Describe what's wrong

After upgrading from 26.6 (or any version from 25.11, where `Geometry` was introduced, to 26.7) to 26.8 or later, every read of a `Geometry` column from an old wide part fails with a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception:

```
Code: 49. DB::Exception: Stream g.MultiPoint.size0 for column g with type Geometry is not found: (while reading column g): (while reading from part .../all_2_2_0/ ...). (LOGICAL_ERROR)
```

This affects `SELECT` of the column, `variantType(g)`, `g.MultiPoint`, merges (`OPTIMIZE ... FINAL` fails the same way, so on a replicated table the merge stays in the replication queue) and mutations. Columns that nest `Geometry` are affected too: `Array(Geometry)` (`Stream a.MultiPoint.size1 ... is not found`) and `JSON(p Geometry)` (`Stream j.p.MultiPoint.size0 ... is not found`). Reading other columns of the part and other variant subcolumns (`g.Point`, `g.LineString`) works. There is no SQL workaround on 26.8: `ALTER ... MODIFY COLUMN` and `OPTIMIZE` need to read the column. Rolling back to 26.6 makes the data readable again, but a part merged on 26.6 again has no `MultiPoint` streams, so the next upgrade fails again.

Old compact parts read fine for the full column (the `MultiPoint` variant has zero rows in every granule, so nothing is read from the shared stream), but reading the `g.MultiPoint` subcolumn from an old compact part fails with `Unexpected substream g.MultiPoint.size0 for column g` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/DataTypes/Serializations/getSubcolumnsDeserializationOrder.cpp#L53). `Dynamic` columns that stored `Geometry` values are not affected, because `Dynamic` stores the concrete types (`Point`, `LineString`). Explicit `Variant(...)` columns are not affected either (see below).

`Geometry` is not experimental: `allow_experimental_geo_types` is obsolete and the type is available by default since 25.11, so this breaks a regular upgrade of any table with a `Geometry` column in wide parts.

### Root cause

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109951 ("Add MultiPoint data type", in 26.8) added `MultiPoint` to the `Geometry` variant. It keeps the persisted discriminators stable by building the `Variant` with `FixedDiscriminatorOrder` and appending `MultiPoint` as discriminator 6 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/DataTypes/DataTypeCustomGeo.cpp#L289), and its test `04511_geometry_discriminators_compatibility` covers `Native` and `RowBinary`. It does not cover MergeTree parts.

`columns.txt` of a part stores the type by name, `Geometry`. On 26.8 that name resolves to the 7-variant type, so the reader uses the 7-variant serialization for parts that were written with 6 variants and have no `g.MultiPoint.*` files. `SerializationVariant::deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams` asks for the streams of every variant, including those with zero rows to read (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationVariant.cpp#L636), and `MergeTreeReaderWide::getStream` allows a missing stream only for a column or subcolumn that the part does not have (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeReaderWide.cpp#L1218-L1224). Since the part's own type (`Geometry`, resolved with the new definition) has a `MultiPoint` subcolumn, it throws.

The supported way of adding a variant, `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN v Variant(String, UInt64, Float64)` from `Variant(String, UInt64)`, does not hit this: it is a metadata-only change (`canSkipConversionToVariant`, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/Storages/MergeTree/MutateTask.cpp#L4710), old parts keep `Variant(String, UInt64)` in `columns.txt`, they are read with their own serialization and the result is converted to the table type. `Geometry` bypasses this because the type name in the part is unchanged while its definition changed. There is no generic mechanism that treats a missing variant stream as an empty variant.

The 26.8 to 26.10 and 26.10 to master transitions do not change the `Geometry` variant list (7 types in 26.8, 26.10 and master), but any future geo type appended to `Geometry` will break wide parts in the same way unless this is fixed generally.

### How to reproduce

```bash
d=$PWD/geom_repro; rm -rf "$d"; mkdir -p "$d"
clickhouse-26.6 local --path "$d" -q "
CREATE DATABASE d ENGINE = Atomic;
CREATE TABLE d.t (id UInt64, g Geometry) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0;
INSERT INTO d.t SELECT number, [(1., 2.), (3., 4.)]::LineString FROM numbers(3);
INSERT INTO d.t SELECT 10, (1., 2.)::Point;
CREATE TABLE d.a (id UInt64, a Array(Geometry)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0;
INSERT INTO d.a SELECT 1, [(1., 2.)::Point::Geometry];"

clickhouse-26.8 local --path "$d" -q "SELECT id, g.Point FROM d.t ORDER BY id"   # works
clickhouse-26.8 local --path "$d" -q "SELECT * FROM d.t"
# Code: 49. DB::Exception: Stream g.MultiPoint.size0 for column g with type Geometry is not found: (while reading column g) ... (LOGICAL_ERROR)
clickhouse-26.8 local --path "$d" -q "OPTIMIZE TABLE d.t FINAL"
# Code: 49. DB::Exception: Stream g.MultiPoint.size0 for column g with type Geometry is not found ... (LOGICAL_ERROR)
clickhouse-26.8 local --path "$d" -q "SELECT * FROM d.a"
# Code: 49. DB::Exception: Stream a.MultiPoint.size1 for column a with type Array(Geometry) is not found ... (LOGICAL_ERROR)
```

The same happens with 26.10 and current master.

### Expected behaviour

Parts written before `MultiPoint` was added to `Geometry` are readable, mergeable and mutable after the upgrade; the `MultiPoint` variant of such parts is read as empty (no rows have discriminator 6), and `g.MultiPoint` returns empty values.

### Proposed fix

Make `SerializationVariant` tolerate a variant whose streams are absent in the part and treat it as an empty variant:

- In `deserializeBinaryBulkStatePrefix` and `deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams`, before descending into variant `i`, check `settings.check_stream_exists_callback` for the variant element path. If the variant's streams do not exist, skip its prefix and data, leave the variant column empty, and throw `INCORRECT_DATA` only if the discriminators of the range reference that variant (`variant_limits[i] > 0`). The existing size check after the loop (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationVariant.cpp#L642) already reports that case. Bucketed `Map` uses the same callback to handle a stream that old parts do not have (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0ea6ec133ccc/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationMap.cpp#L948).
- Set `check_stream_exists_callback` in `MergeTreeReaderWide` for data reads (not only for prefixes), so the wide reader does not reach the `Stream ... is not found` exception for such a variant, and handle the same case in `getSubcolumnsDeserializationOrder` for compact parts with `columns_substreams.txt`.
- Do the same for subcolumn reads (`SerializationVariantElement`, `g.MultiPoint`), which should return an empty column for the missing variant.
- Add a backward compatibility test with a wide part and a compact part written by a pre-`MultiPoint` version (or written with the 6-variant layout), covering `SELECT *`, `variantType`, `g.MultiPoint`, `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`, `Array(Geometry)` and `JSON(p Geometry)`.

An alternative that is local to `Geometry` (for example persisting the concrete `Variant(...)` type in `columns.txt`, or deriving the variant list of an old part from the files it has) would also fix this, but the generic reader change also protects any future type appended to `Geometry`.

Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109951

@groeneai please fix this.

text:
Vector similarity index returns wrong or no neighbours on 26.6 when a part has more than one index granule, fixed on 26.7 and later, needs a backport

On 26.6 a `vector_similarity` index returns wrong rows, wrong `_distance` values, or fewer rows than `LIMIT` whenever a data part contains more than one vector index granule, i.e. when the index is declared with an explicit `GRANULARITY N` and the part has more than `N` table granules. The default `GRANULARITY` (100 million) is not affected, because then every part has a single index granule. 26.7, 26.8, 26.10 and master return the correct result.

The bug was found by an upgrade test: a top-3 query over 256 rows with `index_granularity = 32` and `GRANULARITY 2` returns ids `[44,57,38]` on 26.6.1.2475, while the exact answer (and the answer of 26.8) is `[77,48,149]`.

### Root cause

The HNSW keys inside a vector index granule are row numbers relative to the start of that index granule (`index_size + row` in `updateImpl`, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/26.6/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexVectorSimilarity.cpp#L416).

In `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterMarksUsingIndex` on the 26.6 branch (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/26.6/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp#L2329) the result of `calculateApproximateNearestNeighbors` is assigned to `read_hints.vector_search_results` once per index granule:

```cpp
read_hints.vector_search_results = condition->calculateApproximateNearestNeighbors(granule);
```

This has two defects:

1. Each index granule overwrites the previous one, so only the hits of the last index granule of the part survive in the read hints.
2. The rows are stored as granule-relative row numbers, but `MergeTreeRangeReader::fillDistanceColumnAndFilterForVectorSearch` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/26.6/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeRangeReader.cpp#L1271) compares them with `_part_offset` and fills `_distance` from them.

The mark ranges are computed correctly (`countMarksForRows` is called relative to the index granule start), so the reader reads the right marks, but the row filter and the `_distance` column are built from the last index granule's relative row numbers. Depending on the data, the query returns rows of the first index granule with distances of another row (wrong ids and wrong `_distance`), or nothing at all when the relative row numbers do not fall into the marks that are read (fewer rows than `LIMIT`, including an empty result).

The fix is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108846 (re-land of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105591, which was reverted by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108812). Its `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp` hunk resets `read_hints.vector_search_results` per part, accumulates the hits of all index granules and shifts every row by `getMarkStartingRow(index_mark * skip_index_granularity)`:

```cpp
const size_t first_row_in_index_granule = part->index_granularity->getMarkStartingRow(index_mark * skip_index_granularity);
for (size_t result_pos = 0; result_pos < vector_search_results.rows.size(); ++result_pos)
{
    accumulated_results->rows.push_back(first_row_in_index_granule + vector_search_results.rows[result_pos]);
    accumulated_results->distances->push_back(distances[result_pos]);
}
```

That PR is labelled `pr-performance` (its main purpose is row-level candidate filtering for `vector_search_with_rescoring = 1`), so it was not backported. It is in 26.7 (`26.7.1.1181`) and later. The 26.6 branch still has the old code, and I found no backport PR. The same code is present on 25.8, 26.3, 26.4 and 26.5.

### Repro

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, vec Array(Float32), INDEX idx vec TYPE vector_similarity('hnsw', 'L2Distance', 2) GRANULARITY 1)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 4;

-- Two table granules (rows 0-3 and 4-7), so two vector index granules. Row i has the vector [i, i].
INSERT INTO t SELECT number, [toFloat32(number), toFloat32(number)] FROM numbers(8);

-- The nearest row to [7, 7] is id 7, in the second index granule.
SELECT 'ann', id, L2Distance(vec, [7., 7.]) AS d FROM t ORDER BY d LIMIT 1;
SELECT 'exact', id, L2Distance(vec, [7., 7.]) AS d FROM t ORDER BY d LIMIT 1 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0;
```

Actual on 26.6.1.2475:

```
ann	3	0
exact	7	0
```

Expected (26.7 and later):

```
ann	7	0
exact	7	0
```

The row with granule-relative number 3 of the second index granule is mapped to part offset 3, i.e. id 3, and gets its distance (0). Other variants on 26.6:

- `ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 1` returns id 0 with distance `5.656...` (the distance of id 4).
- `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 3` with the reference vector `[7., 7.]` returns `[3,2,1]` instead of `[7,6,5]`.
- With `GRANULARITY 3` over 16 rows (`index_granularity = 4`) the query with `[15., 15.]` returns no rows at all instead of id 15.

What does not change the result: `index_granularity` (only the number of index granules per part matters), `max_threads`, `vector_search_index_fetch_multiplier`, `max_limit_for_vector_search_queries`, `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`, `vector_search_filter_strategy = 'postfilter'` with a `WHERE`. Each part is handled separately, so a table whose parts each fit into one index granule is correct (two parts of 4 rows each return the right answer, the same rows after `OPTIMIZE TABLE t FINAL` into one part do not).

Workarounds on 26.6: `SETTINGS vector_search_with_rescoring = 1` (exact distances are computed from the full-precision vectors, the read hints are not used), `vector_search_filter_strategy = 'prefilter'` with a `WHERE`, or the default `GRANULARITY` of the index.

### Proposed action

Backport the fix to 26.6. Since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108846 is a performance change with follow-ups (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111003, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119371), the preferred backport is only its `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterMarksUsingIndex` hunk (per-part reset, accumulation over index granules, shift by `first_row_in_index_granule`), plus a stateless test with the repro above. The supported LTS branches 26.3 and 25.8 have the same code and need the same backport.

@groeneai please fix this.

The 26.6 branch still has the old code, and I found no backport PR. The same code is present on 25.8, 26.3, 26.4 and 26.5.

### Repro

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, vec Array(Float32), INDEX idx vec TYPE vector_similarity('hnsw', 'L2Distance', 2) GRANULARITY 1)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 4;

-- Two table granules (rows 0-3 and 4-7), so two vector index granules. Row i has the vector [i, i].
INSERT INTO t SELECT number, [toFloat32(number), toFloat32(number)] FROM numbers(8);

-- The nearest row to [7, 7] is id 7, in the second index granule.
SELECT 'ann', id, L2Distance(vec, [7., 7.]) AS d FROM t ORDER BY d LIMIT 1;
SELECT 'exact', id, L2Distance(vec, [7., 7.]) AS d FROM t ORDER BY d LIMIT 1 SETTINGS use_skip_indexes = 0;
```

Actual on 26.6.1.2475:

```
ann	3	0
exact	7	0
```

Expected (26.7 and later):

```
ann	7	0
exact	7	0
```

The row with granule-relative number 3 of the second index granule is mapped to part offset 3, i.e. id 3, and gets its distance (0). Other variants on 26.6:

- `ORDER BY L2Distance(vec, [0., 0.]) LIMIT 1` returns id 0 with distance `5.656...` (the distance of id 4).
- `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 3` with the reference vector `[7., 7.]` returns `[3,2,1]` instead of `[7,6,5]`.
- With `GRANULARITY 3` over 16 rows (`index_granularity = 4`) the query with `[15., 15.]` returns no rows at all instead of id 15.

What does not change the result: `index_granularity` (only the number of index granules per part matters), `max_threads`, `vector_search_index_fetch_multiplier`, `max_limit_for_vector_search_queries`, `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization`, `vector_search_filter_strategy = 'postfilter'` with a `WHERE`. Each part is handled separately, so a table whose parts each fit into one index granule is correct (two parts of 4 rows each return the right answer, the same rows after `OPTIMIZE TABLE t FINAL` into one part do not).

Workarounds on 26.6: `SETTINGS vector_search_with_rescoring = 1` (exact distances are computed from the full-precision vectors, the read hints are not used), `vector_search_filter_strategy = 'prefilter'` with a `WHERE`, or the default `GRANULARITY` of the index.

### Proposed action

Backport the fix to 26.6. Since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108846 is a performance change with follow-ups (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111003, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119371), the preferred backport is only its `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterMarksUsingIndex` hunk (per-part reset, accumulation over index granules, shift by `first_row_in_index_granule`), plus a stateless test with the repro above. The supported LTS branches 26.3 and 25.8 have the same code and need the same backport.

@groeneai please fix this.

text:
PUT upload INSERT fails with SYNTAX_ERROR for table or database named `function`

### Describe what's wrong

- PUT upload into a database or table named `function` always fails with SYNTAX_ERROR; GET on the same path works.
- Trigger: PUT /function/t.CSV or PUT /function.CSV?database=db, even though the table exists and INSERT INTO `function`.t works over the native protocol.
- Expected the upload to insert the rows; instead it is rejected with a SYNTAX_ERROR and no workaround exists via the URL.
- Back-quoting the database in the URL doesn't help, and a back-quoted last path component isn't routed at all (HTTP 501).

Root cause: `HTTPHandler.cpp:1050-1052` builds `qualified_table` with `backQuoteIfNeed` instead of `backQuote`, so the keyword `function` is left unquoted. `ParserInsertQuery.cpp:110` then treats `FUNCTION` after `INSERT INTO` as the table-function keyword, breaking the generated `INSERT INTO function.t FORMAT CSV` query.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `HTTPHandler::processQuery` builds `qualified_table` with `backQuoteIfNeed` (`HTTPHandler.cpp:1050`/`1052`), which leaves `function` bare because it is a valid identifier, then generates `INSERT INTO function.t FORMAT CSV` (`HTTPHandler.cpp:1122`). `ParserInsertQuery` consumes `FUNCTION` after `INSERT INTO` as the table-function keyword (`ParserInsertQuery.cpp:110`) and fails on the following `.t` / `FORMAT`. The `GET` path splices the same string into `SELECT * FROM function.t`, which parses.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Server/HTTPHandler.cpp:1050`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1df150bae26c5a/src/Server/HTTPHandler.cpp#L1050) — `qualified_table` built with `backQuoteIfNeed` for database and table
- [`src/Server/HTTPHandler.cpp:1122`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1df150bae26c5a/src/Server/HTTPHandler.cpp#L1122) — path upload splices `qualified_table` into `INSERT INTO ... FORMAT ...`
- [`src/Parsers/ParserInsertQuery.cpp:110`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1df150bae26c5a/src/Parsers/ParserInsertQuery.cpp#L110) — `FUNCTION` after `INSERT INTO` switches to the table-function form
- [`src/Server/HTTPQueryConstructor.cpp:341`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1df150bae26c5a/src/Server/HTTPQueryConstructor.cpp#L341) — router rejects a back-quoted last component for `PUT`, so the table cannot be quoted in the URL

Impact: Uploads into a database named `function`, or unqualified uploads into a table named `function`, are refused with a loud `SYNTAX_ERROR`; no rows are written. The only workaround is the regular `POST ?query=INSERT INTO `function`...` form.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Create a database or table named `function` and PUT data to it; the back-quoted URL form (%60function%60) is also rejected because the router returns HTTP 501 for a quoted last path component.

```bash
# A path-table PUT upload must insert into a table named `function`.

BASE_URL="${CLICKHOUSE_PORT_HTTP_PROTO}://${CLICKHOUSE_HOST}:${CLICKHOUSE_PORT_HTTP}"

clickhouse-client -q "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS \`function\`"
clickhouse-client -q "CREATE TABLE \`function\` (a UInt32) ENGINE = Memory"

printf '1\n' | curl -sS -sS -X PUT --data-binary @- "${BASE_URL}/function.CSV?database=default" | grep -o 'SYNTAX_ERROR'
printf '2\n' | curl -sS -sS -X PUT --data-binary @- "${BASE_URL}/default/function.CSV"
clickhouse-client -q "SELECT a FROM \`function\` ORDER BY a"

clickhouse-client -q "DROP TABLE \`function\`"
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

PUT upload into a table or database literally named `function` should insert the data just like the native protocol INSERT does.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
1
2
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The generated INSERT query leaves `function` unquoted, so the parser treats it as the table-function keyword and the request fails with SYNTAX_ERROR.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
SYNTAX_ERROR
2
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Build `qualified_table` with `backQuote` instead of `backQuoteIfNeed` (both parts). `implicit_table_at_top_level` already parses the value as a quoted compound identifier and `SELECT * FROM` accepts quoted names, so always quoting is safe for the `GET` path too. No functional trade-off; the setting value in logs is always back-quoted. The regression case fits as two lines in `05029_http_put_table_upload.sh`.

</details>

### Additional context

Found during automated review of [PR #115849](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115849); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P3 · Finding `h_pr115849_001`


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128581
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1435-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
groupArraySorted over floats with NaN drops real values, and the result depends on N

**Describe what's wrong**

`groupArraySorted(N)` over `Float32` or `Float64` with NaN values returns a result that depends on `N`. With small `N`, NaN comes first and pushes real values out. With larger `N`, NaN ends up last, but real values are still missing.

```sql
SELECT groupArraySorted(3)(x) FROM values('x Float64', (nan), (3), (-inf), (1));
-- [nan,-inf,1]

SELECT arraySlice(arraySort(groupArray(x)), 1, 3) FROM values('x Float64', (nan), (3), (-inf), (1));
-- [-inf,1,3]

SELECT
    groupArraySorted(200)(x) = arraySlice(arraySort(groupArray(x)), 1, 200),
    arrayCount(v -> isNaN(v), groupArraySorted(200)(x))
FROM (SELECT if(number % 100 = 0, nan, toFloat64(sipHash64(number) % 1000000)) AS x FROM numbers(2000));
-- 0    20
```

In the second query, the 20 NaNs are at positions 181 to 200, and 20 of the 200 smallest real values are missing.

**Does it reproduce on the most recent release?**

Yes, on master (26.11.1.986).

**Expected behavior**

The result equals `arraySlice(arraySort(groupArray(x)), 1, N)`, with NaN last, as in `arraySort` and `ORDER BY`. For `Tuple(Float64)` the function already puts NaN last.

**Additional context**

The comparator in `AggregateFunctionGroupArraySorted.cpp` treats NaN as the smallest value, so the heap keeps NaN. The radix sort fallback in `sortAndLimit` then puts NaN after `+inf`.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128555
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1180-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
parseDateTimeBestEffort('Nov-08-2024') returns a wrong date: the day after a month name is read as a time zone offset

**Describe what's wrong**

`parseDateTimeBestEffort` returns a wrong date, with no error, when a month name is followed by a dash and a day. The same date with spaces, or with the day first, parses correctly.

```sql
SELECT parseDateTimeBestEffort('Nov-08-2024', 'UTC');
-- 2026-11-02 04:24:00   (on 2026-11-01)

SELECT parseDateTimeBestEffort('Nov 08 2024', 'UTC');
-- 2024-11-08 00:00:00

SELECT parseDateTimeBestEffort('08-Nov-2024', 'UTC');
-- 2024-11-08 00:00:00

SELECT parseDateTimeBestEffort('Nov/08/2024', 'UTC');
-- Code: 6. Cannot parse string 'Nov/08/2024' as DateTime
```

`'November-08-2024'`, `'Nov-08-24'` and `'Nov-2024'` are also wrong. Schema inference reads `'Nov-08-2024'` as `String`, while `'Nov 08 2024'` is inferred as `DateTime`.

**Does it reproduce on the most recent release?**

Yes, on master (26.11.1.986).

**Expected behavior**

`'Nov-08-2024'` returns `2024-11-08 00:00:00`, the same as `'Nov 08 2024'`.

**Additional context**

After the month name, `-08` is read as a time zone offset of -08:00, and `-2024` as a second offset of -20:24. The two are added, the year falls back to the current year, and the day to 1.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128554
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1181-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
Server crash building projection with `WHERE` on `Tuple` equality

### Describe what's wrong

- An `INSERT` into a `MergeTree` table with a projection filtering `tup = (1, 2)` on a `Tuple` column kills the server.
- Trigger: projection `WHERE` equality to a `Tuple` constant (non-`String`/`Float`/`Decimal` elements) with `optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 1`; `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` crashes too.
- Expected the projection to hold 2 rows; instead the process dies with SIGBUS (exit code 135) on aarch64 `RelWithDebInfo`.
- The persisted mutation from `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` crashes the server again on every restart until removed.

Root cause: `FilterTransform::applyConstantColumnsAfterFilter` turns `tup` into a `ColumnConst`, and `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery` returns the block unmaterialized, so `writeProjectionPartImpl` calls `infos.add(block)` before `MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk::prepareBlockForWriting` materializes it. `SerializationInfoTuple::add` then does `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>` (a plain `static_cast` in release) on the `ColumnConst`.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `FilterTransform::applyConstantColumnsAfterFilter` (FilterTransform.cpp:527) turns `tup` into `ColumnConst` inside the projection query -> `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery` returns the block unmaterialized (ProjectionsDescription.cpp:1128) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeProjectionPartImpl` calls `infos.add(block)` (MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:1304) -> `SerializationInfoTuple::add` does `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>(column)` (SerializationInfoTuple.cpp:53), a plain `static_cast` in release, on a `ColumnConst`.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:1304`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L1304) — `infos.add(block)` on the unmaterialized projection block
- [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationInfoTuple.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationInfoTuple.cpp#L53) — `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>(column)` gets a `ColumnConst`
- [`src/Processors/Transforms/FilterTransform.cpp:527`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Processors/Transforms/FilterTransform.cpp#L527) — PR replaces the filtered column with `ColumnConst` at runtime
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk.cpp:660`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk.cpp#L660) — PR's materialization runs too late (inside the writer)
- [`src/Storages/ProjectionsDescription.cpp:1128`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/ProjectionsDescription.cpp#L1128) — projection block returned without materialization

Impact: The whole server process dies on a valid `INSERT`. After `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` (and any merge or mutation that rebuilds the projection), the persisted mutation crashes the server again on every restart until it is removed. The trigger needs a projection with `WHERE` on an equality to a `Tuple` constant whose elements are not `String`, `Float` or `Decimal`.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

With `optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 0` the same statements succeed.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/1b0c9c1d-fa17-4078-ac94-25954369ccc5)

```sql
-- Test: a projection filtered by equality on a Tuple column is built on INSERT and on MATERIALIZE PROJECTION
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_proj_tuple_eq;
SET optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 1;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_proj_tuple_eq;

CREATE TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq
(
    k UInt64,
    tup Tuple(UInt64, UInt64),
    PROJECTION p (SELECT k, tup WHERE tup = (1, 2) ORDER BY k)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k
SETTINGS ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization = 0.9375;

INSERT INTO t_proj_tuple_eq VALUES (1, (1, 2)), (2, (3, 4)), (3, (1, 2));

ALTER TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq MATERIALIZE PROJECTION p SETTINGS mutations_sync = 1;

SELECT sum(rows) FROM system.projection_parts
WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_proj_tuple_eq' AND name = 'p' AND active;

SELECT k, tup FROM t_proj_tuple_eq ORDER BY k;

DROP TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq;
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

The `INSERT` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` succeed and the projection holds 2 rows.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2
1	(1,2)
2	(3,4)
3	(1,2)
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The server process dies with a Bus error (signal 7) and no rows are written.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
(version 26.11.1.1039 (official build), build id: E1666EB1B30778781B2253A9D32D5E896BC984CF, git hash: bd714c65710bf328d7ae3a4eea30b8dfe0aa2d00) (from thread 658507) (query_id: 50379ad9-8863-4ef3-8b8f-b141e0e997e8) (query: INSERT INTO t_proj_tuple_eq VALUES ) Received signal Bus error (7)
Address: . Access: <not available>. Invalid address alignment.
Stack trace: 0x00000000112c9d60 0x0000000011522b
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Materialize the projection block before anything reads it: convert `ColumnConst` columns to full at the end of `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery`, or before `infos.add(block)` in `writeProjectionPartImpl`. The first option also covers the sort, row-order and `mergeBlock` steps that read the block. It costs one copy of the constant column per projection block. Add the `Tuple` case to `04501_constant_column_after_filter_mergetree_write.sql`.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Merges with `deduplicate_merge_projection_mode = 'rebuild'` reach the same `writeTempProjectionPart` path (MergeTask.cpp:1809). Not run, but it is the same call.

title: Server crash building projection with `WHERE` on `Tuple` equality
body:
### Describe what's wrong

- An `INSERT` into a `MergeTree` table with a projection filtering `tup = (1, 2)` on a `Tuple` column kills the server.
- Trigger: projection `WHERE` equality to a `Tuple` constant (non-`String`/`Float`/`Decimal` elements) with `optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 1`; `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` crashes too.
- Expected the projection to hold 2 rows; instead the process dies with SIGBUS (exit code 135) on aarch64 `RelWithDebInfo`.
- The persisted mutation from `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` crashes the server again on every restart until removed.

Root cause: `FilterTransform::applyConstantColumnsAfterFilter` turns `tup` into a `ColumnConst`, and `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery` returns the block unmaterialized, so `writeProjectionPartImpl` calls `infos.add(block)` before `MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk::prepareBlockForWriting` materializes it. `SerializationInfoTuple::add` then does `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>` (a plain `static_cast` in release) on the `ColumnConst`.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `FilterTransform::applyConstantColumnsAfterFilter` (FilterTransform.cpp:527) turns `tup` into `ColumnConst` inside the projection query -> `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery` returns the block unmaterialized (ProjectionsDescription.cpp:1128) -> `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeProjectionPartImpl` calls `infos.add(block)` (MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:1304) -> `SerializationInfoTuple::add` does `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>(column)` (SerializationInfoTuple.cpp:53), a plain `static_cast` in release, on a `ColumnConst`.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp:1304`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataWriter.cpp#L1304) — `infos.add(block)` on the unmaterialized projection block
- [`src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationInfoTuple.cpp:53`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/DataTypes/Serializations/SerializationInfoTuple.cpp#L53) — `assert_cast<const ColumnTuple &>(column)` gets a `ColumnConst`
- [`src/Processors/Transforms/FilterTransform.cpp:527`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Processors/Transforms/FilterTransform.cpp#L527) — PR replaces the filtered column with `ColumnConst` at runtime
- [`src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk.cpp:660`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartWriterOnDisk.cpp#L660) — PR's materialization runs too late (inside the writer)
- [`src/Storages/ProjectionsDescription.cpp:1128`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/fb7b6cbff26d8e/src/Storages/ProjectionsDescription.cpp#L1128) — projection block returned without materialization

Impact: The whole server process dies on a valid `INSERT`. After `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` (and any merge or mutation that rebuilds the projection), the persisted mutation crashes the server again on every restart until it is removed. The trigger needs a projection with `WHERE` on an equality to a `Tuple` constant whose elements are not `String`, `Float` or `Decimal`.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

With `optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 0` the same statements succeed.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/1b0c9c1d-fa17-4078-ac94-25954369ccc5)

```sql
-- Test: a projection filtered by equality on a Tuple column is built on INSERT and on MATERIALIZE PROJECTION
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_proj_tuple_eq;
SET optimize_constant_columns_after_filter = 1;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_proj_tuple_eq;

CREATE TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq
(
    k UInt64,
    tup Tuple(UInt64, UInt64),
    PROJECTION p (SELECT k, tup WHERE tup = (1, 2) ORDER BY k)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k
SETTINGS ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization = 0.9375;

INSERT INTO t_proj_tuple_eq VALUES (1, (1, 2)), (2, (3, 4)), (3, (1, 2));

ALTER TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq MATERIALIZE PROJECTION p SETTINGS mutations_sync = 1;

SELECT sum(rows) FROM system.projection_parts
WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND table = 't_proj_tuple_eq' AND name = 'p' AND active;

SELECT k, tup FROM t_proj_tuple_eq ORDER BY k;

DROP TABLE t_proj_tuple_eq;
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

The `INSERT` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` succeed and the projection holds 2 rows.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2
1	(1,2)
2	(3,4)
3	(1,2)
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The server process dies with a Bus error (signal 7) and no rows are written.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
(version 26.11.1.1039 (official build), build id: E1666EB1B30778781B2253A9D32D5E896BC984CF, git hash: bd714c65710bf328d7ae3a4eea30b8dfe0aa2d00) (from thread 658507) (query_id: 50379ad9-8863-4ef3-8b8f-b141e0e997e8) (query: INSERT INTO t_proj_tuple_eq VALUES ) Received signal Bus error (7)
Address: . Access: <not available>. Invalid address alignment.
Stack trace: 0x00000000112c9d60 0x0000000011522b
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Materialize the projection block before anything reads it: convert `ColumnConst` columns to full at the end of `ProjectionDescription::calculateByQuery`, or before `infos.add(block)` in `writeProjectionPartImpl`. The first option also covers the sort, row-order and `mergeBlock` steps that read the block. It costs one copy of the constant column per projection block. Add the `Tuple` case to `04501_constant_column_after_filter_mergetree_write.sql`.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Merges with `deduplicate_merge_projection_mode = 'rebuild'` reach the same `writeTempProjectionPart` path (MergeTask.cpp:1809). Not run, but it is the same call.

Found during automated review of [PR #105541](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105541); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr105541_101`

text:
Sort-order-aware join ordering: let DPsub choose `full_sorting_merge` by cost when join inputs are sorted (interesting orders)

### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Use case

Joining large `MergeTree` tables on (a prefix of) their sorting key is common: fact-to-fact joins, several tables sharing a primary key, multi-tenant tables sorted by `(tenant_id, id)`. When both inputs are sorted by the join key, `full_sorting_merge` streams them with bounded memory: the pre-join sorts become `FinishSorting` and the join is sharded by key ranges. A hash join instead materializes the whole build side in memory.

Today the join order optimizer never takes sortedness into account. `DPsub` costs every join as a hash join, the algorithm comes from the `join_algorithm` list, and `full_sorting_merge` is only used when the user forces it. A chain of joins on one key also loses its order between joins, because the join order is chosen without knowing which order a later merge join could reuse.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Make `DPsub` aware of interesting orders (Selinger-style) and let it choose, per join, between a hash join and `full_sorting_merge` by cost:

- Detect which join-key columns each `MergeTree` input can be read in order of, using the same check `optimizeReadInOrder` applies.
- Keep, for every subset of tables, the cheapest plan and the cheapest plan per sort order (equivalence class of join keys) that a later join can still use. The search stays exhaustive, so the result is the cheapest plan under the cost model with sortedness included, e.g. a slightly more expensive merge join whose sorted output lets the next join skip its sort.
- Cost model calibrated on measurements: a merge join wins only when its inputs are already sorted and the build side is large. Plans without sorted inputs are unchanged. The hash alternative accounts for the join runtime filter, which prunes the granules of a sorted probe side when the build keys cover a narrow key range.
- A join chosen as a merge join runs as `full_sorting_merge` (the `join_algorithm` list stays as its fallback), keeps its sides, and builds its key condition on the columns its inputs are sorted by, so the sort order survives through chains and bushy trees.
- Opt-in experimental setting `query_plan_join_order_use_interesting_orders` (default `false`); with it off, behaviour and planning time are the same as before.

First version: inner equi-joins with `ALL` strictness, `DPsub` only, requires `enable_join_transitive_predicates`.

Measured on a Release build with jemalloc, 32 cores, synthetic data (setting off vs on, identical results in every case):

| Scenario | Speedup | Peak memory |
|---|---:|---:|
| 6-table chain on one key, 20M rows each | 2.2x | 10x less |
| Composite key `(tenant_id, id)`, 50M x 50M | 2.7x | 15x less |
| TPC-H-shaped `lineitem ⋈ orders ⋈ shipments`, SF10 sizes | 1.6x | 4.8x less |
| `events ⋈ users`, 100M x 20M | 1.15x | 6.4x less |
| Wide build side under `max_memory_usage = 2 GB` | fails today, 0.3 s with the setting | 263 MiB |

Small build sides, unsorted tables, small dimension tables and narrow build key ranges (where the runtime filter wins) keep the hash join. The join order search takes 3-5% longer for a 12-table star and 11% longer for a 12-table chain on one key (the worst case for `DPsub`).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

A conditional `join_algorithm` token that picks `full_sorting_merge` whenever both inputs are sorted (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109045, https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112973). It works with every join order algorithm and covers `LEFT`/`ANY` joins, but it decides per join after the join order is fixed and always prefers the merge join when inputs are sorted. The measurements in #109045 show that a merge join on sorted inputs can still be slower than a hash join, and a hash join with a runtime filter can be much faster when the build keys cover a narrow range; deciding by cost inside the join order search handles both, and can pick an order that keeps a chain sorted. The two approaches can complement each other.

### Additional context

Known limitations: without column statistics (`use_statistics = 0`) a narrow build key range is not detected; outer joins and orders required by `ORDER BY`/`GROUP BY` above the joins are not considered yet.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109045
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112973
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109005

text:
Analyzer: hashing a subquery column walks the whole subquery, GROUP BY passes over a wide CTE spend seconds in `getTreeHash`

**Describe the situation**

`IQueryTreeNode::getTreeHash` of a `ColumnNode` includes the subtree of the column source (the weak pointer to the `TableNode` / `QueryNode` the column comes from). For a table that is cheap. For a subquery or CTE it is the whole subquery body. Every hash-keyed container of expressions in the analyzer passes rebuilds `QueryTreeNodeWithHash` on each `contains` / `insert` / `find`, so each lookup of a key that is a column of a subquery costs the size of that subquery.

A `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS` over a CTE of 16 columns, each a ~250-node expression, with 32 sets of 15 keys takes 1.6 s, of which 1.5 s is `QueryAnalysisMicroseconds`. The same query over the materialized CTE takes 8 ms. The time is linear in the number of key occurrences: 8 sets take 0.56 s.

Profile of the 32-set query (CPU, 1 ms period, 3 runs, inclusive samples):

| frame | share |
|---|---|
| `QueryTreePassManager::run` | 91% |
| `IQueryTreeNode::getTreeHash` | 90% |
| `GroupingFunctionsResolvePass::run` | 56% |
| `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass::run` | 34% |
| `Planner::buildPlanForQueryNode` | 2% |
| `QueryAnalysisPass::run` | 1% |

The two GROUP BY passes dominate this query because they hash every key of every set up to 4 times (`used_keys_in_set.contains` + `insert`, `aggregation_key_to_index.contains` + `emplace`; key set built on both visitor traversals). The same pattern exists in every other pass that keeps a set or map of expressions. Counting nodes visited by `getTreeHash` per query on a 32-column subquery of ~7700 nodes (one query per optimization, each a single statement):

| what the query does | nodes hashed per query |
|---|---|
| `GROUP BY` with `group_by_use_nulls = 1` (`nullable_group_by_keys` in `IdentifierResolveScope`) | 2.5M |
| `WHERE (c = 1 OR c = 2 OR c = 3) AND ...` (`LogicalExpressionOptimizerPass`) | 2.0M |
| `grouping()` over GROUPING SETS (`GroupingFunctionsResolvePass`) | 1.5M |
| `min(k)` of a key (`AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass`) | 1.5M |
| `LIMIT 1 BY toString(k)` (`OptimizeLimitByInjectiveFunctionsPass`) | 1.5M |
| correlated subquery (`QueryNode::getCorrelatedColumnsSet`) | 1.5M |
| `LIKE` chain (`ConvertOrLikeChainPass`) | 1.3M |
| `ORDER BY k, toString(k)` (`OptimizeRedundantFunctionsInOrderByPass`) | 0.75M |
| `sum(c), count(c), avg(c)` with `optimize_syntax_fuse_functions` (`FuseFunctionsPass`) | 0.75M |
| `GROUP BY k1 + k2, k1, k2` (`OptimizeGroupByFunctionKeysPass`) | 0.63M |
| `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL INTERPOLATE` (`ValidationUtils`) | 0.29M |
| `LEFT JOIN` with `join_use_nulls = 1` (`join_columns_with_changed_types`) | 0.26M |

The tree has 8k nodes; a query hashes it 30 to 300 times over.

**How to reproduce**

Versions: master (9556ebaa51c, 26.10.1.1) and every release with the analyzer; measured on 25.8 and master.

- master at 9556ebaa51c (26.10.1.1), Release build, single node, `max_threads` default, `enable_analyzer = 1` (the only analyzer there).
- The generator below writes the queries (`python3 gen.py <dir>` gives `cte_8.sql`, `cte_32.sql`, `table_setup.sql`, `table_8.sql`, `table_32.sql`). Shape:

```sql
WITH src AS (SELECT number,
    intDiv((intDiv((number + 0), 1) + 1), 1) ... AS c0,   -- 16 columns, each ~250 nodes
    ...
  FROM numbers(10))
SELECT c0, ..., c15, sum(number), min(c0)
FROM src
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (c0, c1, ..., c14),
    (c1, c2, ..., c15),
    ...                       -- 32 sets of 15 keys
)
FORMAT Null
```

- Control: `CREATE TABLE src_t ENGINE = Memory AS <the same SELECT>` and run the outer query `FROM src_t`.

<details><summary>gen.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproduction for: analyzer hashes the whole column source for every GROUP BY key lookup.
Writes <out>/cte_<sets>.sql (keys are columns of a wide CTE) and <out>/table_<sets>.sql (same keys, CTE body materialized)."""
import sys
out = sys.argv[1]
def expr(i, n):
    e = f"number + {i}"
    for j in range(n):
        e = f"({e} + {j % 7 + 1})" if j % 2 else f"intDiv({e}, 1)"
    return e
width, nodes, keys = 16, 250, 16
cols = ",\n    ".join(f"{expr(i, nodes)} AS c{i}" for i in range(width))
key_names = [f"c{i}" for i in range(keys)]
body = f"SELECT number,\n    {cols}\n  FROM numbers(10)"
open(f"{out}/table_setup.sql", "w").write(f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS src_t;\nCREATE TABLE src_t ENGINE = Memory AS {body};\n")
for sets in (8, 32):
    gs = ",\n    ".join("(" + ", ".join(key_names[(s + j) % keys] for j in range(keys - 1)) + ")" for s in range(sets))
    tail = f"GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (\n    {gs}\n)\nFORMAT Null"
    open(f"{out}/cte_{sets}.sql", "w").write(f"WITH src AS ({body})\nSELECT {', '.join(key_names)}, sum(number), min(c0)\nFROM src\n{tail}")
    open(f"{out}/table_{sets}.sql", "w").write(f"SELECT {', '.join(key_names)}, sum(number), min(c0)\nFROM src_t\n{tail}")
```

</details>

| query | `query_duration_ms` (min of 3) | `QueryAnalysisMicroseconds` / 1000 |
|---|---|---|
| CTE, 32 sets | 1588 | 1500 |
| CTE, 8 sets | 559 | 472 |
| table, 32 sets | 8 | 2 |
| table, 8 sets | 3 | 1 |

`min(c0)` is there so that `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass` cannot skip key collection; the CTE uses `numbers(10)` so that execution is nothing. All 16 columns are referenced so that `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumnsPass` keeps the CTE wide; in practice the CTE is wide because the outer query needs the columns.

**Expected performance**

Hashing a column reference should not depend on the size of its source. The table form shows the achievable cost: 8 ms.

**Why it is safe to change the hash**

`QueryTreeNodeWithHash::operator==` is `hash == hash && isEqual(...)`, and `isEqual` compares the sources itself (pointer short-circuit, structural otherwise). The contract the containers need is only `isEqual ⇒ equal hash`. A coarser hash that does not walk the source keeps that contract; columns of the same name and type from different sources collide and are told apart by `isEqual`.

What must keep the full hash: places that use the hash as an identity without `isEqual`, e.g. the `PreparedSets` key (`Planner/CollectSets.cpp`), `subquery_hash` in `buildQueryTreeForShard`, `EXISTS` action names in `PlannerActionsVisitor`, `calculateHashTableCacheKeys`, the scalar subquery / CTE / lambda caches in `QueryAnalyzer`, CNF and `ComparisonGraph`.

**Two implementations, both measured**

| branch | change | CTE 32 sets | analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| master | | 1588 ms | 1500 ms |
| https://github.com/filimonov/ClickHouse/tree/sup-31360-alt5 | 39 lines in `IQueryTreeNode.cpp`: a weak QUERY/UNION node (reached only as a column source) is hashed by its alias and projection columns (name + type) instead of its body, like a table is hashed by its storage id. Global, no pass changes. | 137 ms | 52 ms |
| https://github.com/filimonov/ClickHouse/tree/sup-31360-scale1 | `CompareOptions::hash_column_sources = false` policy, `QueryTreeNodePtrWithHashNoSources*` aliases in `HashUtils.h`, applied to the 14 intra-query containers listed above (one-line type changes); full hash kept for the identity users. Adds ProfileEvent `QueryTreeHashNodes`, a stateless test that checks each converted optimization with same-named columns from two subqueries, a stateless test that bounds `QueryTreeHashNodes` per query, a gtest for the hash contract. | 139 ms | 53 ms |

Both pass the GROUP BY / correlated / subquery / CTE / analyzer stateless sets with the same results as master. Two smaller independent improvements that do not touch hashing: collect GROUP BY keys lazily in `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass` (only after the first eliminable aggregate is seen, only on the rewriting traversal), and hash each key occurrence once in `GroupingFunctionsResolvePass` (`try_emplace` instead of `contains` + `insert` + `find`); together they bring the CTE query to ~640 ms without changing `getTreeHash`.

You can use any variant, or do a different one for PR.

**Additional context**

Related earlier fixes that address the resolver but not the passes: #88043, #107516, #106957, #106818, #108757.

| `LIKE` chain (`ConvertOrLikeChainPass`) | 1.3M |
| `ORDER BY k, toString(k)` (`OptimizeRedundantFunctionsInOrderByPass`) | 0.75M |
| `sum(c), count(c), avg(c)` with `optimize_syntax_fuse_functions` (`FuseFunctionsPass`) | 0.75M |
| `GROUP BY k1 + k2, k1, k2` (`OptimizeGroupByFunctionKeysPass`) | 0.63M |
| `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL INTERPOLATE` (`ValidationUtils`) | 0.29M |
| `LEFT JOIN` with `join_use_nulls = 1` (`join_columns_with_changed_types`) | 0.26M |

The tree has 8k nodes; a query hashes it 30 to 300 times over.

**How to reproduce**

Versions: master (9556ebaa51c, 26.10.1.1) and every release with the analyzer; measured on 25.8 and master.

- master at 9556ebaa51c (26.10.1.1), Release build, single node, `max_threads` default, `enable_analyzer = 1` (the only analyzer there).
- The generator below writes the queries (`python3 gen.py <dir>` gives `cte_8.sql`, `cte_32.sql`, `table_setup.sql`, `table_8.sql`, `table_32.sql`). Shape:

```sql
WITH src AS (SELECT number,
    intDiv((intDiv((number + 0), 1) + 1), 1) ... AS c0,   -- 16 columns, each ~250 nodes
    ...
  FROM numbers(10))
SELECT c0, ..., c15, sum(number), min(c0)
FROM src
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (c0, c1, ..., c14),
    (c1, c2, ..., c15),
    ...                       -- 32 sets of 15 keys
)
FORMAT Null
```

- Control: `CREATE TABLE src_t ENGINE = Memory AS <the same SELECT>` and run the outer query `FROM src_t`.

<details><summary>gen.py</summary>

```python
"""Reproduction for: analyzer hashes the whole column source for every GROUP BY key lookup.
Writes <out>/cte_<sets>.sql (keys are columns of a wide CTE) and <out>/table_<sets>.sql (same keys, CTE body materialized)."""
import sys
out = sys.argv[1]
def expr(i, n):
    e = f"number + {i}"
    for j in range(n):
        e = f"({e} + {j % 7 + 1})" if j % 2 else f"intDiv({e}, 1)"
    return e
width, nodes, keys = 16, 250, 16
cols = ",\n    ".join(f"{expr(i, nodes)} AS c{i}" for i in range(width))
key_names = [f"c{i}" for i in range(keys)]
body = f"SELECT number,\n    {cols}\n  FROM numbers(10)"
open(f"{out}/table_setup.sql", "w").write(f"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS src_t;\nCREATE TABLE src_t ENGINE = Memory AS {body};\n")
for sets in (8, 32):
    gs = ",\n    ".join("(" + ", ".join(key_names[(s + j) % keys] for j in range(keys - 1)) + ")" for s in range(sets))
    tail = f"GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (\n    {gs}\n)\nFORMAT Null"
    open(f"{out}/cte_{sets}.sql", "w").write(f"WITH src AS ({body})\nSELECT {', '.join(key_names)}, sum(number), min(c0)\nFROM src\n{tail}")
    open(f"{out}/table_{sets}.sql", "w").write(f"SELECT {', '.join(key_names)}, sum(number), min(c0)\nFROM src_t\n{tail}")
```

</details>

| query | `query_duration_ms` (min of 3) | `QueryAnalysisMicroseconds` / 1000 |
|---|---|---|
| CTE, 32 sets | 1588 | 1500 |
| CTE, 8 sets | 559 | 472 |
| table, 32 sets | 8 | 2 |
| table, 8 sets | 3 | 1 |

`min(c0)` is there so that `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass` cannot skip key collection; the CTE uses `numbers(10)` so that execution is nothing. All 16 columns are referenced so that `RemoveUnusedProjectionColumnsPass` keeps the CTE wide; in practice the CTE is wide because the outer query needs the columns.

**Expected performance**

Hashing a column reference should not depend on the size of its source. The table form shows the achievable cost: 8 ms.

**Why it is safe to change the hash**

`QueryTreeNodeWithHash::operator==` is `hash == hash && isEqual(...)`, and `isEqual` compares the sources itself (pointer short-circuit, structural otherwise). The contract the containers need is only `isEqual ⇒ equal hash`. A coarser hash that does not walk the source keeps that contract; columns of the same name and type from different sources collide and are told apart by `isEqual`.

What must keep the full hash: places that use the hash as an identity without `isEqual`, e.g. the `PreparedSets` key (`Planner/CollectSets.cpp`), `subquery_hash` in `buildQueryTreeForShard`, `EXISTS` action names in `PlannerActionsVisitor`, `calculateHashTableCacheKeys`, the scalar subquery / CTE / lambda caches in `QueryAnalyzer`, CNF and `ComparisonGraph`.

**Two implementations, both measured**

| branch | change | CTE 32 sets | analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| master | | 1588 ms | 1500 ms |
| https://github.com/filimonov/ClickHouse/tree/sup-31360-alt5 | 39 lines in `IQueryTreeNode.cpp`: a weak QUERY/UNION node (reached only as a column source) is hashed by its alias and projection columns (name + type) instead of its body, like a table is hashed by its storage id. Global, no pass changes. | 137 ms | 52 ms |
| https://github.com/filimonov/ClickHouse/tree/sup-31360-scale1 | `CompareOptions::hash_column_sources = false` policy, `QueryTreeNodePtrWithHashNoSources*` aliases in `HashUtils.h`, applied to the 14 intra-query containers listed above (one-line type changes); full hash kept for the identity users. Adds ProfileEvent `QueryTreeHashNodes`, a stateless test that checks each converted optimization with same-named columns from two subqueries, a stateless test that bounds `QueryTreeHashNodes` per query, a gtest for the hash contract. | 139 ms | 53 ms |

Both pass the GROUP BY / correlated / subquery / CTE / analyzer stateless sets with the same results as master. Two smaller independent improvements that do not touch hashing: collect GROUP BY keys lazily in `AggregateFunctionOfGroupByKeysPass` (only after the first eliminable aggregate is seen, only on the rewriting traversal), and hash each key occurrence once in `GroupingFunctionsResolvePass` (`try_emplace` instead of `contains` + `insert` + `find`); together they bring the CTE query to ~640 ms without changing `getTreeHash`.

You can use any variant, or do a different one for PR.

**Additional context**

Related earlier fixes that address the resolver but not the passes: #88043, #107516, #106957, #106818, #108757.

INSERT SELECT from fileCluster/urlCluster fails to fill DEFAULT columns

### Describe what's wrong

- INSERT INTO d SELECT * FROM fileCluster(...) or urlCluster(...) fails instead of inserting.
- Triggered when the source files lack columns that have DEFAULT expressions on the destination table.
- Expected the DEFAULT expressions to be filled in like file()/url() do.
- Instead nodes raise UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH, or CANNOT_INSERT_NULL_IN_ORDINARY_COLUMN.

Root cause: `ITableFunctionCluster::updateStructureAndFormatArgumentsIfNeeded` edits a copy of the argument list (`ASTs args = expression_list->children;` in ITableFunctionCluster.h:31), so the structure/format updates never reach the node query. Each node then re-infers the schema from the files and ends up missing the insertion table's DEFAULT columns.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `IStorageCluster::read` (IStorageCluster.cpp:203) -> `StorageFileCluster::updateQueryToSendIfNeeded` (StorageFileCluster.cpp:123) / `StorageURLCluster::updateQueryToSendIfNeeded` (StorageURLCluster.cpp:128) -> `ITableFunctionCluster::updateStructureAndFormatArgumentsIfNeeded`, which edits a copy of the argument list (ITableFunctionCluster.h:31). The node query keeps no structure, the node re-infers the schema from the files, and the insertion table's columns are missing from it.

Affected locations:
- [`src/TableFunctions/ITableFunctionCluster.h:31`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/b1e2520f04f04b/src/TableFunctions/ITableFunctionCluster.h#L31) — argument vector copied; structure and format edits are lost
- [`src/Storages/StorageFileCluster.cpp:125`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/b1e2520f04f04b/src/Storages/StorageFileCluster.cpp#L125) — structure sent as names and types only
- [`src/Storages/StorageURLCluster.cpp:130`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/b1e2520f04f04b/src/Storages/StorageURLCluster.cpp#L130) — structure sent as names and types only

Impact: `INSERT ... SELECT` from `fileCluster`/`urlCluster` into a table whose `DEFAULT` columns are absent from the source fails on every attempt; every plain `SELECT` from them also makes each node re-infer the schema. Workaround: write the structure explicitly or use `file`/`url`.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Requires use_structure_from_insertion_table_in_table_functions = 2 and input_format_defaults_for_omitted_fields = 1.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/85441f17-a2db-433f-847f-d7e0c2ad4d7b)

```sql
-- `INSERT ... SELECT FROM fileCluster(...)` on the initiator must fill the fields missing in the file with the
-- `DEFAULT` expressions of the destination table, the same as `INSERT ... SELECT FROM file(...)`.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_05480;
SET use_structure_from_insertion_table_in_table_functions = 2;
SET input_format_defaults_for_omitted_fields = 1;

INSERT INTO TABLE FUNCTION file(currentDatabase() || '_05480.jsonl', 'JSONEachRow', 'id UInt32') SELECT number + 1 FROM numbers(2) SETTINGS engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_05480;
CREATE TABLE t_05480 (id UInt32, q UInt32 DEFAULT 7, e UInt32 DEFAULT id * 10) ENGINE = Memory;

INSERT INTO t_05480 SELECT * FROM file(currentDatabase() || '_05480.jsonl', 'JSONEachRow');
SELECT 'file', * FROM t_05480 ORDER BY id;
TRUNCATE TABLE t_05480;

INSERT INTO t_05480 SELECT * FROM fileCluster('test_cluster_one_shard_three_replicas_localhost', currentDatabase() || '_05480.jsonl', 'JSONEachRow')
SETTINGS parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0;
SELECT 'fileCluster', * FROM t_05480 ORDER BY id;

DROP TABLE t_05480;
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

INSERT ... SELECT from fileCluster/urlCluster should fill missing columns with the destination table's DEFAULT expressions, matching file()/url() behavior.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
file	1	7	10
file	2	7	20
fileCluster	1	7	10
fileCluster	2	7	20
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The node re-infers schema from the raw files and either can't resolve the DEFAULT column, gets a column count mismatch, or inserts NULL into a non-nullable column.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
file	1	7	10
file	2	7	20
Reason: return code: 47
Code: 47. DB::Exception: Received from 127.0.0.1:19010. DB::Exception: Identifier '__table1.q' cannot be resolved from table_function with name __table1. Maybe you meant: ['__table1.id']. In scope SELECT __table1.id AS id, __table1.q AS q, __table1.e AS e FROM fileCluster('test_cluster_one_shard_three_replicas_localhost', '<db>_05480.jsonl', 'JSONEac
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Take `ASTs & args = expression_list->children;` (the erase/insert of the cluster name then works in place), and build the URL/File structure with the same `DEFAULT`-carrying builder as `getStructureToSend` (move it next to `getStorageColumnsReadByDefault`) so the nodes do not fall back to type defaults once the structure arrives.

</details>

### Additional context

Same pattern as #128344.

Open risks:
- Fixing only the copy turns the exception into silent type defaults (names-and-types structure), i.e. the original #128299 symptom for these two functions.

Found during automated review of [PR #128344](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128344); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr128344_102`

- Resolved by: #128492
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1263-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

First start of a new build fails once with UUID collision when system.all_* union tables are replaced (fix #127630 not on release/26.10)

The first start of a new build fails once with `Mapping for table with UUID=... already exists. It happened due to UUID collision ... (TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS)` when `system.all_*` union tables are replaced at startup. The second start succeeds. Every upgrade, rollback and patch bump restarts each server twice.

With `create_union_system_log_tables` (in the default server config since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117943) and `prepare_system_log_tables_on_startup` (implied by `startup_scripts`), a build whose union table schema differs from the stored one (always: `all_trace_log` holds the build id) replaces the `system.all_*` tables during startup. The replaced table is queued for an asynchronous drop, then `DatabaseCatalog::loadMarkedAsDroppedTables` loads it again from `metadata_dropped` and registers its UUID a second time, and the server exits.

Fixed on master by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127630; `release/26.10` does not have it (checked 2026-10-31), and 26.8 has union tables too.

Reproduced with two servers: 26.10.2.91 <-> 26.10.2.138 and 26.8.1.638 <-> 26.10.2.138, every binary change in both directions fails the first start; restarts on the same build are clean. Servers without `prepare_system_log_tables_on_startup` (ClickHouse Cloud's regular services) did not hit it.

@groeneai please backport https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127630 to 26.10 and 26.8.

- Merged into: `26.11.1.691-master` (included in `26.11` and later)

JSONExtract into DateTime/DateTime64 returns 1970-01-01 on 26.8+ under old compatibility with date_time_input_format = best_effort

`JSONExtract` into `DateTime`/`DateTime64` returns `1970-01-01` (no error) on 26.8+ for an ISO 8601 value when `compatibility` is old and the profile has `date_time_input_format = best_effort`. Materialized views then write epoch values silently. This hit a ClickHouse Cloud customer whose service runs with an old `compatibility`.

26.8 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109252) made `JSONExtract` parse `DateTime`/`DateTime64` with `cast_string_to_date_time_mode` instead of `date_time_input_format`, and `compatibility <= 26.4` gives `cast_string_to_date_time_mode = basic`.

```bash
Q="SELECT JSONExtract('{\"a\":\"2026-10-19T07:30:26.743Z\"}', 'a', 'DateTime64(3, \\'UTC\\')')"
clickhouse-26.6 local --compatibility=23.9 --date_time_input_format=best_effort --query "$Q"   # 2026-10-19 07:30:26.743
clickhouse-26.8 local --compatibility=23.9 --date_time_input_format=best_effort --query "$Q"   # 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000
```

Present in 26.8.1.638, 26.10.2.91, 26.10.2.138 and master 26.11.1.1460. Fix in review: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128048; it needs backports to 26.8 and 26.10.

Found by the upgrade/rollback harness (`compat_ledger`), confirmed on ClickHouse Cloud staging.

@groeneai please drive this to merge and backport.

26.6 legacy Delta Lake reader: LOGICAL_ERROR 'No such column in schema' on a partitioned table after a delete

26.6 legacy Delta Lake reader (`allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs = 0`): `LOGICAL_ERROR` on a partitioned table after a delete. 26.8 and 26.10 are fine.

```bash
python3 -c "
import pyarrow as pa
from deltalake import write_deltalake, DeltaTable
t = pa.table({'id': pa.array(range(10), pa.int64()), 'part': [f'p{i%3}' for i in range(10)], 'v': pa.array(range(10), pa.int64())})
write_deltalake('/tmp/t', t, mode='append', partition_by=['part'])
DeltaTable('/tmp/t').delete('id % 5 = 0')"
clickhouse-26.6 local --query "SELECT count() FROM deltaLakeLocal('/tmp/t') SETTINGS allow_experimental_delta_kernel_rs = 0"
# Code: 49. DB::Exception: No such column in schema: part (schema: ). (LOGICAL_ERROR)
```

Low priority: non-default reader, 26.6 only. Fix on `release/26.6` only if that line stays supported.

Found by the upgrade/rollback harness.

@groeneai please fix this.
