text:
Iceberg: tables created by 26.6 become unreadable after ADD COLUMN on 26.8+ (last-column-id ignores nested field ids, Duplicate field id)

Iceberg tables created by 26.6 become unreadable after `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` on 26.8 or 26.10, for every ClickHouse version and for pyiceberg. No rollback repairs them.

26.6 writes `last-column-id` without counting nested field ids: a table `(id Int64, arr Array(Int64))` gets `last-column-id: 2` although the array element has id 3. 26.8 and 26.10 write 3 for new tables, but trust the stored value, so `ADD COLUMN` assigns id 3 to the new column and every reader fails with `Duplicate field id 3. (ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION)` (pyiceberg: `KeyError: 'Field "element" does not exist in schema'`). On 26.6 alone `ADD COLUMN` already fails the same way.

```bash
d=$PWD/ice; rm -rf $d; mkdir -p $d
clickhouse-26.6 local --query "SET allow_experimental_insert_into_iceberg = 1;
    CREATE TABLE t (id Int64, arr Array(Int64)) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('$d/t', 'Parquet');
    INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, [1, 2]);"
clickhouse-26.8 local --query "SET allow_experimental_insert_into_iceberg = 1;
    CREATE TABLE t ENGINE = IcebergLocal('$d/t', 'Parquet');
    ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN extra Nullable(String);
    SELECT * FROM t;"
# Code: 743. DB::Exception: Duplicate field id 3. (ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION)
```

Where: `src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/MetadataGenerator.cpp` (`generateAddColumnMetadata` takes `last_column_id` from the metadata as is). Fix: start new ids from `max(last-column-id, max field id over all schemas including nested ids) + 1`, which also repairs tables written by 26.6 and by other writers with the same mistake. Please add a stateless test that writes metadata with a too-small `last-column-id`.

Found by the upgrade/rollback harness (`tests/immortal` in the private repository), `26.6 -> 26.8`.

title: MergeTree PREWHERE keeps filtering before `EventDate >= '2013-07-01'` and `URL <> ''` because they count as able to throw; recognizing that they cannot makes ClickBench Q37/Q38 9-21% faster on top of #128442

text:
MergeTree PREWHERE steps filter the whole block before every next condition, even one that cannot throw; filtering only when needed makes ClickBench Q42 6-10% faster on a fully merged hits table

### Describe the situation
On x86 (4 vCPU) with `query_plan_merge_filters` (default), each MergeTree PREWHERE step filters all its columns before the next. That is needed only if the next condition can throw or the reader converts or fills its columns; skipping it otherwise makes ClickBench Q42 6–10% faster.

Server-side mean latency, master vs patched, 10 paired rounds x 3 servers per arm; change with 95% CI.

**`hits` merged into one part** (`OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`): `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` dense, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` sparse.

| Query, columns cache, layout | master, ms | patched, ms | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q42, cache off, 1 part | 14.58 | 13.66 | −6.3% [−9.5, −3.0] |
| Q43, cache off, 1 part | 11.44 | 11.10 | −3.0% [−4.5, −1.5] |
| Q39, cache off, 1 part | 47.14 | 45.80 | −2.8% [−4.7, −1.0] |
| Q3, cache off, 1 part (control) | 118.36 | 118.50 | +0.1% [−2.3, +2.6] |
| Q42, cache on, 1 part | 9.60 | 8.65 | −9.8% [−12.3, −7.2] |
| Q43, cache on, 1 part | 8.66 | 8.34 | −3.7% [−6.1, −1.1] |
| Q39, cache on, 1 part | 12.07 | 11.40 | −5.5% [−8.1, −2.8] |
| Q3, cache on, 1 part (control) | 17.29 | 17.52 | +1.3% [−1.6, +4.3] |

"cache off" is the default; "cache on" is `use_columns_cache = 1`. Q3 has no `WHERE`, so the patch does not run for it.

- On the same rows in 12 parts with merges stopped (table below), `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part that holds 613,490 of the 738,172 rows Q42 and Q43 read; there Q42 changes by −6.2% / −11.8% and Q43 by −3.9% / −7.6% (cache off / on).
- On top of #128432's first two commits, the first version of this patch (it builds the same steps on this table) makes Q42 2.5% / 3.7% faster (cache off / on) and Q39 5.2% faster with the cache on, and leaves Q43 unchanged on the merged table: the two gains overlap (see Related work).
- #124498 MergeTree query (`a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90`, 30M random rows, one part): 502.6 → 433.8 ms (−13.7% [−15.8, −11.5]); reading the four conditions in one step takes 420.7 ms.
- Peak query memory, with every allocation tracked, grows by 1.5 MB on Q42 with the cache off (1.8 MB on 12 parts) and by 4.9 MB on the #124498 query (4 threads): the patch keeps one block of PREWHERE columns per reading thread unfiltered until the combined filter.
- On the 12-part table, the first version of this patch (same PREWHERE steps there) left Q37, Q38, Q40, Q41 and Q8 unchanged, made Q39 3.9% faster with the cache on, and raised 4-client throughput by 1.4% / 3.4% (cache off / on).

<details><summary>Same comparison on 12 parts with merges stopped, where DontCountHits is sparse</summary>

The `CounterID = 62` rows are in two of the 12 parts. `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part with 613,490 of these 738,172 rows and dense in the other; `IsLink` and `IsDownload` are sparse in both; `IsRefresh` is dense in both. 8 rounds x 3 servers per arm.

| Query, columns cache, layout | master, ms | patched, ms | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q42, cache off, 12 parts | 15.96 | 14.98 | −6.2% [−10.7, −1.4] |
| Q43, cache off, 12 parts | 11.93 | 11.47 | −3.9% [−7.5, 0.0] |
| Q3, cache off, 12 parts (control) | 117.89 | 119.71 | +1.5% [−0.2, +3.3] |
| Q42, cache on, 12 parts | 10.64 | 9.38 | −11.8% [−13.1, −10.5] |
| Q43, cache on, 12 parts | 9.83 | 9.09 | −7.6% [−10.2, −4.9] |
| Q3, cache on, 12 parts (control) | 18.24 | 18.41 | +0.9% [−3.5, +5.5] |

Filtering a sparse column costs more than filtering a dense one, so skipping the `DontCountHits` filter passes saves more here on Q43, and on Q42 with the cache on, than on the merged table.

The first version of the patch, 8 rounds over Q3, Q8 and Q37–Q43 on this table: Q42 −7.0% [−8.8, −5.2] cache off and −9.8% [−13.3, −6.3] cache on, Q43 cache on −6.8% [−10.3, −3.2], Q39 cache on −3.9% [−6.4, −1.4]; Q37, Q38, Q40, Q41 and the controls between −2.1% and +1.5%, all intervals including 0.

</details>

<details><summary>Why it happens and what the patch changes</summary>

`query_plan_merge_filters = 1` passes `force_short_circuit_execution` to `tryBuildPrewhereSteps`, which then sets `need_filter` on every PREWHERE step. So after each step `ReadResult::applyFilter` filters every column in the block, and every column a later step reads is filtered right after it is read, even when the step keeps almost all rows (in Q43, `IsRefresh = 0` keeps 98% and `DontCountHits = 0` 93% of the rows the primary key selects). Without forcing, `ReadResult::optimize` combines the step filters and applies them when fewer than 60% of the rows pass, or after the last step.

The forced filter keeps the rows an earlier condition rejects away from two things:
- the next condition, for example `d != 0 AND intDiv(1000, d) > 5`. Since #111954 a condition that may throw forces the filter in any case;
- the reader, which converts a column after a pending `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` and computes the `DEFAULT` of a column missing in a part on the whole block it reads (`MergeTreeReadersChain::executeActionsBeforePrewhere`).

The patch keeps the forced filter unless all of the following hold:
- every condition of the next step meets the contract that `short_circuit_function_evaluation_reorder_arguments` uses to evaluate an `and` argument on more rows (`canBeMovedToTheFrontOfAndChain` in `FilterStep.cpp`): cheap, `canThrow` is false, stateless, no observable side effects, deterministic;
- `ReadFromMergeTree::canReadPrewhereColumnsAhead` holds, the check #111954 uses before reading columns ahead: no pending data, `ALTER` or metadata mutation, no masking policy, and every part stores each PREWHERE column with its current type;
- the last step filters (`PrewhereInfo::need_filter`), so the columns read after PREWHERE see only the matching rows. The old analyzer does not set it for `PREWHERE` together with `WHERE`; the patch then keeps every forced filter.

Comparisons of numbers qualify. A `Date` compared with a `String` can throw (`comparisonCanThrow`), and functions that do not describe `canThrowIfKnown` count as throwing, so the step before them still filters: this is why `EventDate >= '2013-07-14'` limits Q43 and why Q37/Q38 (`URL <> ''`, `Title <> ''`) do not change. `Memory` tables and the Parquet reader call `tryBuildPrewhereSteps` without forcing and are not affected.

Correctness checks:
- New stateless test `05475_prewhere_forced_filter_reader_conversions` (in the patch): `g = 1` keeps 90% of the rows, and a column missing in the part with `DEFAULT toUInt64(s)`, or a `String` column with a pending `MODIFY COLUMN ... UInt64`, holds `'x'` only in the rejected rows. It reads that column in a later PREWHERE step, after PREWHERE, and after PREWHERE with the old analyzer and a `WHERE`. Master and the patch return the expected results; the first version of this patch threw `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` on the two queries that read the column in a later step. With `query_plan_merge_filters = 0`, master throws on those two as well, because its steps then do not filter.
- Complete grouped results of Q37–Q43 (no `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`) are identical to master with the columns cache on and off, on both tables.
- 12 queries where a later condition throws on rows an earlier condition rejects (division by zero in `intDiv`, `toDate` and `toUInt64` of strings, `Map` values, `throwIf`, and a subquery filter merged with the outer one): identical results and no exceptions.
- 353 stateless tests matching `short_circuit`, `merge_filters`, `throwif`, `guard` and `prewhere`: 307 pass, including the new test; the other 46 fail identically on master in this environment (no `test.hits`, clusters, ZooKeeper, S3 or pandas). With pandas installed, `02473_multistep_prewhere` and `02473_multistep_split_prewhere`, two of those 46, pass on master and the patch. The new test also passes 20 runs with random settings on master and the patch.

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master e4afc4fd7f50f14b0bb11ad83a9c0b85f3cc1b59 (26.11.1). Up to c189bd99fbda59c78489a6734c49397533bdd591 there is no change to `MergeTreeSplitPrewhereIntoReadSteps.cpp`, the range reader, `MergeTreeReadersChain` or `FilterStep.cpp`; `ReadFromMergeTree.cpp` changed only in how parallel replicas name a read (#119350). Every step is forced to filter since `query_plan_merge_filters` was enabled by default in #71539 (November 2024).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

- Data: ClickBench `hits` loaded with the official `create.sql` (MergeTree, `ORDER BY (CounterID, EventDate, UserID, EventTime, WatchID)`) plus `auto_statistics_types = ''`, 99,997,497 rows. Merged table: `OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL` (one part). 12-part table: the same rows before merging, merges stopped.
- Queries: lines 3, 39, 42 and 43 of ClickBench `queries.sql` (Q3 as a control; Q39 on the merged table only). Default settings (4 threads); for the "on" rows `use_columns_cache = 1`.
- Hardware and build: AWS x86 4 vCPU (Xeon 8375C), 30 GiB; Release build, clang 21, both binaries from the same build directory.
- Procedure: three servers per binary on hard-linked copies of the data. In each round, for each server in rotated order and each query, `clickhouse benchmark -c 1 -i 30 --query "..."` after 15 warm-up runs. Latency is the mean server-side duration of the 30 runs from `system.query_log` (`QueryFinish`, `event_time_microseconds - query_start_time_microseconds`), then the geometric mean over the three servers of a binary. The change is the geometric mean of the per-round ratios with a 95% t-interval. 10 rounds on the merged table, 8 on the 12-part table.
- First version of the patch (same PREWHERE steps on the 12-part table: no mutations, no masking policy, every part has every column with its current type, and the planner sets `need_filter`), 8 rounds over Q3, Q8 and Q37–Q43; throughput with 2 servers per binary, `clickhouse benchmark -c 4 -i 500` over Q37, Q39, Q41, Q42 and Q43, 4 alternating rounds; median QPS 35.4 → 35.9 cache off, 69.0 → 71.3 cache on.
- #124498 query: the issue's table (`a`, `b`, `c`, `d` UInt32 = `rand(i) % 100`, `e` UInt64) as MergeTree `ORDER BY tuple()`, 30M rows, one part after `OPTIMIZE FINAL`; `SELECT sum(e) FROM t_perf WHERE a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90` with default settings. One data directory, the two binaries alternating per round, 6 rounds of 15 runs after 5 warm-up runs, mean server-side duration; the one-step reference is master with `enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps = 0`. The result is identical in every round.
- Memory: `max_untracked_memory = 0`, 10 runs per query and binary, median `memory_usage` from `system.query_log`. Merged table: Q42 11.8 → 13.3 MB cache off and 6.4 → 6.0 MB cache on; Q43 9.8 → 10.1 MB and 6.6 → 7.0 MB. 12-part table: Q42 11.1 → 12.9 MB cache off and 5.8 → 5.6 MB cache on; Q43 9.0 → 9.0 MB and 5.6 → 5.8 MB. #124498 query 13.8 → 18.7 MB with 4 threads and 4.7 → 5.9 MB with 1 thread (its four `UInt32` columns of one block take about 1 MB).

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A PREWHERE step should copy its columns through its filter only when something later in the read must not see the rejected rows, or when the filter removes enough rows to pay for the copy.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111954 forces the filter before a condition that may throw and introduced `canReadPrewhereColumnsAhead`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122508 defines the contract used here for evaluating an `and` argument on more rows.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/71539 enabled `query_plan_merge_filters`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128432 drops the carried and intermediate filter columns that each PREWHERE step filters again, while this patch removes forced filter passes. Both edit the same `PrewhereExprStep` initializer in `tryBuildPrewhereSteps`, each was measured alone against the same master, and their gains are not additive. On the merged table, on top of #128432's first two commits, the first version of this patch (same steps there) changed Q42 by −2.5% [−3.6, −1.3] / −3.7% [−5.5, −1.9] (cache off / on) and Q39 by −5.2% [−7.5, −2.8] with the cache on, and left Q43 and Q39 with the cache off unchanged (8 rounds x 3 servers). On the 12-part table with the cache on, it changed Q42 by −9.6% [−12.3, −6.8] and Q39 by −4.5% [−8.2, −0.7], and Q43 was not significant (5 rounds x 2 servers; cache off not measured).
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128381 (PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128396) makes filtering sparse columns cheaper. Each patch was measured alone against the same master. On the 12-part table, where `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part holding most `CounterID = 62` rows, #128381 makes each filtering pass over it cheaper and this patch removes most of those passes, so their Q42 and Q43 gains there overlap and do not add up. On a merged table or the official load, where `DontCountHits` is dense, #128381 does not change Q42 and Q43 (see the discussion there), while this patch does (table above). `IsLink` and `IsDownload` are sparse in every layout, so on Q39 the two gains overlap in all of them.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128347 caches the rows a PREWHERE selects, so a repeated query with a cached condition skips these steps. Where it applies, the two patches' gains do not add up; first runs and queries whose condition is not cached keep this patch's gain.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124498 reports the cost of per-step filtering for non-selective conjunctions on `Memory`, with a MergeTree comparison (`a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90`). This patch removes MergeTree's forced filter between such numeric conditions: on that query it takes 433.8 ms instead of 502.6 ms here, against 420.7 ms for one step. It does not change the `Memory` path.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125978 (open) fixes a comparison that `comparisonCanThrow` reports as safe although it can throw (`Tuple` with `Variant`, #125919). #122508 uses this classification only to move a cheap condition ahead of heavier ones; this patch evaluates such a condition on the rows any earlier step rejects, so until #125978 lands, that comparison would throw in a guarded multi-column PREWHERE that master answers.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128342 (open) describes `canThrowIfKnown` for `empty`/`notEmpty`; with it, the `URL <> ''` and `Title <> ''` steps of Q37/Q38 could stop forcing the filter too.

</details>

### Additional context
<details><summary>Full patch</summary>

One change on e4afc4fd: the code change and the new stateless test.

```diff
+-- With query_plan_merge_filters = 1, a PREWHERE step materializes its filter before the reader fills a column missing

+-- and throw here on the rows that `g = 1` rejects. The first condition keeps 90% of the rows, so the filter is not
+-- applied by the heuristic for selective steps either.
+
+SET enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps = 1, query_plan_merge_filters = 1;
+
+DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_prewhere_reader_default;
+CREATE TABLE t_prewhere_reader_default (k UInt64, g UInt8, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;
+INSERT INTO t_prewhere_reader_default SELECT number, number % 10 != 0, if(number % 10 = 0, 'x', toString(number)) FROM numbers(100000);
+ALTER TABLE t_prewhere_reader_default ADD COLUMN n UInt64 DEFAULT toUInt64(s);
+
+SELECT 'default, column of a later step';
+SELECT count() FROM t_prewhere_reader_default PREWHERE g = 1 AND n > 5;
+SELECT 'default, column read after PREWHERE';
+SELECT sum(n) FROM t_prewhere_reader_default PREWHERE g = 1 AND k > 5;
+-- The old analyzer does not filter by the last PREWHERE step when there is a WHERE.
+SELECT 'default, column read after PREWHERE, old analyzer with WHERE';
+SELECT sum(n) FROM t_prewhere_reader_default PREWHERE g = 1 AND k > 5 WHERE n > 0 SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, optimize_move_to_prewhere = 0;
+
+DROP TABLE t_prewhere_reader_default;
+
+DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_prewhere_reader_conversion;
+CREATE TABLE t_prewhere_reader_conversion (k UInt64, g UInt8, v String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192;
+SYSTEM STOP MERGES t_prewhere_reader_conversion;
+INSERT INTO t_prewhere_reader_conversion SELECT number, number % 10 != 0, if(number % 10 = 0, 'x', toString(number)) FROM numbers(100000);
+-- The mutation stays pending, so the reader converts `v` to UInt64 when it reads the part.
+ALTER TABLE t_prewhere_reader_conversion MODIFY COLUMN v UInt64 SETTINGS alter_sync = 0;
+
+SELECT 'conversion, column of a later step';
+SELECT count() FROM t_prewhere_reader_conversion PREWHERE g = 1 AND v > 5;
+SELECT 'conversion, column read after PREWHERE';
+SELECT sum(v) FROM t_prewhere_reader_conversion PREWHERE g = 1 AND k > 5;
+SELECT 'conversion, column read after PREWHERE, old analyzer with WHERE';
+SELECT sum(v) FROM t_prewhere_reader_conversion PREWHERE g = 1 AND k > 5 WHERE v > 0 SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, optimize_move_to_prewhere = 0;
+
+DROP TABLE t_prewhere_reader_conversion;
```

title: MergeTree PREWHERE steps filter the whole block before every next condition, even one that cannot throw; filtering only when needed makes ClickBench Q42 6-10% faster on a fully merged hits table
body:
### Describe the situation
On x86 (4 vCPU) with `query_plan_merge_filters` (default), each MergeTree PREWHERE step filters all its columns before the next. That is needed only if the next condition can throw or the reader converts or fills its columns; skipping it otherwise makes ClickBench Q42 6–10% faster.

Server-side mean latency, master vs patched, 10 paired rounds x 3 servers per arm; change with 95% CI.

**`hits` merged into one part** (`OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`): `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` dense, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` sparse.

| Query, columns cache, layout | master, ms | patched, ms | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q42, cache off, 1 part | 14.58 | 13.66 | −6.3% [−9.5, −3.0] |
| Q43, cache off, 1 part | 11.44 | 11.10 | −3.0% [−4.5, −1.5] |
| Q39, cache off, 1 part | 47.14 | 45.80 | −2.8% [−4.7, −1.0] |
| Q3, cache off, 1 part (control) | 118.36 | 118.50 | +0.1% [−2.3, +2.6] |
| Q42, cache on, 1 part | 9.60 | 8.65 | −9.8% [−12.3, −7.2] |
| Q43, cache on, 1 part | 8.66 | 8.34 | −3.7% [−6.1, −1.1] |
| Q39, cache on, 1 part | 12.07 | 11.40 | −5.5% [−8.1, −2.8] |
| Q3, cache on, 1 part (control) | 17.29 | 17.52 | +1.3% [−1.6, +4.3] |

"cache off" is the default; "cache on" is `use_columns_cache = 1`. Q3 has no `WHERE`, so the patch does not run for it.

- On the same rows in 12 parts with merges stopped (table below), `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part that holds 613,490 of the 738,172 rows Q42 and Q43 read; there Q42 changes by −6.2% / −11.8% and Q43 by −3.9% / −7.6% (cache off / on).
- On top of #128432's first two commits, the first version of this patch (it builds the same steps on this table) makes Q42 2.5% / 3.7% faster (cache off / on) and Q39 5.2% faster with the cache on, and leaves Q43 unchanged on the merged table: the two gains overlap (see Related work).
- #124498 MergeTree query (`a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90`, 30M random rows, one part): 502.6 → 433.8 ms (−13.7% [−15.8, −11.5]); reading the four conditions in one step takes 420.7 ms.
- Peak query memory, with every allocation tracked, grows by 1.5 MB on Q42 with the cache off (1.8 MB on 12 parts) and by 4.9 MB on the #124498 query (4 threads): the patch keeps one block of PREWHERE columns per reading thread unfiltered until the combined filter.
- On the 12-part table, the first version of this patch (same PREWHERE steps there) left Q37, Q38, Q40, Q41 and Q8 unchanged, made Q39 3.9% faster with the cache on, and raised 4-client throughput by 1.4% / 3.4% (cache off / on).

<details><summary>Same comparison on 12 parts with merges stopped, where DontCountHits is sparse</summary>

The `CounterID = 62` rows are in two of the 12 parts. `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part with 613,490 of these 738,172 rows and dense in the other; `IsLink` and `IsDownload` are sparse in both; `IsRefresh` is dense in both. 8 rounds x 3 servers per arm.

| Query, columns cache, layout | master, ms | patched, ms | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q42, cache off, 12 parts | 15.96 | 14.98 | −6.2% [−10.7, −1.4] |
| Q43, cache off, 12 parts | 11.93 | 11.47 | −3.9% [−7.5, 0.0] |
| Q3, cache off, 12 parts (control) | 117.89 | 119.71 | +1.5% [−0.2, +3.3] |
| Q42, cache on, 12 parts | 10.64 | 9.38 | −11.8% [−13.1, −10.5] |
| Q43, cache on, 12 parts | 9.83 | 9.09 | −7.6% [−10.2, −4.9] |
| Q3, cache on, 12 parts (control) | 18.24 | 18.41 | +0.9% [−3.5, +5.5] |

Filtering a sparse column costs more than filtering a dense one, so skipping the `DontCountHits` filter passes saves more here on Q43, and on Q42 with the cache on, than on the merged table.

The first version of the patch, 8 rounds over Q3, Q8 and Q37–Q43 on this table: Q42 −7.0% [−8.8, −5.2] cache off and −9.8% [−13.3, −6.3] cache on, Q43 cache on −6.8% [−10.3, −3.2], Q39 cache on −3.9% [−6.4, −1.4]; Q37, Q38, Q40, Q41 and the controls between −2.1% and +1.5%, all intervals including 0.

</details>

<details><summary>Why it happens and what the patch changes</summary>

`query_plan_merge_filters = 1` passes `force_short_circuit_execution` to `tryBuildPrewhereSteps`, which then sets `need_filter` on every PREWHERE step. So after each step `ReadResult::applyFilter` filters every column in the block, and every column a later step reads is filtered right after it is read, even when the step keeps almost all rows (in Q43, `IsRefresh = 0` keeps 98% and `DontCountHits = 0` 93% of the rows the primary key selects). Without forcing, `ReadResult::optimize` combines the step filters and applies them when fewer than 60% of the rows pass, or after the last step.

The forced filter keeps the rows an earlier condition rejects away from two things:
- the next condition, for example `d != 0 AND intDiv(1000, d) > 5`. Since #111954 a condition that may throw forces the filter in any case;
- the reader, which converts a column after a pending `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` and computes the `DEFAULT` of a column missing in a part on the whole block it reads (`MergeTreeReadersChain::executeActionsBeforePrewhere`).

The patch keeps the forced filter unless all of the following hold:
- every condition of the next step meets the contract that `short_circuit_function_evaluation_reorder_arguments` uses to evaluate an `and` argument on more rows (`canBeMovedToTheFrontOfAndChain` in `FilterStep.cpp`): cheap, `canThrow` is false, stateless, no observable side effects, deterministic;
- `ReadFromMergeTree::canReadPrewhereColumnsAhead` holds, the check #111954 uses before reading columns ahead: no pending data, `ALTER` or metadata mutation, no masking policy, and every part stores each PREWHERE column with its current type;
- the last step filters (`PrewhereInfo::need_filter`), so the columns read after PREWHERE see only the matching rows. The old analyzer does not set it for `PREWHERE` together with `WHERE`; the patch then keeps every forced filter.

Comparisons of numbers qualify. A `Date` compared with a `String` can throw (`comparisonCanThrow`), and functions that do not describe `canThrowIfKnown` count as throwing, so the step before them still filters: this is why `EventDate >= '2013-07-14'` limits Q43 and why Q37/Q38 (`URL <> ''`, `Title <> ''`) do not change. `Memory` tables and the Parquet reader call `tryBuildPrewhereSteps` without forcing and are not affected.

Correctness checks:
- New stateless test `05475_prewhere_forced_filter_reader_conversions` (in the patch): `g = 1` keeps 90% of the rows, and a column missing in the part with `DEFAULT toUInt64(s)`, or a `String` column with a pending `MODIFY COLUMN ... UInt64`, holds `'x'` only in the rejected rows. It reads that column in a later PREWHERE step, after PREWHERE, and after PREWHERE with the old analyzer and a `WHERE`. Master and the patch return the expected results; the first version of this patch threw `CANNOT_PARSE_TEXT` on the two queries that read the column in a later step. With `query_plan_merge_filters = 0`, master throws on those two as well, because its steps then do not filter.
- Complete grouped results of Q37–Q43 (no `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`) are identical to master with the columns cache on and off, on both tables.
- 12 queries where a later condition throws on rows an earlier condition rejects (division by zero in `intDiv`, `toDate` and `toUInt64` of strings, `Map` values, `throwIf`, and a subquery filter merged with the outer one): identical results and no exceptions.
- 353 stateless tests matching `short_circuit`, `merge_filters`, `throwif`, `guard` and `prewhere`: 307 pass, including the new test; the other 46 fail identically on master in this environment (no `test.hits`, clusters, ZooKeeper, S3 or pandas). With pandas installed, `02473_multistep_prewhere` and `02473_multistep_split_prewhere`, two of those 46, pass on master and the patch. The new test also passes 20 runs with random settings on master and the patch.

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master e4afc4fd7f50f14b0bb11ad83a9c0b85f3cc1b59 (26.11.1). Up to c189bd99fbda59c78489a6734c49397533bdd591 there is no change to `MergeTreeSplitPrewhereIntoReadSteps.cpp`, the range reader, `MergeTreeReadersChain` or `FilterStep.cpp`; `ReadFromMergeTree.cpp` changed only in how parallel replicas name a read (#119350). Every step is forced to filter since `query_plan_merge_filters` was enabled by default in #71539 (November 2024).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

- Data: ClickBench `hits` loaded with the official `create.sql` (MergeTree, `ORDER BY (CounterID, EventDate, UserID, EventTime, WatchID)`) plus `auto_statistics_types = ''`, 99,997,497 rows. Merged table: `OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL` (one part). 12-part table: the same rows before merging, merges stopped.
- Queries: lines 3, 39, 42 and 43 of ClickBench `queries.sql` (Q3 as a control; Q39 on the merged table only). Default settings (4 threads); for the "on" rows `use_columns_cache = 1`.
- Hardware and build: AWS x86 4 vCPU (Xeon 8375C), 30 GiB; Release build, clang 21, both binaries from the same build directory.
- Procedure: three servers per binary on hard-linked copies of the data. In each round, for each server in rotated order and each query, `clickhouse benchmark -c 1 -i 30 --query "..."` after 15 warm-up runs. Latency is the mean server-side duration of the 30 runs from `system.query_log` (`QueryFinish`, `event_time_microseconds - query_start_time_microseconds`), then the geometric mean over the three servers of a binary. The change is the geometric mean of the per-round ratios with a 95% t-interval. 10 rounds on the merged table, 8 on the 12-part table.
- First version of the patch (same PREWHERE steps on the 12-part table: no mutations, no masking policy, every part has every column with its current type, and the planner sets `need_filter`), 8 rounds over Q3, Q8 and Q37–Q43; throughput with 2 servers per binary, `clickhouse benchmark -c 4 -i 500` over Q37, Q39, Q41, Q42 and Q43, 4 alternating rounds; median QPS 35.4 → 35.9 cache off, 69.0 → 71.3 cache on.
- #124498 query: the issue's table (`a`, `b`, `c`, `d` UInt32 = `rand(i) % 100`, `e` UInt64) as MergeTree `ORDER BY tuple()`, 30M rows, one part after `OPTIMIZE FINAL`; `SELECT sum(e) FROM t_perf WHERE a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90` with default settings. One data directory, the two binaries alternating per round, 6 rounds of 15 runs after 5 warm-up runs, mean server-side duration; the one-step reference is master with `enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps = 0`. The result is identical in every round.
- Memory: `max_untracked_memory = 0`, 10 runs per query and binary, median `memory_usage` from `system.query_log`. Merged table: Q42 11.8 → 13.3 MB cache off and 6.4 → 6.0 MB cache on; Q43 9.8 → 10.1 MB and 6.6 → 7.0 MB. 12-part table: Q42 11.1 → 12.9 MB cache off and 5.8 → 5.6 MB cache on; Q43 9.0 → 9.0 MB and 5.6 → 5.8 MB. #124498 query 13.8 → 18.7 MB with 4 threads and 4.7 → 5.9 MB with 1 thread (its four `UInt32` columns of one block take about 1 MB).

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A PREWHERE step should copy its columns through its filter only when something later in the read must not see the rejected rows, or when the filter removes enough rows to pay for the copy.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111954 forces the filter before a condition that may throw and introduced `canReadPrewhereColumnsAhead`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122508 defines the contract used here for evaluating an `and` argument on more rows.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/71539 enabled `query_plan_merge_filters`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128432 drops the carried and intermediate filter columns that each PREWHERE step filters again, while this patch removes forced filter passes. Both edit the same `PrewhereExprStep` initializer in `tryBuildPrewhereSteps`, each was measured alone against the same master, and their gains are not additive. On the merged table, on top of #128432's first two commits, the first version of this patch (same steps there) changed Q42 by −2.5% [−3.6, −1.3] / −3.7% [−5.5, −1.9] (cache off / on) and Q39 by −5.2% [−7.5, −2.8] with the cache on, and left Q43 and Q39 with the cache off unchanged (8 rounds x 3 servers). On the 12-part table with the cache on, it changed Q42 by −9.6% [−12.3, −6.8] and Q39 by −4.5% [−8.2, −0.7], and Q43 was not significant (5 rounds x 2 servers; cache off not measured).
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128381 (PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128396) makes filtering sparse columns cheaper. Each patch was measured alone against the same master. On the 12-part table, where `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part holding most `CounterID = 62` rows, #128381 makes each filtering pass over it cheaper and this patch removes most of those passes, so their Q42 and Q43 gains there overlap and do not add up. On a merged table or the official load, where `DontCountHits` is dense, #128381 does not change Q42 and Q43 (see the discussion there), while this patch does (table above). `IsLink` and `IsDownload` are sparse in every layout, so on Q39 the two gains overlap in all of them.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128347 caches the rows a PREWHERE selects, so a repeated query with a cached condition skips these steps. Where it applies, the two patches' gains do not add up; first runs and queries whose condition is not cached keep this patch's gain.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124498 reports the cost of per-step filtering for non-selective conjunctions on `Memory`, with a MergeTree comparison (`a < 90 AND b < 90 AND c < 90 AND d < 90`). This patch removes MergeTree's forced filter between such numeric conditions: on that query it takes 433.8 ms instead of 502.6 ms here, against 420.7 ms for one step. It does not change the `Memory` path.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125978 (open) fixes a comparison that `comparisonCanThrow` reports as safe although it can throw (`Tuple` with `Variant`, #125919). #122508 uses this classification only to move a cheap condition ahead of heavier ones; this patch evaluates such a condition on the rows any earlier step rejects, so until #125978 lands, that comparison would throw in a guarded multi-column PREWHERE that master answers.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128342 (open) describes `canThrowIfKnown` for `empty`/`notEmpty`; with it, the `URL <> ''` and `Title <> ''` steps of Q37/Q38 could stop forcing the filter too.

</details>

title: MergeTree on a local disk reads 128 KiB at every isolated granule: end each read at the requested byte ranges (cold ClickBench Q19 -23%, SELECT * point lookup -20%)

text:
MergeTree PREWHERE read steps keep filtering columns that no later step needs; dropping them makes ClickBench Q39 and Q41-Q43 5-16% faster on a fully merged hits table

### Describe the situation
When MergeTree splits PREWHERE into read steps, each step carries the columns earlier steps read and their filter results, and filters them again, even if no later step needs them. Dropping them makes ClickBench Q39 and Q41–Q43 5–16% faster on a fully merged hits table (x86, 4 vCPU).

Server-side mean latency, master vs patched, 10 paired rounds x 3 servers per arm; change with 95% CI.

**`hits` merged into one part** (`OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`): `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` dense, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` sparse.

<details><summary>Why it happens and what the patch changes</summary>

With `enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps` (default), Q43's `WHERE CounterID = 62 AND EventDate >= '2013-07-14' AND EventDate <= '2013-07-15' AND IsRefresh = 0 AND DontCountHits = 0` is read in four PREWHERE steps (`IsRefresh`, `DontCountHits`, `EventDate`, then `CounterID`, primary key columns last) before the main read of `EventTime`. With `query_plan_merge_filters = 1` (default) every step applies its filter, and `ReadResult::applyFilter` filters everything the block still holds. Two kinds of columns stay in the block although nothing reads them:

1. **Projected-out inputs (`ReadResult::additional_columns`).** Each step stores the columns it projects out, so that a later step can compute the `DEFAULT` of a column that is missing in the part (`evaluateMissingDefaults`). Since #111795 they are carried over all later steps, so every step filters the inputs of all earlier steps again. The first commit keeps them only if a later reader of the chain requests a column with a default expression or a subcolumn, which are the only columns `fillMissingColumns` leaves to `evaluateMissingDefaults`. Reads in which a later step requests such a column keep the current behaviour.
2. **Intermediate filter columns.** Since #71539, `tryBuildPrewhereSteps` never assigns `Step::original_node`, so `remove_filter_column` is false for every step except the last, and each `equals(...)` result travels to the end of the read and is filtered at every step. The second commit sets `original_node` for a single-condition step, so its filter column is removed unless it is an output of the original PREWHERE DAG or a later step uses it (the existing check), and removes the AND that combines several conditions of one step, which nothing else references. PREWHERE on `Memory` tables uses the same steps and now drops these columns too; the Parquet reader does not use `remove_filter_column`.

The check in the first commit looks up the default expression of each requested column. A readers chain is built for every read task, while a reader is reused by the consecutive tasks of a part, so the third commit computes the check once per reader and does not ask the first reader, which has no earlier step. Evaluated for every task and every reader, the check took 1.7% of the CPU samples of Q3 with the columns cache and made Q3 and Q8 1–2% slower on the merged table.

CPU samples of Q43 with the columns cache, 12 parts (first two commits): `ReadResult::applyFilter` 15.7% → 0.4%, of which `filterBlock` on the additional columns 11.9% → 0%. What remains is filtering each newly read column with the accumulated filter (about 18%).

Correctness checks:
- Complete grouped results of Q37–Q43 (no `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`) are identical to master with the columns cache on and off, on both tables.
- 24 differential queries over a table with `DEFAULT` and `MATERIALIZED` columns added after the first insert (so some parts miss them), `Nested` and `Tuple` subcolumns, `Nullable` and `LowCardinality` conditions, a condition reused by a later one, a condition selected as an output, and lightweight `DELETE`/`UPDATE`: identical results. 12 similar queries on a `Memory` table: identical results.
- 405 stateless tests matching `prewhere`, `missing`, `default_expr`, `multistep`, `read_steps`, `patch_part`, `lightweight_update`, `lightweight_delete`, `add_column` and `alter_column`: 347 pass (including `04628_multistep_prewhere_default_column`, `05227_single_step_prewhere_default_column` and the `02559_multiple_read_steps_in_prewhere*` tests); the other 58 fail or time out the same way on master in this environment (no `test.hits`, clusters, ZooKeeper or S3).

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master e4afc4fd7f50f14b0bb11ad83a9c0b85f3cc1b59 (26.11.1); no change to these code paths up to 1ee49128da7308cf86b6b769ba651cabf885b07d. Intermediate filter columns are kept since #71539 (November 2024); the projected-out columns are carried over all steps since #111795 (August 2026).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

- Data: ClickBench `hits` loaded with the official `create.sql` (MergeTree, `ORDER BY (CounterID, EventDate, UserID, EventTime, WatchID)`) plus `auto_statistics_types = ''`, 99,997,497 rows. Main table: merged into one part with `OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`; `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` (6.7% and 9.4% non-zero rows) use the default serialization, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` (2.1% and 0.9%) sparse serialization. Second table: the same rows in 12 parts, merges stopped.
- Queries: lines 37–43 of ClickBench `queries.sql` (Q37–Q43), with Q3 and Q8 as controls. Default settings (4 threads); for the "on" rows `use_columns_cache = 1`.
- Hardware and build: AWS x86 4 vCPU (Xeon 8375C), 30 GiB; Release build, clang 21, both binaries from the same build directory.
- Procedure: three servers per binary on hard-linked copies of the data. In each of 10 rounds, for each server in rotated order and each query, `clickhouse benchmark -c 1 -i 30 --query "..."` after 15 warm-up runs. Latency is the mean server-side duration of the 30 runs from `system.query_log` (`QueryFinish`, `event_time_microseconds - query_start_time_microseconds`), then the geometric mean over the three servers of a binary. The change is the geometric mean of the 10 per-round ratios with a 95% t-interval.
- Throughput: merged table, 2 servers per binary, `clickhouse benchmark -c 4 -i 500` over Q37, Q39, Q41, Q42 and Q43, 4 alternating rounds; median QPS.

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

Splitting PREWHERE into read steps should not make later steps copy columns that no later step or output needs; each column should be filtered about once, as with a single step.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111795 carries the projected-out columns over all later steps, to fix missing `DEFAULT` columns.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117533 keeps a removed filter column among them for the same purpose.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/71539 left `Step::original_node` unset.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/118630 (open, checked at 8897fe8) changes the same decision, `keep_additional_columns`. When patch parts exist, it applies them at every step boundary to the projected-out columns as well, and re-evaluates from them the `DEFAULT` columns filled by this or an earlier step. If both land, a step must also keep these columns in that case, e.g. `(!is_last_reader && later_reader_may_evaluate_defaults) || (!patch_readers.empty() && !result.columns_filled_by_defaults.empty())`, not only when a later step may evaluate defaults.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124498 reports these kept intermediate filter columns for split PREWHERE on `Memory`, with a MergeTree comparison. The second commit removes them for both engines; it was not measured on that workload. The other causes it names, filtering each later-read column from full size by the combined mask and the scalar mask merge, are not changed.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124484 attributes wrong values for a stored column named like a condition to the same unset `original_node`; open https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125670 fixes it by renaming such computed columns and does not change `remove_filter_column`. The second commit still keeps a filter column that a later step or output uses, so it does not replace that fix.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128381 (PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128396) makes filtering sparse columns cheaper. Each patch was measured alone against the same master. On the 12-part table, its Q39, Q42 and Q43 gains come largely from the repeated filtering of sparse flag columns at later PREWHERE steps, which this patch removes, so the two gains do not add up there. On the merged table, where `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` are dense, it does not change Q42 and Q43 (see the discussion there), while this patch does.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128347 caches the rows a PREWHERE selects, so a repeated query can skip these steps. Where it applies, the two patches' gains on repeated Q37-Q42 do not add up; first runs and queries whose condition is not cached keep this patch's gain.

</details>

### Additional context
<details><summary>Full patch</summary>

Three commits on e4afc4fd: "Keep the columns projected out by a PREWHERE step only when a later step may evaluate defaults of missing columns", "Remove the filter column of an intermediate PREWHERE step when no later step or output uses it" and "Compute mayEvaluateMissingDefaults once per reader and do not ask the first reader of the chain".

title: MergeTree PREWHERE read steps keep filtering columns that no later step needs; dropping them makes ClickBench Q39 and Q41-Q43 5-16% faster on a fully merged hits table
body:
### Describe the situation
When MergeTree splits PREWHERE into read steps, each step carries the columns earlier steps read and their filter results, and filters them again, even if no later step needs them. Dropping them makes ClickBench Q39 and Q41–Q43 5–16% faster on a fully merged hits table (x86, 4 vCPU).

Server-side mean latency, master vs patched, 10 paired rounds x 3 servers per arm; change with 95% CI.

**`hits` merged into one part** (`OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`): `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` dense, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` sparse.

| Query, columns cache, layout | master, ms | patched, ms | Change [95% CI] |

| Q43, cache off, 1 part | 11.22 | 10.07 | −10.3% [−12.1, −8.5] |
| Q42, cache off, 1 part | 14.38 | 13.21 | −8.2% [−9.1, −7.2] |

On the same rows in 12 parts with merges stopped (second table below), the gains are slightly larger, e.g. Q43 −11.9% and Q42 −8.8% with the cache off: there `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part that holds most of the rows these queries read, and a sparse column costs more to filter again than a dense one.

<details><summary>Same comparison on 12 parts with merges stopped, where DontCountHits is sparse</summary>

The `CounterID = 62` rows are in two of the 12 parts. `DontCountHits` is sparse in the part with 613,490 of these 738,172 rows; `IsLink` and `IsDownload` are sparse in both; `IsRefresh` is dense in both.

The first Q3 run with the cache on includes one batch of 30 runs at 31.6 ms on one patched server (all other batches 17.2–18.6 ms), so Q3 and Q8 were measured again ("repeat").

</details>

<details><summary>Why it happens and what the patch changes</summary>

With `enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps` (default), Q43's `WHERE CounterID = 62 AND EventDate >= '2013-07-14' AND EventDate <= '2013-07-15' AND IsRefresh = 0 AND DontCountHits = 0` is read in four PREWHERE steps (`IsRefresh`, `DontCountHits`, `EventDate`, then `CounterID`, primary key columns last) before the main read of `EventTime`. With `query_plan_merge_filters = 1` (default) every step applies its filter, and `ReadResult::applyFilter` filters everything the block still holds. Two kinds of columns stay in the block although nothing reads them:

1. **Projected-out inputs (`ReadResult::additional_columns`).** Each step stores the columns it projects out, so that a later step can compute the `DEFAULT` of a column that is missing in the part (`evaluateMissingDefaults`). Since #111795 they are carried over all later steps, so every step filters the inputs of all earlier steps again. The first commit keeps them only if a later reader of the chain requests a column with a default expression or a subcolumn, which are the only columns `fillMissingColumns` leaves to `evaluateMissingDefaults`. Reads in which a later step requests such a column keep the current behaviour.
2. **Intermediate filter columns.** Since #71539, `tryBuildPrewhereSteps` never assigns `Step::original_node`, so `remove_filter_column` is false for every step except the last, and each `equals(...)` result travels to the end of the read and is filtered at every step. The second commit sets `original_node` for a single-condition step, so its filter column is removed unless it is an output of the original PREWHERE DAG or a later step uses it (the existing check), and removes the AND that combines several conditions of one step, which nothing else references. PREWHERE on `Memory` tables uses the same steps and now drops these columns too; the Parquet reader does not use `remove_filter_column`.

The check in the first commit looks up the default expression of each requested column. A readers chain is built for every read task, while a reader is reused by the consecutive tasks of a part, so the third commit computes the check once per reader and does not ask the first reader, which has no earlier step. Evaluated for every task and every reader, the check took 1.7% of the CPU samples of Q3 with the columns cache and made Q3 and Q8 1–2% slower on the merged table.

CPU samples of Q43 with the columns cache, 12 parts (first two commits): `ReadResult::applyFilter` 15.7% → 0.4%, of which `filterBlock` on the additional columns 11.9% → 0%. What remains is filtering each newly read column with the accumulated filter (about 18%).

Correctness checks:
- Complete grouped results of Q37–Q43 (no `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`) are identical to master with the columns cache on and off, on both tables.
- 24 differential queries over a table with `DEFAULT` and `MATERIALIZED` columns added after the first insert (so some parts miss them), `Nested` and `Tuple` subcolumns, `Nullable` and `LowCardinality` conditions, a condition reused by a later one, a condition selected as an output, and lightweight `DELETE`/`UPDATE`: identical results. 12 similar queries on a `Memory` table: identical results.
- 405 stateless tests matching `prewhere`, `missing`, `default_expr`, `multistep`, `read_steps`, `patch_part`, `lightweight_update`, `lightweight_delete`, `add_column` and `alter_column`: 347 pass (including `04628_multistep_prewhere_default_column`, `05227_single_step_prewhere_default_column` and the `02559_multiple_read_steps_in_prewhere*` tests); the other 58 fail or time out the same way on master in this environment (no `test.hits`, clusters, ZooKeeper or S3).

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master e4afc4fd7f50f14b0bb11ad83a9c0b85f3cc1b59 (26.11.1); no change to these code paths up to 1ee49128da7308cf86b6b769ba651cabf885b07d. Intermediate filter columns are kept since #71539 (November 2024); the projected-out columns are carried over all steps since #111795 (August 2026).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

- Data: ClickBench `hits` loaded with the official `create.sql` (MergeTree, `ORDER BY (CounterID, EventDate, UserID, EventTime, WatchID)`) plus `auto_statistics_types = ''`, 99,997,497 rows. Main table: merged into one part with `OPTIMIZE TABLE hits FINAL`; `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` (6.7% and 9.4% non-zero rows) use the default serialization, `IsLink` and `IsDownload` (2.1% and 0.9%) sparse serialization. Second table: the same rows in 12 parts, merges stopped.
- Queries: lines 37–43 of ClickBench `queries.sql` (Q37–Q43), with Q3 and Q8 as controls. Default settings (4 threads); for the "on" rows `use_columns_cache = 1`.
- Hardware and build: AWS x86 4 vCPU (Xeon 8375C), 30 GiB; Release build, clang 21, both binaries from the same build directory.
- Procedure: three servers per binary on hard-linked copies of the data. In each of 10 rounds, for each server in rotated order and each query, `clickhouse benchmark -c 1 -i 30 --query "..."` after 15 warm-up runs. Latency is the mean server-side duration of the 30 runs from `system.query_log` (`QueryFinish`, `event_time_microseconds - query_start_time_microseconds`), then the geometric mean over the three servers of a binary. The change is the geometric mean of the 10 per-round ratios with a 95% t-interval.
- Throughput: merged table, 2 servers per binary, `clickhouse benchmark -c 4 -i 500` over Q37, Q39, Q41, Q42 and Q43, 4 alternating rounds; median QPS.

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

Splitting PREWHERE into read steps should not make later steps copy columns that no later step or output needs; each column should be filtered about once, as with a single step.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111795 carries the projected-out columns over all later steps, to fix missing `DEFAULT` columns.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117533 keeps a removed filter column among them for the same purpose.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/71539 left `Step::original_node` unset.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/118630 (open, checked at 8897fe8) changes the same decision, `keep_additional_columns`. When patch parts exist, it applies them at every step boundary to the projected-out columns as well, and re-evaluates from them the `DEFAULT` columns filled by this or an earlier step. If both land, a step must also keep these columns in that case, e.g. `(!is_last_reader && later_reader_may_evaluate_defaults) || (!patch_readers.empty() && !result.columns_filled_by_defaults.empty())`, not only when a later step may evaluate defaults.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124498 reports these kept intermediate filter columns for split PREWHERE on `Memory`, with a MergeTree comparison. The second commit removes them for both engines; it was not measured on that workload. The other causes it names, filtering each later-read column from full size by the combined mask and the scalar mask merge, are not changed.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124484 attributes wrong values for a stored column named like a condition to the same unset `original_node`; open https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125670 fixes it by renaming such computed columns and does not change `remove_filter_column`. The second commit still keeps a filter column that a later step or output uses, so it does not replace that fix.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128381 (PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128396) makes filtering sparse columns cheaper. Each patch was measured alone against the same master. On the 12-part table, its Q39, Q42 and Q43 gains come largely from the repeated filtering of sparse flag columns at later PREWHERE steps, which this patch removes, so the two gains do not add up there. On the merged table, where `IsRefresh` and `DontCountHits` are dense, it does not change Q42 and Q43 (see the discussion there), while this patch does.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128347 caches the rows a PREWHERE selects, so a repeated query can skip these steps. Where it applies, the two patches' gains on repeated Q37-Q42 do not add up; first runs and queries whose condition is not cached keep this patch's gain.

</details>

### Additional context
<details><summary>Full patch</summary>

Three commits on e4afc4fd: "Keep the columns projected out by a PREWHERE step only when a later step may evaluate defaults of missing columns", "Remove the filter column of an intermediate PREWHERE step when no later step or output uses it" and "Compute mayEvaluateMissingDefaults once per reader and do not ask the first reader of the chain".

`mayEvaluateMissingDefaults` restates when `fillMissingColumns` leaves a column to `evaluateMissingDefaults` (a `DEFAULT` expression, or a subcolumn of an available column). arrayIntersect fails with a literal [NULL] argument: Conversion from UInt8 to Nothing is not supported

**Describe what's wrong**

`arrayIntersect` fails when one argument is a literal array of `NULL`s, such as `[NULL]`, and another argument has typed elements. The same call works when `[NULL]` is cast to the other argument's type.

```sql
SELECT arrayIntersect([1, NULL], [NULL]);
-- Code: 70. DB::Exception: Conversion from UInt8 to Nothing is not supported. (CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE)

SELECT arrayIntersect([1, NULL], CAST([NULL] AS Array(Nullable(UInt8))));
-- [NULL]

SELECT arrayIntersect([1, 2], [NULL]);
-- Code: 386. DB::Exception: There is no subtype for types UInt8, Nothing because some of them are Nothing. (NO_COMMON_TYPE)

SELECT arrayIntersect([1, 2], []);
-- []
```

The failure also happens for a table column, even with no rows, for example `arrayIntersect(a, [NULL])` where `a` is `Array(Nullable(UInt8))`. `arrayUnion` and `arraySymmetricDifference` accept the same arguments.

**Does it reproduce on the most recent release?**

Yes, on master (26.11.1.986) and on 25.8.33.6.

**Expected behavior**

`arrayIntersect([1, NULL], [NULL])` returns `[NULL]` and `arrayIntersect([1, 2], [NULL])` returns `[]`, the same values as the `CAST` and `[]` forms above.

**Additional context**

The elements of `[NULL]` have type `Nullable(Nothing)`. `getMostSubtype` over `Nullable(UInt8)` and `Nullable(Nothing)` returns `Nullable(Nothing)`, and the function then tries to cast the other arguments to `Array(Nullable(Nothing))`. With an argument that is not `Nullable`, `getMostSubtype` throws.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128425
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1182-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

UNKNOWN_FUNCTION on repeated run of cluster join with lambda filter

### Describe what's wrong

- Join over an object-storage `*Cluster` function with a lambda filter fails with UNKNOWN_FUNCTION on replicas.
- Trigger is `arrayExists(x -> x > 1 AND x < 1000, [t.a])` in `WHERE`, at default `compile_expressions=1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression=3`.
- First run succeeds; every run after that fails once the lambda body gets compiled.
- Workaround is setting `compile_expressions = 0`.

Root cause: `isSerializableFilterNode` in IStorageCluster.cpp accepts any COLUMN node including a `ColumnFunction` carrying a compiled lambda. The initiator ships that compiled lambda's dump as a function name, and the replica's `ActionsDAG::deserialize` calls `FunctionFactory::get` on it and fails.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `isSerializableFilterNode` (IStorageCluster.cpp:86-90) accepts any `COLUMN` node that is not a set, including the `ColumnFunction` constant carrying the lambda. The initiator planner compiles lambda bodies unless `mayBeSerializedForRemoteExecution` (PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp:1112), which is set only for logical plans and parallel replicas (PlannerContext.cpp:95), so `ActionsDAG::serialize` writes the JIT function's dump as its name. Replica: `addFilterPushedDownByInitiator` (StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1002) -> `ActionsDAG::deserialize` -> `deserializeConstant` -> `FunctionFactory::get` (ActionsDAG.cpp:5646) -> `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp:89`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6529350e55f54c/src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp#L89) — non-set COLUMN nodes (lambda ColumnFunction constants) accepted as serializable
- [`src/Planner/PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp:1112`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6529350e55f54c/src/Planner/PlannerActionsVisitor.cpp#L1112) — lambda bodies compiled unless mayBeSerializedForRemoteExecution
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1002`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6529350e55f54c/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp#L1002) — replica deserializes the shipped filter
- [`src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp:5646`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/6529350e55f54c/src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp#L5646) — FunctionFactory::get on the compiled function's dump name

Impact: A previously working join over an object-storage `*Cluster` function with an array lambda (`arrayExists`, `arrayFilter`, `arrayAll`, ...) on the function's columns in `WHERE` fails on its second and later executions at default settings. Workaround: `compile_expressions = 0`.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Reproduces with `icebergLocalCluster` over a local Parquet table using `min_count_to_compile_expression = 0` to force compilation on first run.

```bash
# A lambda in the filter of a join with a cluster table function must work when the lambda body is compiled.

TABLE="t_default_${RANDOM}"
TABLE_PATH="/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/${TABLE}/"
CLUSTER_FN="icebergLocalCluster('test_shard_localhost', '${TABLE_PATH}', 'Parquet')"

clickhouse-client --query "CREATE TABLE ${TABLE} (a Int64) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('${TABLE_PATH}', 'Parquet')"
clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --query "INSERT INTO ${TABLE} VALUES (1), (2), (3)"

clickhouse-client --query "
    SELECT count() FROM ${CLUSTER_FN} AS t, (SELECT 1 AS k) AS n
    WHERE arrayExists(x -> x > 1 AND x < 1000, [t.a])
    ORDER BY ALL
    SETTINGS compile_expressions = 1, min_count_to_compile_expression = 0"

clickhouse-client --query "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ${TABLE}"
rm -rf "${TABLE_PATH}"
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

The query should return the correct count on every run regardless of lambda compilation.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

From the second execution onward the replica throws UNKNOWN_FUNCTION while deserializing the pushed-down filter.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
Reason: having stderror:
<Error> executeQuery: Code: 46. DB::Exception: Unknown function and(greater(Int64, 1 : UInt8), less(Int64, 1000 : UInt16)). (UNKNOWN_FUNCTION)
5. src/Functions/FunctionFactory.cpp:101:15: DB::FunctionFactory::getImpl
7. src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp:5646:61: DB::ActionsDAG::deserialize
8. src/Interpreters/ActionsDAG.cpp:5343:28: DB::deserializeConstant
9. src/Interpreter
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Reject atoms that contain lambda carriers (`ColumnFunction` constants or `FunctionCapture` nodes) in `isSerializableFilterNode`, or plan with `may_be_serialized_for_remote_execution` set when the table expression is read by `ReadFromCluster`. The first loses pushdown for lambda atoms; the second disables lambda JIT on the initiator for those queries.

</details>

### Additional context

Found during automated review of [PR #125615](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125615); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr125615_002`


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #129182
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1389-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
Evaluate libbz2-rs-sys as an opt-in bzip2 replacement: compatibility, benchmarks and slow-case optimization

Can you investigate whether `libbz2-rs-sys` can replace C bzip2 in ClickHouse without a performance regression? Please own the prototype, compatibility checks, actual benchmarking and targeted optimization, not just a literature review.

Use upstream ClickHouse and the public `libbz2-rs-sys` crate. Start with version 0.2.6; explain any reason to evaluate another version separately.

### 1. Prototype

Add an opt-in `USE_BZIP2_RS` CMake option, default OFF, using the existing `BZ2_*` C ABI. Cover ClickHouse's bzip2 readers/writers and archive consumers. Preserve the existing C build unchanged as the baseline. Check ABI, allocator, error-handling and supported-platform compatibility. Do not equate “written in Rust” with an end-to-end memory-safety guarantee.

### 2. Correctness

Run the existing bzip2 functional tests with the option ON and OFF on amd64 and arm64. Include truncated and concatenated streams and archive handling. Verify interoperability in both directions: C compression → Rust decompression and Rust compression → C decompression. Check encoder byte equivalence separately; it is not implied by a successful roundtrip. Do not weaken or skip tests.

### 3. Benchmark

Use ClickHouse's performance tooling with matched Release builds from the same source revision. Measure compression at levels 1 and 9 and decompression of both, using identical inputs of at least 100 MB. Run at least 7 successful measured samples per case after warmup on amd64 and arm64. Interleave implementations, avoid concurrent build/test workloads, and verify that timeouts or adaptive stopping did not truncate the sample count.

Publish exact commands, revisions, hardware, compiler/Rust versions, effective optimization/LTO/CPU flags, input hashes and raw measurements. Report medians, standard deviations, Rust/C ratios, justified 95% confidence intervals, query-accounted peak memory and binary-size deltas. Distinguish query memory from process RSS.

### 4. Decision

Target no more than 1% slowdown on every case. If results are inconclusive, say so. If Rust is slower, profile the bottleneck and evaluate targeted optimizations one at a time without degrading the C baseline or changing the workload. Report unsuccessful experiments too.

Return a reproducible report and the prototype patch. If execution is unavailable, name the exact blocker and mark measurements as not executed. Keep defaults unchanged and do not open a PR until asked.

### 5. Slow cases and optimization

Go beyond the main dataset. Compare C and Rust across small inputs, large streams, highly repetitive data, incompressible data, mixed text/binary data, concatenated streams, and streaming reads/writes with different chunk sizes. Cover compression levels 1–9 in this supplementary matrix.

Separate valid-input throughput from malformed/truncated-input rejection cost. Keep malformed-input experiments bounded by time and memory limits.

For each reproducible Rust slowdown:

- Preserve the input or a deterministic generator and publish the reproduction command.
- Profile both implementations and identify the hot path. Distinguish algorithm cost, allocations/copies, bounds checks, buffering, and compiler/code-generation differences.
- Implement targeted fixes where supported by the evidence. Keep crate changes in a reviewable upstream patch, not an untracked vendor edit.
- Re-run correctness checks and the original benchmark matrix after each candidate fix. Reject fixes that weaken safety, change semantics, exceed the supported CPU baseline, or shift the regression onto another workload.
- Report before/after timings, uncertainty, memory use and remaining gaps. Do not hide individual slow cases behind an aggregate average.

Keep the original acceptance workload fixed. Treat the supplementary matrix as additional evidence, not a replacement for failed measurements. If the search becomes open-ended, stop with the measured slow cases ranked by impact and the next concrete optimization experiment.

text:
Reading a view whose body has two `ARRAY JOIN`s fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` since 26.8

### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe what's wrong

A `SELECT` from an ordinary view whose body has two `ARRAY JOIN` clauses fails with `Code: 48. Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)`. The same `SELECT` run directly works. 26.6 and 26.7 read the view fine; 26.8 and later throw.

The exception comes from `tryGetTrivialViewUnderlyingStorage()` in `src/Storages/StorageView.cpp`, added in #101791. It tests `select->arrayJoinExpressionList().first`, and `ASTSelectQuery::arrayJoinExpressionList()` goes through `getFirstArrayJoin()`, which throws on the second `ARRAY JOIN` instead of returning the first one. The check only needs to know whether there is any `ARRAY JOIN` at all.

Consequences:
- a refreshable materialized view that selects from such a view fails on every refresh (`REFRESH_FAILED`, cause `Code: 48`);
- `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0` avoids the error for an `SQL SECURITY INVOKER` view, but on 26.10 and 26.11 an `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view still fails with the setting off: there the same function is also called from `StorageView::isSealed()` (stack below).


### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

Official Docker images `clickhouse/clickhouse-server`, default config and settings, `clickhouse-client`.

| version | `SELECT * FROM v` | same, `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0` | `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view, setting `= 0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26.6.8.7 | OK | (no such setting) | (no such setting) |
| 26.7.38.18 | OK | (no such setting) | (no such setting) |
| 26.8.36.3 | Code: 48 | OK | OK |
| 26.9.27.3 | Code: 48 | OK | OK |
| 26.10.3.7 | Code: 48 | OK | Code: 48 |
| 26.11.1.974 (`head`, a7f713612c80) | Code: 48 | OK | Code: 48 |

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, a Array(Array(UInt32))) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, [[1, 2], [3]]);
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y;

SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y ORDER BY y;  -- OK, 3 rows
SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y;                                           -- Code: 48
SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;  -- OK, 3 rows

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv REFRESH EVERY 1 HOUR ENGINE = Memory AS SELECT * FROM v;
SYSTEM WAIT VIEW mv;                                                  -- Code: 730 REFRESH_FAILED, cause Code: 48

CREATE VIEW vd SQL SECURITY DEFINER AS SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y;
SELECT * FROM vd ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;  -- Code: 48 on 26.10 and 26.11
```

Output on 26.11.1.974:

```
:) SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y ORDER BY y;
   ┌─id─┬─y─┐
1. │  1 │ 1 │
2. │  1 │ 2 │
3. │  1 │ 3 │
   └────┴───┘
:) SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y;
Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
:) SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;
   ┌─id─┬─y─┐
1. │  1 │ 1 │
2. │  1 │ 2 │
3. │  1 │ 3 │
   └────┴───┘
:) SYSTEM WAIT VIEW mv;
Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 730. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Refresh failed: Code: 48. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED),. (REFRESH_FAILED)
:) SELECT * FROM vd ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;
Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
```


### Expected behavior

`SELECT * FROM v` returns the same three rows as the view body, as on 26.7; the refresh of `mv` succeeds.


### Error message and/or stacktrace

26.10.3.7, failed refresh of `mv` (`system.view_refreshes.exception`):

```
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
4. DB::ASTSelectQuery::arrayJoinExpressionList() const
5. DB::(anonymous namespace)::tryGetTrivialViewUnderlyingStorage(boost::intrusive_ptr<DB::IAST> const&, std::shared_ptr<DB::Context const>)
6. DB::StorageView::tryGetUnderlyingDistributed(std::shared_ptr<DB::StorageSnapshot> const&, std::shared_ptr<DB::Context const>) const
7. DB::(anonymous namespace)::buildQueryPlanForTableExpression(...)
8. DB::buildJoinTreeQueryPlan(...)
9. DB::Planner::buildPlanForQueryNode()
```

26.11.1.974, `SELECT ... FROM vd` with `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0` (`system.query_log.stack_trace`):

```
4. DB::ASTSelectQuery::arrayJoinExpressionList() const
5. DB::(anonymous namespace)::tryGetTrivialViewUnderlyingStorage(boost::intrusive_ptr<DB::IAST> const&, std::shared_ptr<DB::Context const>)
6. DB::StorageView::isSealed(DB::StorageInMemoryMetadata const&, std::shared_ptr<DB::Context const> const&) const
7. DB::StorageView::readImpl(...)
```


### Related issues and pull requests

Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101791

title: Reading a view whose body has two `ARRAY JOIN`s fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` since 26.8
body:
### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe what's wrong

A `SELECT` from an ordinary view whose body has two `ARRAY JOIN` clauses fails with `Code: 48. Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)`. The same `SELECT` run directly works. 26.6 and 26.7 read the view fine; 26.8 and later throw.

The exception comes from `tryGetTrivialViewUnderlyingStorage()` in `src/Storages/StorageView.cpp`, added in #101791. It tests `select->arrayJoinExpressionList().first`, and `ASTSelectQuery::arrayJoinExpressionList()` goes through `getFirstArrayJoin()`, which throws on the second `ARRAY JOIN` instead of returning the first one. The check only needs to know whether there is any `ARRAY JOIN` at all.

Consequences:
- a refreshable materialized view that selects from such a view fails on every refresh (`REFRESH_FAILED`, cause `Code: 48`);
- `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0` avoids the error for an `SQL SECURITY INVOKER` view, but on 26.10 and 26.11 an `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view still fails with the setting off: there the same function is also called from `StorageView::isSealed()` (stack below).


### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

Official Docker images `clickhouse/clickhouse-server`, default config and settings, `clickhouse-client`.

| version | `SELECT * FROM v` | same, `optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0` | `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` view, setting `= 0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26.6.8.7 | OK | (no such setting) | (no such setting) |
| 26.7.38.18 | OK | (no such setting) | (no such setting) |
| 26.8.36.3 | Code: 48 | OK | OK |
| 26.9.27.3 | Code: 48 | OK | OK |
| 26.10.3.7 | Code: 48 | OK | Code: 48 |
| 26.11.1.974 (`head`, a7f713612c80) | Code: 48 | OK | Code: 48 |

```sql
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, [[1, 2], [3]]);
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y;

SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y ORDER BY y;  -- OK, 3 rows
SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y;                                           -- Code: 48
SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;  -- OK, 3 rows

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv REFRESH EVERY 1 HOUR ENGINE = Memory AS SELECT * FROM v;
SYSTEM WAIT VIEW mv;                                                  -- Code: 730 REFRESH_FAILED, cause Code: 48

CREATE VIEW vd SQL SECURITY DEFINER AS SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y;
SELECT * FROM vd ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;  -- Code: 48 on 26.10 and 26.11
```

Output on 26.11.1.974:

```
:) SELECT id, y FROM t ARRAY JOIN a AS x ARRAY JOIN x AS y ORDER BY y;
   ┌─id─┬─y─┐
1. │  1 │ 1 │
2. │  1 │ 2 │
3. │  1 │ 3 │
   └────┴───┘
:) SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y;
Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
:) SELECT * FROM v ORDER BY y SETTINGS optimize_trivial_view_pushdown_to_distributed = 0;
   ┌─id─┬─y─┐
1. │  1 │ 1 │
2. │  1 │ 2 │
3. │  1 │ 3 │
   └────┴───┘
:) SYSTEM WAIT VIEW mv;
Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 730. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Refresh failed: Code: 48. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED),. (REFRESH_FAILED)

Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:9000. DB::Exception: Support for more than one ARRAY JOIN in query is not implemented. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
```


### Expected behavior

`SELECT * FROM v` returns the same three rows as the view body, as on 26.7; the refresh of `mv` succeeds.

text:
Allow specifying alternative compression codecs when one does not apply for all data types.

### Company or project name

ClickHouse

### Use case

PCO is strictly better than ZSTD, but applies only for numeric types.
This makes it impossible to specify it as the default for supported types and ZSTD as a fallback.
While it would be a natural thing to do, and I want it.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a codec combinator `FirstApplicable`, e.g., `CODEC(FirstApplicable(PCO, ZSTD(3)))`, and allow using it in every context, e.g., `default_compression_codec = 'FirstApplicable(PCO, ZSTD(3))'`.

For the sake of generality, allow explicit usage of the `Multiple` codec, e.g.: 
`FirstApplicable(PCO, Multiple(T64, ZSTD(3)), ZSTD(3))`

### Describe alternatives you've considered

There is also a project on automatic codec selection. It is only loosely related.

### Additional context

The combined codec shouldn't get its own codec byte or header - it only selects the actual codec.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128473
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1527-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
