text:
Parallel replicas for object storage: work stealing breaks the cache locality of the stable task distribution

**Company or project name**

[adsb.exposed](https://adsb.exposed/), an experiment with Iceberg tables read with parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_for_object_storage_tables = 1`), 50 replicas, 26.11.

**Describe the situation**

`StorageObjectStorageStableTaskDistributor` assigns every file to a replica by rendezvous hashing of the replica address and the file path, so that the same file goes to the same replica in every query and is read from its cache. But the assignment doesn't hold in practice: the same query, repeated, keeps reading 20-40% of its bytes from S3 instead of the filesystem cache (counters summed over 50 hosts):

| run | 1/10 sample: from cache / from S3 | full table: from cache / from S3 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.1 GB / 4.9 GB | 5.9 GB / 1.2 GB |
| 2 | 2.7 GB / 0.8 GB | 5.8 GB / 2.4 GB |
| 3 | 2.7 GB / 0.9 GB | 5.3 GB / 3.1 GB |

The likely reason is the work stealing in `getAnyUnprocessedFile`. Once the iterator is exhausted, a replica that asks for a task gets a file of the replica with the most remaining bytes, among the replicas that have already asked for tasks (`replica_seen`), immediately. The wait, `cluster_function_wait_for_replica_ms` (0 by default), only protects the replicas that haven't asked yet. So the files queued for a replica that is busy reading its previous file are taken by whichever replica asks first.

That happens a lot when the iterator is slow, as it is for Iceberg: the initiator reads the manifests while the replicas wait, and at the end most replicas are idle and ask for tasks at the same time. Which replica gets which file then depends on timing, so it is different in every query, and the files end up in the caches of random replicas.

I didn't confirm it from per-file logs, only from the counters: a stable assignment would make the repeated runs read nearly nothing from S3.

**Expected behavior**

A replica shouldn't take a file of a replica that is still working on its own files, at least not before it had a chance to take it. For example:

- steal only from a replica that hasn't asked for a task for some time, i.e. apply a wait (like `cluster_function_wait_for_replica_ms`) since the last request of the owner, not only before its first request, with a non-zero default;
- or, like the reading coordinator of parallel replicas for MergeTree, steal only when the owner has much more work left than the others, so that the balancing doesn't move files when the replicas are roughly balanced;

The distributed cache would make this matter less, because it's shared by the replicas (see ClickHouse/clickhouse-private#84330), but the filesystem cache and the page cache are per replica, and outside ClickHouse Cloud they are the only caches.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128433
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1559-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
Iceberg (and other object storage tables): report total_rows_approx from the row counts in the metadata, so that progress can be shown

### Company or project name

ClickHouse, Inc. ([adsb.exposed](https://adsb.exposed/), which shows a progress bar of the queries computed from `system.processes`)

### Describe the situation

A query reading an Iceberg table reports no total number of rows to read: `total_rows_approx` in `system.processes` (and in the progress of the native/HTTP protocol) stays 0 for the whole query, while `read_rows` grows. A client can't show the progress of such a query.

Measured on ClickHouse Cloud 26.11.1.1311, polling `system.processes` every 0.5 s during one query:

| table | `read_rows` | `total_rows_approx` |
|---|---|---|
| Iceberg table (`IcebergS3`, without a catalog) | 0 → 6.32 billion | **0** throughout |
| MergeTree table with the same data | 0 → 6.02 billion | 342,978,833,268 from the start |

The Iceberg file iterator reports progress per data file as `FileProgress(0, file_size_in_bytes)` (`IcebergIterator.cpp`), i.e. a total in bytes; but `system.processes` has no column for a total in bytes, and the sources of object storage tables never call `ISource::addTotalRowsApprox`, which MergeTree uses.

The number of rows of every data file is known from the metadata before it is read: `record_count` of the manifest entry (required by the Iceberg spec). The same holds for Delta Lake (`numRecords` in the file statistics), and for Parquet files the row count is in the footer.

### Expected

- For Iceberg (and other data lakes), add the `record_count` of every data file returned by the iterator, after the pruning by partitions and min/max, to the total rows to read (`addTotalRowsApprox`), so that `total_rows_approx` reflects the files the query actually reads. With position deletes, the count before applying them is fine as an approximation.
- With parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_for_object_storage_tables`), the initiator iterates the files and can report the total for the whole query.
- For plain `S3`/`File` tables of Parquet files, the row count from the footer (when it is read anyway) could be used the same way.

text:
HTTP `Request URI` trace line logs the `query` parameter with credentials unmasked

**Describe what's wrong**

The HTTP handler logs `Request URI: ...` at `Trace` level (and attaches the URI to the OpenTelemetry span `clickhouse.uri`). `maskSensitiveQueryParametersInURI` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108475) hides parameters whose names look sensitive (`password`, `secret`, `key`, ...), but not the `query` parameter. A query sent in the URL with credentials in its text, for example `s3(url, key, secret)`, is therefore logged URL-encoded with the secret in plain text, even though the `executeQuery` line of the same query shows `[HIDDEN]`. `system.text_log` stores it at its default `trace` level.

The URL-encoded form also escapes `query_masking_rules` written for the plain value (in the test config, `P@ssw0rd` is logged as `P%40ssw0rd` and is not matched).

**Does it reproduce on the most recent release?**

Yes, on master `26.11.1.941`.

**How to reproduce**

```
curl "http://localhost:8123/?query=SELECT+*+FROM+s3(%27http://127.0.0.1:1/x.csv%27,%27AKIAEXAMPLE%27,%27TopSecretValue%27,%27CSV%27,%27a+String%27)"
```

Server log:

```
<Trace> DynamicQueryHandler: Request URI: /?query=SELECT+*+FROM+s3(%27http://127.0.0.1:1/x.csv%27,%27AKIAEXAMPLE%27,%27TopSecretValue%27,%27CSV%27,%27a+String%27)
<Debug> executeQuery: (from 127.0.0.1:59410) SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/x.csv', 'AKIAEXAMPLE', '[HIDDEN]', 'CSV', 'a String') (stage: Complete)
```

**Expected behavior**

The `query` parameter in the logged URI and in the span attribute is either hidden or replaced with the masked query text, so that the trace line does not contain more than the `executeQuery` line.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108475

text:
Credentials of an unknown or not compiled-in table function (typo, or `deltaLake` without Rust) are logged unmasked

**Describe what's wrong**

When a query calls a table function that is not registered in the running server, its credential arguments are written to the server log (`executeQuery` line, the exception `in query:` line) and `system.query_log` in plain text, instead of `[HIDDEN]`.

Since the secret-argument specs moved from the parser to the factory registrations (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123364), `SecretArgumentsRegistry::find` returns no secrets for an `ORDINARY_FUNCTION` name that neither `TableFunctionFactory` nor `FunctionFactory` knows, unless it only differs in case from a function with secrets (`src/Interpreters/SecretArgumentsRegistry.cpp`: "Every table function has a spec, so an unknown function has no secrets"). Unknown table and database engines are masked fail-closed (`maskEveryArgument`), unknown table functions are not. The statement is logged before the table function is resolved, so the secret is already in the log by the time `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` is thrown.

Two ways to hit it:

1. A typo in the table function name, for example `s3Clustr` instead of `s3Cluster`.
2. Docs: naiveBayesClassifier has conflicting duplicate configuration instructions

### Documentation page

https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/functions/regular-functions/machine-learning-functions

### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe the issue

The machine-learning functions page contains two `naiveBayesClassifier` sections with conflicting configuration requirements.

The first section says the model must be configured in ClickHouse's server configuration. The later generated section says that the first argument must be the name of a dictionary with the `NAIVE_BAYES` layout. The current implementation also validates that the named dictionary uses the `NAIVE_BAYES` layout.

Having both instructions on the same page makes it unclear which setup is currently supported. Users following the first section may configure a model that the current function cannot use.

Expected behavior: keep one current description and state that `naiveBayesClassifier` requires a `NAIVE_BAYES` dictionary. If the configuration-file model is still supported, document the two interfaces separately.

### Additional context

Duplicate stale section:
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/reference/functions/regular-functions/machine-learning-functions.mdx#L21

Generated current section:
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/reference/functions/regular-functions/machine-learning-functions.mdx#L269

Current implementation:
https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Functions/FunctionNaiveBayesClassifier.cpp#L379

text:
ReplicatedMergeTree: mutations hang after mutating a fully expired part with ttl_only_drop_parts

### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe what's wrong

With `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` (and default `materialize_ttl_recalculate_only = 0`), MATERIALIZE TTL replaces a fully expired part with an empty part whose level is incremented by one.

On ReplicatedMergeTree the MUTATE_PART entry has `new_part_name = all_0_0_0_1`, but the part committed to disk and to Keeper is `all_0_0_1_1`. When the entry finishes, the replication queue records the entry's part name, not the committed one.

As a result:

- The MATERIALIZE TTL mutation itself finishes.
- Every following mutation has `parts_to_do_names = ['all_0_0_0_1']`, a part that does not exist, and stays `is_done = 0` forever. Table system.mutations shows no fail reason and no postpone reason, and table system.replication_queue is empty.
- The real part `all_0_0_1_1` is not in the queue's virtual parts, so the merge predicate rejects it. It cannot be mutated, dropped by clearEmptyParts or dropped with ALTER TABLE ... DROP PART (fails with PART_IS_TEMPORARILY_LOCKED).

`SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA` (or a server restart) unblocks the mutations, because the queue is re-initialized from the parts in Keeper.

**Fiddle**: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/faca9ec5-0ff0-4be3-963e-d3b25b6839cb

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

Reproduces with the latest 26.3-lts release and the latest version. A single replica is enough.

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (d DateTime, v UInt64)
ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{database}/t', 'r1')
ORDER BY d
SETTINGS ttl_only_drop_parts = 1;

-- one part, all rows will be expired by the TTL below
INSERT INTO t SELECT now() - INTERVAL 10 DAY, number FROM numbers(10);

ALTER TABLE t MODIFY TTL d + INTERVAL 1 DAY SETTINGS materialize_ttl_after_modify = 0;

-- the fully expired part is replaced with an empty part all_0_0_1_1,
-- while the MUTATE_PART entry (and the replication queue) has all_0_0_0_1
ALTER TABLE t MATERIALIZE TTL SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2;

SELECT name, rows FROM system.parts WHERE table = 't' AND active;

-- any following mutation waits for all_0_0_0_1, which does not exist
ALTER TABLE t UPDATE v = v + 1 WHERE 1;
SELECT sleep(3) FORMAT Null;
SELECT mutation_id, command, parts_to_do_names, is_done FROM system.mutations WHERE table = 't' ORDER BY mutation_id;

-- reloading the queue state from Keeper unblocks it
SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA t;
SELECT sleep(3) FORMAT Null;
SELECT mutation_id, command, parts_to_do_names, is_done FROM system.mutations WHERE table = 't' ORDER BY mutation_id;
```

Output:

```
┌─name────────┬─rows─┐
│ all_0_0_1_1 │    0 │
└─────────────┴──────┘
┌─mutation_id─┬─command────────────────────┬─parts_to_do_names─┬─is_done─┐
│ 0000000000  │ (MATERIALIZE TTL)          │ []                │       1 │
│ 0000000001  │ (UPDATE v = v + 1 WHERE 1) │ ['all_0_0_0_1']   │       0 │
└─────────────┴────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴─────────┘
-- after SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA
┌─mutation_id─┬─command────────────────────┬─parts_to_do_names─┬─is_done─┐
│ 0000000000  │ (MATERIALIZE TTL)          │ []                │       1 │
│ 0000000001  │ (UPDATE v = v + 1 WHERE 1) │ []                │       1 │
└─────────────┴────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴─────────┘
```

### Expected behavior

The UPDATE finishes without `SYSTEM RESTART REPLICA`, and the empty part is removed by the cleanup thread.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

There is no error. The cleanup thread logs this on every iteration:

```
<Trace> Will drop empty part all_0_0_1_1
<Debug> Cannot drop part: 'Part all_0_0_1_1 does not contain in snapshot of previous virtual parts'
```

### Related issues and pull requests

Related: [#65488](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/65488) and reintroduces [#72751](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/72751) - MATERIALIZE TTL respects `ttl_only_drop_parts` and drops fully expired parts by replacing them with an empty part

### Additional context

With `materialize_ttl_recalculate_only = 1`, MATERIALIZE TTL only recalculates TTL and keeps `all_0_0_0_1` with its rows. The part is then dropped by a regular TTLDropMerge through a MERGE_PARTS entry, and the following mutations finish. This works as a workaround.

The existing test [05210_materialize_ttl_of_attached_part_with_dropped_column](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/cc5af2c4d1b181d0d3106f36161bea69d035eed7/tests/queries/0_stateless/05210_materialize_ttl_of_attached_part_with_dropped_column.sql) has a replicated arm, but its TTL never expires, so the empty-part path is not covered for ReplicatedMergeTree.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128644
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1409-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

Paimon `ADD COLUMNS` is invisible until the next commit: ClickHouse uses the snapshot schema id instead of the latest schema

### Describe what's wrong

A Paimon schema change (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS`, `RENAME COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, ...) writes a new `schema/schema-N` file but no new snapshot. ClickHouse takes the table schema from the `schemaId` of the latest snapshot instead of the latest schema file, so the change is invisible until some later commit creates a snapshot: `SELECT <added column>` fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, and `DESCRIBE` shows the old columns. Spark, Flink and pypaimon read the table with the latest schema and return the added column as NULL for the existing rows.

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295), `spark_paimon`, seed 0 (Spark `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS` after an append). Reproduced below with pypaimon, without a JVM.

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Reproduced on `master`: `SELECT version()` = `26.11.1.941`, commit `a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840`.

### How to reproduce

Writer (`pip install pypaimon`, tested with pypaimon 2.1.0):

```python
# write_add_column.py
import sys
import pyarrow as pa
from pypaimon import CatalogFactory, Schema
from pypaimon.schema.data_types import AtomicType
from pypaimon.schema.schema_change import SchemaChange

catalog = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": sys.argv[1]})
catalog.create_database("default", True)
schema = pa.schema([("id", pa.int64()), ("a", pa.string())])
catalog.create_table("default.t_add", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema, options={"file.format": "parquet"}), False)
table = catalog.get_table("default.t_add")
wb = table.new_batch_write_builder()
w, c = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit()
w.write_arrow(pa.Table.from_pylist([{"id": 1, "a": "x"}], schema=schema))
c.commit(w.prepare_commit())
w.close()
c.close()

# Schema change only: writes schema/schema-1, no new snapshot.
catalog.alter_table("default.t_add", [SchemaChange.add_column("b", AtomicType("INT"))])

t = catalog.get_table("default.t_add")
rb = t.new_read_builder()
print("pypaimon:", rb.new_read().to_arrow(rb.new_scan().plan().splits()).to_pylist())
```

```bash
python3 write_add_column.py /tmp/wh
# pypaimon: [{'id': 1, 'a': 'x', 'b': None}]
ls /tmp/wh/default.db/t_add/schema /tmp/wh/default.db/t_add/snapshot
# schema-0 schema-1    LATEST snapshot-1
clickhouse local -q "DESCRIBE paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add')"
clickhouse local -q "SELECT id, a, b FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add')"
```

The same happens with Spark: `INSERT INTO paimon.default.t VALUES (...)`, then `ALTER TABLE paimon.default.t ADD COLUMNS (b INT)`; Spark `SELECT * FROM paimon.default.t` returns `b` as NULL.

### Expected behavior

`DESCRIBE` lists `id`, `a`, `b`, and the query returns `1	x	\N`, as pypaimon and Spark do.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

`DESCRIBE` lists only `id` and `a`, and:

```
Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown expression identifier `b`. Maybe you meant: ['a']. In scope SELECT id, a, b FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add'). (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)
```

After the next commit to the table (for example one more append), the column appears. The same applies to `RENAME COLUMN` and `DROP COLUMN`: until the next commit ClickHouse keeps exposing the old name or the dropped column.

### Root cause

`PaimonMetadata::loadLatestState` takes `schema_id` from the latest snapshot ([`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp:326-341`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L326-L341), the comment says "use schema_id, not latest"), and `getTableSchema` / `buildStorageMetadataFromState` build the columns from that id ([`:420-428`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L420-L428), [`:448-460`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L448-L460)). In Paimon the table schema of a read of the latest state is the latest schema file (`SchemaManager.latest()`), while a snapshot's `schemaId` is only the schema that the commit was written with; data files are then mapped from their own schema to the read schema. Using the latest schema file for the latest state (and the snapshot schema only for time travel) fixes the `ADD COLUMNS` case directly; for `RENAME` / `DROP` the per-file field id mapping from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127545 is needed as well, otherwise exposing the latest schema earlier makes the by-name problem appear earlier too.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127545


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128335
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1003-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

```python
catalog = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": sys.argv[1]})
catalog.create_database("default", True)
schema = pa.schema([("id", pa.int64()), ("a", pa.string())])
catalog.create_table("default.t_add", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema, options={"file.format": "parquet"}), False)
table = catalog.get_table("default.t_add")
wb = table.new_batch_write_builder()
w, c = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit()
w.write_arrow(pa.Table.from_pylist([{"id": 1, "a": "x"}], schema=schema))
c.commit(w.prepare_commit())
w.close()
c.close()

# Schema change only: writes schema/schema-1, no new snapshot.
catalog.alter_table("default.t_add", [SchemaChange.add_column("b", AtomicType("INT"))])

t = catalog.get_table("default.t_add")
rb = t.new_read_builder()
print("pypaimon:", rb.new_read().to_arrow(rb.new_scan().plan().splits()).to_pylist())
```

```bash
python3 write_add_column.py /tmp/wh
# pypaimon: [{'id': 1, 'a': 'x', 'b': None}]
ls /tmp/wh/default.db/t_add/schema /tmp/wh/default.db/t_add/snapshot
# schema-0 schema-1    LATEST snapshot-1
clickhouse local -q "DESCRIBE paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add')"
clickhouse local -q "SELECT id, a, b FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add')"
```

The same happens with Spark: `INSERT INTO paimon.default.t VALUES (...)`, then `ALTER TABLE paimon.default.t ADD COLUMNS (b INT)`; Spark `SELECT * FROM paimon.default.t` returns `b` as NULL.

### Expected behavior

`DESCRIBE` lists `id`, `a`, `b`, and the query returns `1	x	\N`, as pypaimon and Spark do.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

`DESCRIBE` lists only `id` and `a`, and:

```
Code: 47. DB::Exception: Unknown expression identifier `b`. Maybe you meant: ['a']. In scope SELECT id, a, b FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_add'). (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)
```

After the next commit to the table (for example one more append), the column appears. The same applies to `RENAME COLUMN` and `DROP COLUMN`: until the next commit ClickHouse keeps exposing the old name or the dropped column.

### Root cause

`PaimonMetadata::loadLatestState` takes `schema_id` from the latest snapshot ([`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp:326-341`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L326-L341), the comment says "use schema_id, not latest"), and `getTableSchema` / `buildStorageMetadataFromState` build the columns from that id ([`:420-428`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L420-L428), [`:448-460`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/PaimonMetadata.cpp#L448-L460)). In Paimon the table schema of a read of the latest state is the latest schema file (`SchemaManager.latest()`), while a snapshot's `schemaId` is only the schema that the commit was written with; data files are then mapped from their own schema to the read schema. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127545

text:
Paimon tables with a `ROW` (struct) column are unreadable: "Unsupported Paimon type: ROW"

### Describe what's wrong

A Paimon table with a `ROW` (struct) column cannot be read at all: `DESCRIBE`, `SELECT *` and even `SELECT id` (a column that is not the struct) fail with `Unsupported Paimon type: ROW` (`BAD_ARGUMENTS`). The Paimon type parser handles the nested types `ARRAY` and `MAP` but not `ROW`. `ROW` is a standard Paimon type that Spark (`STRUCT<...>`), Flink and pypaimon all write, and the Parquet data file itself reads fine as a `Tuple`.

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295), `spark_paimon`, seed 1 (table written by Spark). Reproduced below with pypaimon, without a JVM.

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Reproduced on `master`: `SELECT version()` = `26.11.1.941`, commit `a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840`.

### How to reproduce

Writer (`pip install pypaimon`, tested with pypaimon 2.1.0):

```python
# write_row.py
import sys
import pyarrow as pa
from pypaimon import CatalogFactory, Schema

catalog = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": sys.argv[1]})
catalog.create_database("default", True)
schema = pa.schema([("id", pa.int64()), ("s", pa.struct([("f0", pa.string()), ("f1", pa.int32())]))])
catalog.create_table("default.t_row", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema, options={"file.format": "parquet"}), False)
table = catalog.get_table("default.t_row")
wb = table.new_batch_write_builder()
w, c = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit()
w.write_arrow(pa.Table.from_pylist([{"id": 1, "s": {"f0": "a", "f1": 1}}], schema=schema))
c.commit(w.prepare_commit())
w.close()
c.close()
```

```bash
python3 write_row.py /tmp/wh
clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_row')"
clickhouse local -q "SELECT id FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_row')"
```

The schema file written by pypaimon (Spark writes the same shape):

```json
{"id": 1, "name": "s", "type": {"type": "ROW", "fields": [{"id": 2, "name": "f0", "type": "STRING"}, {"id": 3, "name": "f1", "type": "INT"}], "nullable": true}}
```

### Expected behavior

`s` is read as a named `Tuple(f0 Nullable(String), f1 Nullable(Int32))` (as Iceberg `struct` and Delta Lake `struct` are), and the query returns `1	('a',1)`.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

```
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unsupported Paimon type: ROW. (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
```

### Root cause

The composite branch of the Paimon type parser only knows `ARRAY` and `MAP` and throws for everything else: [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h:272-288`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h#L272-L288). A `ROW` case needs to parse `fields` recursively into a named `DataTypeTuple`. Since nested field ids are also assigned (`f0` is id 2 above), the by-name column resolution issue https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127545 applies to struct subfields as well.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109758 (made the error message for this case readable, the type is still unsupported)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115042

- Merged into: `26.11.1.1063-master` (included in `26.11` and later)

text:
Paimon `DATE` is read as `Date` instead of `Date32`: dates before 1970 or after 2149 fail with VALUE_IS_OUT_OF_RANGE_OF_DATA_TYPE

### Describe what's wrong

ClickHouse maps the Paimon `DATE` type to `Date` instead of `Date32`. `Date` only covers 1970-01-01 to 2149-06-06, so any Paimon table holding a date outside that range fails to read: `1969-12-31` gives `Input value -1 is out of allowed Date range` (`VALUE_IS_OUT_OF_RANGE_OF_DATA_TYPE`), and `2200-01-01` gives `Input value 84006 is out of allowed Date range`. A single such value makes every query touching the column fail. Paimon `DATE` is a 32-bit day count, the same as Iceberg and Delta Lake `date`, which ClickHouse already maps to `Date32` (`Iceberg/SchemaProcessor.cpp`, `DeltaLakeMetadata.cpp`).

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295), `spark_paimon`, seed 0 (table written by Spark). Reproduced below with pypaimon, without a JVM.

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Reproduced on `master`: `SELECT version()` = `26.11.1.941`, commit `a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840`.

### How to reproduce

Writer (`pip install pypaimon`, tested with pypaimon 2.1.0):

```python
# write_date.py
import sys, datetime
import pyarrow as pa
from pypaimon import CatalogFactory, Schema

catalog = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": sys.argv[1]})
catalog.create_database("default", True)
schema = pa.schema([("id", pa.int64()), ("d", pa.date32())])
catalog.create_table("default.t_date", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema, options={"file.format": "parquet"}), False)
table = catalog.get_table("default.t_date")
wb = table.new_batch_write_builder()
w, c = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit()
w.write_arrow(pa.Table.from_pylist([{"id": 1, "d": datetime.date(1969, 12, 31)}, {"id": 2, "d": datetime.date(2024, 1, 1)}], schema=schema))
c.commit(w.prepare_commit())
w.close()
c.close()
```

```bash
python3 write_date.py /tmp/wh
clickhouse local -q "DESCRIBE paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_date')"
clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_date') ORDER BY id"
# the data file itself reads fine:
clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('/tmp/wh/default.db/t_date/bucket-0/*.parquet') ORDER BY id"
```

### Expected behavior

`d` is `Nullable(Date32)` and the query returns:

```
1	1969-12-31
2	2024-01-01
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

`DESCRIBE` reports `d Nullable(Date)` and the `SELECT` fails:

```
Code: 321. DB::Exception: Input value -1 is out of allowed Date range, which is [0, 65535]: read stage: ColumnData: column: d: (in file/uri /tmp/wh/default.db/t_date/bucket-0/data-...-0.parquet): While executing ParquetV3BlockInputFormat: While executing ReadFromObjectStorage. (VALUE_IS_OUT_OF_RANGE_OF_DATA_TYPE)
```

Reading the same Parquet file with `file()` returns both rows (`1969-12-31`, `2024-01-01`).

### Root cause

The Paimon type parser creates `DataTypeDate` for `DATE`: [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h:212-216`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Types.h#L212-L216). It should be `DataTypeDate32`. The partition value path already reads a `DATE` partition as a signed `getInt` ([`Paimon/Utils.cpp:223`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Utils.cpp#L223), [`:306`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Paimon/Utils.cpp#L306)), so it is compatible with `Date32`. The shared type matrix in [`tests/integration/helpers/paimon_utils.py:78`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/tests/integration/helpers/paimon_utils.py#L78) pins `Nullable(Date)` and would need to be updated together with the fix.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/119272

- Merged into: `26.11.1.1061-master` (included in `26.11` and later)

text:
Iceberg: cannot create a table with a `Bool` column (`Unsupported type for iceberg Bool`)

### What happens

`CREATE TABLE ... (b Bool) ENGINE = IcebergLocal(...)` (and `IcebergS3`) fails with `Unsupported type for iceberg Bool`, although Iceberg has a `boolean` primitive type and ClickHouse already maps Iceberg `boolean` to `Bool` when reading. ClickHouse can read and even `INSERT` into an existing Iceberg table with a `boolean` column written by another engine; it only refuses to create one (or to `ADD COLUMN` one). The same applies to `Nullable(Bool)`, to `Bool` nested in `Array`, and to `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN b Nullable(Bool)`.

The limitation is documented in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/integrations/iceberg.mdx#L112, but there is no format reason for it for `Bool`: it is the one ClickHouse type with an exact Iceberg counterpart that the writer does not map.

### How to reproduce

```bash
clickhouse local -q "CREATE TABLE t_bool (b Bool) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/tmp/ice_bool/')"
```

Reading and inserting into a `boolean` table written by PyIceberg works:

```bash
pip install 'pyiceberg[sql-sqlite]' pyarrow
mkdir -p /tmp/ice_wh
python3 -c "
import pyarrow as pa
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog
from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
from pyiceberg.types import NestedField, BooleanType, IntegerType
c = SqlCatalog('c', uri='sqlite:////tmp/ice_wh/cat.db', warehouse='file:///tmp/ice_wh')
c.create_namespace('db')
t = c.create_table('db.tbool', Schema(NestedField(1, 'id', IntegerType(), required=False), NestedField(2, 'b', BooleanType(), required=False)))
t.append(pa.table({'id': pa.array([1, 2, 3], pa.int32()), 'b': pa.array([True, False, None])}))"

clickhouse local -q "
SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1;
CREATE TABLE x ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/tmp/ice_wh/db/tbool');
INSERT INTO x VALUES (4, true);
SELECT * FROM x ORDER BY id;"
```

### Expected

The table is created with an Iceberg `boolean` column (`"type": "boolean"` in the schema).

### Actual

```
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unsupported type for iceberg Bool. (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
```

The PyIceberg table is described as `b Nullable(Bool)` and the `INSERT` works (`1 true / 2 false / 3 \N / 4 true`).

### Version

```
SELECT version()
26.11.1.941
```

Public master build `build_amd_release` at commit https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840

### Root cause

`getIcebergType` has no case for `Bool`. `Bool` is `TypeIndex::UInt8` with a custom name, and the switch has no `UInt8` case either, so it falls through to `default`:

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L773 (`getIcebergType`)
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L872 (`default: throw ... Unsupported type for iceberg`)

The reverse mapping exists: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/SchemaProcessor.cpp#L635 (`boolean` -> `Bool`).

A fix would map `UInt8` with the `Bool` custom name to `boolean`. The data path already works: PyIceberg reads back the row ClickHouse inserted into the `boolean` column above (`StaticTable.from_metadata` on the new `v2.metadata.json` returns `b = [True, False, None, True]`). If `Bool` gets min/max bounds in manifests, they need the Iceberg single-byte `boolean` encoding.

Related observation: `Int8`, `UInt8`, `Int16` and `UInt16` are refused for the same reason (`Unsupported type for iceberg Int8`). Iceberg has no 8/16-bit integers, but they could be widened to `int` as Spark does for `ByteType`/`ShortType`; that is a separate decision.

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295, gate `clickhouse_iceberg_bool`).

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295

ClickHouse can read and even `INSERT` into an existing Iceberg table with a `boolean` column written by another engine; it only refuses to create one (or to `ADD COLUMN` one). The same applies to `Nullable(Bool)`, to `Bool` nested in `Array`, and to `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN b Nullable(Bool)`.

The limitation is documented in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/integrations/iceberg.mdx#L112, but there is no format reason for it for `Bool`: it is the one ClickHouse type with an exact Iceberg counterpart that the writer does not map.

### How to reproduce

```bash
clickhouse local -q "CREATE TABLE t_bool (b Bool) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/tmp/ice_bool/')"
```

Reading and inserting into a `boolean` table written by PyIceberg works:

```bash
pip install 'pyiceberg[sql-sqlite]' pyarrow
mkdir -p /tmp/ice_wh
python3 -c "
import pyarrow as pa
from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog
from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
from pyiceberg.types import NestedField, BooleanType, IntegerType
c = SqlCatalog('c', uri='sqlite:////tmp/ice_wh/cat.db', warehouse='file:///tmp/ice_wh')
c.create_namespace('db')
t = c.create_table('db.tbool', Schema(NestedField(1, 'id', IntegerType(), required=False), NestedField(2, 'b', BooleanType(), required=False)))
t.append(pa.table({'id': pa.array([1, 2, 3], pa.int32()), 'b': pa.array([True, False, None])}))"

clickhouse local -q "
SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1;
CREATE TABLE x ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/tmp/ice_wh/db/tbool');
INSERT INTO x VALUES (4, true);
SELECT * FROM x ORDER BY id;"
```

### Expected

The table is created with an Iceberg `boolean` column (`"type": "boolean"` in the schema).

### Actual

```
Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unsupported type for iceberg Bool. (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
```

The PyIceberg table is described as `b Nullable(Bool)` and the `INSERT` works (`1 true / 2 false / 3 \N / 4 true`).

### Version

```
SELECT version()
26.11.1.941
```

Public master build `build_amd_release` at commit https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840

### Root cause

`getIcebergType` has no case for `Bool`. `Bool` is `TypeIndex::UInt8` with a custom name, and the switch has no `UInt8` case either, so it falls through to `default`:

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L773 (`getIcebergType`)
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L872 (`default: throw ... Unsupported type for iceberg`)

The reverse mapping exists: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/SchemaProcessor.cpp#L635 (`boolean` -> `Bool`).

A fix would map `UInt8` with the `Bool` custom name to `boolean`. The data path already works: PyIceberg reads back the row ClickHouse inserted into the `boolean` column above (`StaticTable.from_metadata` on the new `v2.metadata.json` returns `b = [True, False, None, True]`). If `Bool` gets min/max bounds in manifests, they need the Iceberg single-byte `boolean` encoding.

Related observation: `Int8`, `UInt8`, `Int16` and `UInt16` are refused for the same reason (`Unsupported type for iceberg Int8`). Iceberg has no 8/16-bit integers, but they could be widened to `int` as Spark does for `ByteType`/`ShortType`; that is a separate decision.

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295, gate `clickhouse_iceberg_bool`).

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295

Parquet: signed-order `UINT_64` / `UINT_32` statistics written by polars 0.20 fail the query with `min_value > max_value` instead of being ignored

**Describe what's wrong**

polars 0.20 writes the `min_value` / `max_value` statistics of unsigned integer columns (`UINT_32`, `UINT_64`) using signed comparison, while declaring `TYPE_ORDER` in `column_orders`. When a row group contains values both below and above `2^63` (or `2^31`), the unsigned interpretation of these statistics has `min_value > max_value`. ClickHouse then fails the whole query with `INCORRECT_DATA` instead of ignoring the unusable statistics. This affects any `WHERE` on the column and even a plain `SELECT max(u)`, while the data itself is read correctly.

**Does it reproduce on the most recent release?**

Yes, on master `26.11.1.941` (commit `a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840`).

**How to reproduce**

```python
# pip install polars==0.20.31
import polars as pl
pl.DataFrame({'u': pl.Series([1, 2**63], dtype=pl.UInt64)}).write_parquet('polars_u64.parquet')
```

The footer has `column_orders = [TYPE_ORDER]` and `Statistics(min_value = 0x0000000000000080 /* 2^63 */, max_value = 0x0100000000000000 /* 1 */)`.

```
$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('polars_u64.parquet')"
1
9223372036854775808

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('polars_u64.parquet') WHERE u > 1"
Code: 117. DB::Exception: Statistics have min_value > max_value: 9223372036854775808 > 1: in column chunk statistics for column 'u'; use input_format_parquet_filter_push_down=0 to ignore: ... (INCORRECT_DATA)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('polars_u64.parquet') WHERE u > 1 SETTINGS input_format_parquet_filter_push_down = 0"
Code: 117. DB::Exception: Statistics have min_value > max_value: 9223372036854775808 > 1: in column index; use input_format_parquet_page_filter_push_down=0 to ignore: ... (INCORRECT_DATA)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT max(u) FROM file('polars_u64.parquet')"
Code: 117. DB::Exception: Statistics have min_value > max_value: 9223372036854775808 > 1: in column chunk statistics for column 'u'; use optimize_min_max_from_files=0 to ignore: ... (INCORRECT_DATA)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('polars_u64.parquet') WHERE u > 1 SETTINGS input_format_parquet_filter_push_down = 0, input_format_parquet_page_filter_push_down = 0"
9223372036854775808
```

`UInt32` columns behave the same (`Statistics have min_value > max_value: 2147483648 > 1954088999`). pyarrow's dataset scanner returns the correct row for the same filter (`ds.dataset('polars_u64.parquet').to_table(filter=pc.field('u') > 1)`). Newer polars (2.x) writes correct unsigned statistics, but files written by polars 0.20 exist in data lakes.

**Expected behavior**

The statistics are ignored for pruning (and for `optimize_min_max_from_files`), and the queries return `9223372036854775808` and `max(u) = 9223372036854775808`.

Ignoring a `min_value > max_value` range is also enough to be safe against this particular writer bug: if all values of a row group (or page) share the top bit, signed and unsigned order agree and the statistics are correct; if they do not, the signed minimum has the top bit set and the signed maximum does not, so the unsigned range is always inverted and detectable. A signed-order range that is not inverted is therefore never wrong.

**Root cause (master `2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1`)**

`Reader::adjustRangeFromIndexIfNeeded` throws on an inverted range ([Reader.cpp#L2880-L2883](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L2880-L2883)). It is called for row group statistics in `getHyperrectangleForRowGroup` ([Reader.cpp#L501](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L501)), for the column index ([Reader.cpp#L2812](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L2812)) and for the top-K range ([Reader.cpp#L599](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L599)). `readMinMaxFromStatistics` has its own copy of the check ([Reader.cpp#L740-L741](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L740-L741)). The comment next to the top-K call says such statistics "must fail closed rather than become pruning input", but failing the query is stricter than needed: the same functions already fall back to "no statistics" (`Range::createWholeUniverse` or `std::nullopt`) when `decodeField` reports an unusable bound ([Reader.cpp#L493-L497](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L493-L497)), and an inverted range could be treated the same way.

**Additional context**

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103039
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/118110

text:
Iceberg format version 1 metadata written by ClickHouse lacks the required `schema` and `partition-spec` fields, PyIceberg cannot open the table

### What happens

ClickHouse writes Iceberg format version 1 metadata without the `schema` field, which format version 1 requires. PyIceberg (and any reader that follows the spec strictly) cannot open the table. This affects every metadata file ClickHouse writes for a v1 table, including the one written by `CREATE TABLE`, not only the one after the first `INSERT`.

The Iceberg spec ([Table Metadata Fields](https://iceberg.apache.org/spec/#table-metadata-fields)) marks these fields as required in v1 and optional in v2:

- `schema`: "The table's current schema. (Deprecated: use `schemas` and `current-schema-id` instead)". Missing from ClickHouse output.
- `partition-spec`: "The table's current partition spec, stored as only fields. Note that this is used by writers to partition data, but is not used when reading because reads use the specs stored in manifest files. (Deprecated: use `partition-specs` and `default-spec-id` instead)". Also missing from ClickHouse output.

ClickHouse writes only the v2 forms (`schemas` + `current-schema-id`, `partition-specs` + `default-spec-id`). The Java implementation writes both forms for v1 tables for this reason. PyIceberg needs only `schema`: after adding `schema` (a copy of `schemas[0]`) to the file by hand, PyIceberg opens the table and reads the row back correctly, so no other field blocks it.

### How to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/ice_v1
clickhouse local -q "
SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1;
CREATE TABLE t (id Int32, s String) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/tmp/ice_v1/') SETTINGS iceberg_format_version = 1;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a');
SELECT * FROM t;"

pip install pyiceberg pyarrow
python3 -c "
import glob
from pyiceberg.table import StaticTable
StaticTable.from_metadata(sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/ice_v1/metadata/*.metadata.json'))[-1])"
```

### Expected

PyIceberg loads the table (and `scan().to_arrow()` returns the row `1, 'a'`). Both `v1.metadata.json` and `v2.metadata.json` contain `schema` and `partition-spec`.

### Actual

ClickHouse reads its own table back (`1 a`), but PyIceberg fails on both `v1.metadata.json` and `v2.metadata.json`:

```
pyiceberg.exceptions.ValidationError: 1 validation error for TableMetadataWrapper
1.schema
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'current-schema-id': 0, ...}, input_type=dict]
```

Checked with PyIceberg 0.12.0.

### Version

```
SELECT version()
26.11.1.941
```

Public master build `build_amd_release` at commit https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840

### Root cause

`createEmptyMetadataFile` writes `schemas` and `partition-specs` and never the v1 fields `schema` and `partition-spec`, whatever `format_version` is:

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L1294 (`schemas`)
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Utils.cpp#L1303 (`partition-specs`)

Every later metadata file is a modified copy of the previous one (`MetadataGenerator`), so the fields never appear. A fix also has to keep `schema` in sync with the current schema in the schema-evolution paths of `MetadataGenerator.cpp` (they add to `schemas` and update `current-schema-id`, e.g. https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/MetadataGenerator.cpp#L482), and `partition-spec` in sync with the default spec.

### Other v1 spec deviations seen in the same files

- The first snapshot carries `"parent-snapshot-id": -1`, and `metadata-log` lists the file it is in instead of the previous file. Both are already addressed by the open PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125409 (for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/118812). Neither blocks PyIceberg.
- `last-partition-id` is 999 for an unpartitioned table, which matches the Java convention (`PARTITION_DATA_ID_START - 1`), so it is fine.

Found by the foreign-writer differential fuzzer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295, gate `clickhouse_iceberg_v1_metadata`).

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125409
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127437
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128295

text:
Parquet: empty data pages that Arrow C++ writes in repeated columns fail with `Invalid offset index` or `ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF`, and `datapage_v2_empty_datapage.snappy.parquet` fails with `CANNOT_DECOMPRESS`

**Describe what's wrong**

Arrow C++ (pyarrow) writes an empty data page (`num_values = 0`, and `num_rows = 0` for `DataPageV2`) in the middle of a repeated column chunk when pages are tiny. pyarrow reads such files back correctly, but ClickHouse fails on them in two different ways:

1. With the page index (offset index) present, any read of the column fails with `INCORRECT_DATA: Invalid offset index`, because the empty page and the next page have the same `first_row_index`. This happens for both `DataPage` v1 and v2.
2. With `DataPageV2` and no offset index (or `input_format_parquet_use_offset_index = 0`), the read fails with `ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF`. The same file with `DataPage` v1 reads correctly.

Generate the files with pyarrow (tested with pyarrow 26.0.0):

```python
import pyarrow as pa, pyarrow.parquet as pq

        path = f'empty_page_v{version[0]}_{"index" if page_index else "noindex"}.parquet'
        pq.write_table(t, path, data_page_version=version, data_page_size=1, write_batch_size=1, write_page_index=page_index)

```
```
offset=4   DICTIONARY_PAGE num_values=3
offset=32  DATA_PAGE_V2 num_values=1 num_rows=1
offset=61  DATA_PAGE_V2 num_values=1 num_rows=1
offset=90  DATA_PAGE_V2 num_values=0 num_rows=0 def_len=0 rep_len=0 uncompressed=1
offset=113 DATA_PAGE_V2 num_values=1 num_rows=1
```

```

Code: 117. DB::Exception: Invalid offset index: PageLocation(offset=128, compressed_page_size=34, first_row_index=2), prev offset: 128, prev row: 2, end offset: 162, num rows: 3: read stage: OffsetIndex: column: x: ... (INCORRECT_DATA)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('empty_page_v2_index.parquet')"
Code: 117. DB::Exception: Invalid offset index: PageLocation(offset=113, compressed_page_size=29, first_row_index=2), prev offset: 113, prev row: 2, end offset: 142, num rows: 3: read stage: OffsetIndex: column: x: ... (INCORRECT_DATA)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('empty_page_v2_noindex.parquet')"
Code: 32. DB::Exception: Attempt to read after eof: read stage: ColumnData: column: x: ... (ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('empty_page_v2_index.parquet') SETTINGS input_format_parquet_use_offset_index = 0"
Code: 32. DB::Exception: Attempt to read after eof: ... (ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF)

$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('empty_page_v1_noindex.parquet')"
[1]
[2]
[3]
```

```
$ curl -sSfLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/parquet-testing/56653c437c8092f704a092d0d1d4e600124cd49f/data/datapage_v2_empty_datapage.snappy.parquet
$ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM file('datapage_v2_empty_datapage.snappy.parquet')"
Code: 271. DB::Exception: Malformed snappy compressed page (couldn't get uncompressed length): read stage: ColumnData: column: value: ... (CANNOT_DECOMPRESS)
```

All files read like pyarrow does: `[1] [2] [3]` and `NULL`.

**Root cause (master `2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1`)**

1. `Reader::decodeOffsetIndex` requires a strictly increasing `first_row_index` ([Reader.cpp#L3145-L3153](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L3145-L3153), `loc.first_row_index <= prev_row_index`). `parquet.thrift` does say that `page_locations[i].first_row_index < page_locations[i+1].first_row_index` is required, so Arrow's file violates the spec, but Arrow C++ is the most common writer and its own reader accepts the file. Accepting equal `first_row_index` (treating the earlier page as zero rows, which the page header confirms for v2) would make these files readable.
2. On the sequential path, `Reader::skipToRowOrNextPage` calls `initializeDataPage` for the next page and returns immediately when `row_idx` is not set ([Reader.cpp#L3594-L3603](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L3594-L3603)), ignoring its `false` result. The page loop then calls `readRowsInPage` on the uninitialized page, whose `num_values` is still that of the previous page (`initializeDataPage` does not reset it), so the value decoder most likely runs past the 1-byte empty page. `readRowsInPage` asserts `page.initialized` ([Reader.cpp#L4154](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L4154)), so a debug build would likely abort here instead of throwing. A v1 page has no row count for repeated columns, so it is initialized with `num_values = 0` and works by accident.
3. `Reader::decompressPageIfCompressed` ([Reader.cpp#L4333-L4341](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L4333-L4341)) passes the 0-byte values section to `decompress`, and `snappy::GetUncompressedLength` rejects an empty input ([Reader.cpp#L225-L226](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/Parquet/Reader.cpp#L225-L226)). A `DataPageV2` whose values section is empty (`uncompressed_page_size` equal to the level lengths) has nothing to decompress; pyarrow reads this file.

**Additional context**

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114464
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114530
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125130

`INSERT INTO <Distributed with sharding key> SELECT FROM s3Cluster(...)` still writes type defaults instead of `DEFAULT` expressions

### Describe what's wrong

`INSERT INTO <Distributed table> SELECT * FROM s3Cluster(...)` writes the default values of the column types (`0`, `''`, `1970-01-01`) instead of the `DEFAULT` expressions of the destination table for fields missing in the source files, when the `Distributed` table has a deterministic sharding key (for example `id`) and `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 2` (the default). No error is raised. When a TTL depends on such a column, the rows expire right after insertion.

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657 fixed this for a replicated destination and for a `Distributed` destination sharded by `rand()`, but a deterministic sharding key makes `StorageDistributed::distributedWriteFromClusterStorage` fall back to the ordinary `INSERT SELECT` (added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/121070), and the ordinary path loses the `DEFAULT`s the same way as `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0`.

Results with two files, one with only `id` (rows 1 and 3) and one with all fields (row 2), destination `(id UInt32, d Date DEFAULT '2000-01-01', q UInt32 DEFAULT 7)`:

| destination | `parallel_distributed_insert_select` | path | rows 1 and 3 | correct |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 0 | ordinary `INSERT SELECT`, only the `SELECT` is distributed | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 1 | forwarded `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each shard | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 2 | forwarded `INSERT` into the local table on each shard | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 0 | ordinary | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 1 | forwarded `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 2 | falls back to ordinary (server log: `Parallel distributed INSERT SELECT into default.dist_id ... is not possible: the rows read from S3 cannot satisfy its deterministic sharding key (id); falling back to the ordinary INSERT SELECT`) | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | default (2), plain `s3(...)` instead of `s3Cluster` | ordinary, non-distributed read | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |

So the affected cases are every `INSERT ... SELECT FROM s3Cluster(...)` (and other object storage `*Cluster` functions, presumably also `s3` auto-converted by `parallel_replicas_for_cluster_engines`) that runs through the ordinary `INSERT SELECT` path: `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0` for any destination, and `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 2` into a `Distributed` table with a deterministic sharding key. With the default settings, the latter is what a user writing into a sharded `Distributed` table gets.

This is the same incident pattern as the one fixed by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657 (object storage ingestion writing zero and epoch values, then TTL deleting the rows).

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes, on master: `26.11.1.941`, commit https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840, which includes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657.

### How to reproduce

A server with MinIO at `127.0.0.1:19100` (bucket `test`, user `minio`/`minio123`) and a cluster of two localhost shards:

```xml
<clickhouse>
    <listen_host>127.0.0.1</listen_host>
    <listen_host>127.0.0.2</listen_host>
    <remote_servers>
        <two_shards>
            <shard><replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard>
            <shard><replica><host>127.0.0.2</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard>
        </two_shards>
    </remote_servers>
</clickhouse>
```

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_1.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow', 'id UInt32') VALUES (1), (3);
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_2.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow', 'id UInt32, d Date, q UInt32') VALUES (2, '2001-02-03', 5);

CREATE TABLE local_b2 (id UInt32, d Date DEFAULT '2000-01-01', q UInt32 DEFAULT 7) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE dist_id AS local_b2 ENGINE = Distributed(two_shards, default, local_b2, id);

INSERT INTO dist_id SELECT * FROM s3Cluster('two_shards', 'http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_{1,2}.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow')
SETTINGS distributed_foreground_insert = 1;

SELECT * FROM local_b2 ORDER BY id;
```

Actual:

```
1	1970-01-01	0
2	2001-02-03	5
3	1970-01-01	0
```

Expected (what the same query with `s3(...)` instead of `s3Cluster(...)`, or with `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1`, produces):

```
1	2000-01-01	7
2	2001-02-03	5
3	2000-01-01	7
```

The same wrong result with `SETTINGS parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0` into any destination, including `Distributed(..., rand())`.

### Root cause (public master 2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1)

- `InterpreterInsertQuery::execute` tries `IStorage::distributedWrite` and then the replicated / data lake path only when `parallel_distributed_insert_select != 0` ([`src/Interpreters/InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1579-1593`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Interpreters/InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp#L1579-L1593)); otherwise it builds the ordinary `INSERT SELECT` pipeline.
- `StorageDistributed::distributedWriteFromClusterStorage` returns `{}` for `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 2` and a deterministic sharding key ([`src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp:1571-1584`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp#L1571-L1584)), so the query takes the ordinary path. The fallback itself is right (the files are distributed by path hash, not by the key), but it does not fall back to the `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1` style (forward the `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each node, which keeps the `DEFAULT`s and respects the key), it goes all the way to the ordinary path.
- In the ordinary path the initiator reads `s3Cluster` through `IStorageCluster::read`, which calls `updateQueryToSendIfNeeded(..., /*add_structure_and_format=*/true)` ([`src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp:121`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp#L121)). `StorageObjectStorageCluster::updateQueryToSendIfNeeded` adds `storage_snapshot->metadata->getColumns().getAll().toNamesAndTypesDescription()` as the structure of the forwarded `SELECT` ([`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageCluster.cpp:426`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageCluster.cpp#L426), used at lines 450 and 477). On the initiator, that metadata was taken from the insertion table (`use_structure_from_insertion_table_in_table_functions`) and has the `DEFAULT` expressions, but the structure string has names and types only. Each worker parses `JSONEachRow` with that structure and fills the missing fields with type defaults, and the initiator receives complete rows, so the `INSERT` into the destination never sees the fields as omitted and does not evaluate the `DEFAULT`s.

Possible fixes: make the deterministic-sharding-key fallback forward the `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each node (the `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1` behavior, which already produces correct results); and for the ordinary path, send the `DEFAULT` expressions to the workers (or let them evaluate the defaults of the insertion table), or keep the omitted-field information so that the initiator applies the `DEFAULT`s.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/121070
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/120488

| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 0 | ordinary `INSERT SELECT`, only the `SELECT` is distributed | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 1 | forwarded `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each shard | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., rand())` | 2 | forwarded `INSERT` into the local table on each shard | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 0 | ordinary | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 1 | forwarded `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | 2 | falls back to ordinary (server log: `Parallel distributed INSERT SELECT into default.dist_id ... is not possible: the rows read from S3 cannot satisfy its deterministic sharding key (id); falling back to the ordinary INSERT SELECT`) | `('1970-01-01', 0)` | no |
| `Distributed(..., id)` | default (2), plain `s3(...)` instead of `s3Cluster` | ordinary, non-distributed read | `('2000-01-01', 7)` | yes |

So the affected cases are every `INSERT ... SELECT FROM s3Cluster(...)` (and other object storage `*Cluster` functions, presumably also `s3` auto-converted by `parallel_replicas_for_cluster_engines`) that runs through the ordinary `INSERT SELECT` path: `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0` for any destination, and `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 2` into a `Distributed` table with a deterministic sharding key. With the default settings, the latter is what a user writing into a sharded `Distributed` table gets.

This is the same incident pattern as the one fixed by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657 (object storage ingestion writing zero and epoch values, then TTL deleting the rows).

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes, on master: `26.11.1.941`, commit https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/a018bd2bbaa600293f77e00e75adfa519d74f840, which includes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657.

### How to reproduce

A server with MinIO at `127.0.0.1:19100` (bucket `test`, user `minio`/`minio123`) and a cluster of two localhost shards:

```xml
<clickhouse>
    <listen_host>127.0.0.1</listen_host>
    <listen_host>127.0.0.2</listen_host>
    <remote_servers>
        <two_shards>
            <shard><replica><host>127.0.0.1</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard>
            <shard><replica><host>127.0.0.2</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard>
        </two_shards>
    </remote_servers>
</clickhouse>
```

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_1.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow', 'id UInt32') VALUES (1), (3);
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_2.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow', 'id UInt32, d Date, q UInt32') VALUES (2, '2001-02-03', 5);

CREATE TABLE local_b2 (id UInt32, d Date DEFAULT '2000-01-01', q UInt32 DEFAULT 7) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE dist_id AS local_b2 ENGINE = Distributed(two_shards, default, local_b2, id);

INSERT INTO dist_id SELECT * FROM s3Cluster('two_shards', 'http://127.0.0.1:19100/test/b2/part_{1,2}.jsonl', 'minio', 'minio123', 'JSONEachRow')
SETTINGS distributed_foreground_insert = 1;

SELECT * FROM local_b2 ORDER BY id;
```

Actual:

```
1	1970-01-01	0
2	2001-02-03	5
3	1970-01-01	0
```

Expected (what the same query with `s3(...)` instead of `s3Cluster(...)`, or with `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1`, produces):

```
1	2000-01-01	7
2	2001-02-03	5
3	2000-01-01	7
```

The same wrong result with `SETTINGS parallel_distributed_insert_select = 0` into any destination, including `Distributed(..., rand())`.

### Root cause (public master 2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1)

- `InterpreterInsertQuery::execute` tries `IStorage::distributedWrite` and then the replicated / data lake path only when `parallel_distributed_insert_select != 0` ([`src/Interpreters/InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1579-1593`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Interpreters/InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp#L1579-L1593)); otherwise it builds the ordinary `INSERT SELECT` pipeline.
- `StorageDistributed::distributedWriteFromClusterStorage` returns `{}` for `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 2` and a deterministic sharding key ([`src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp:1571-1584`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/StorageDistributed.cpp#L1571-L1584)), so the query takes the ordinary path. The fallback itself is right (the files are distributed by path hash, not by the key), but it does not fall back to the `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1` style (forward the `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each node, which keeps the `DEFAULT`s and respects the key), it goes all the way to the ordinary path.
- In the ordinary path the initiator reads `s3Cluster` through `IStorageCluster::read`, which calls `updateQueryToSendIfNeeded(..., /*add_structure_and_format=*/true)` ([`src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp:121`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/IStorageCluster.cpp#L121)). `StorageObjectStorageCluster::updateQueryToSendIfNeeded` adds `storage_snapshot->metadata->getColumns().getAll().toNamesAndTypesDescription()` as the structure of the forwarded `SELECT` ([`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageCluster.cpp:426`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2eafca8a6ccef2f47d1bbcaf1281940e4ead37a1/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageCluster.cpp#L426), used at lines 450 and 477). On the initiator, that metadata was taken from the insertion table (`use_structure_from_insertion_table_in_table_functions`) and has the `DEFAULT` expressions, but the structure string has names and types only. Each worker parses `JSONEachRow` with that structure and fills the missing fields with type defaults, and the initiator receives complete rows, so the `INSERT` into the destination never sees the fields as omitted and does not evaluate the `DEFAULT`s.

Possible fixes: make the deterministic-sharding-key fallback forward the `INSERT` into the `Distributed` table on each node (the `parallel_distributed_insert_select = 1` behavior, which already produces correct results); and for the ordinary path, send the `DEFAULT` expressions to the workers (or let them evaluate the defaults of the insertion table), or keep the omitted-field information so that the initiator applies the `DEFAULT`s.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127657
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/121070
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/120488

text:
INSERT … SELECT retry loses rows after OPTIMIZE FINAL rewrites an unchanged source, despite identical deduplication token and settings

### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe the unexpected behaviour

Retrying an interrupted INSERT … SELECT with identical SQL, settings, and insert_deduplication_token silently loses rows if OPTIMIZE TABLE Source FINAL rewrites the source between attempts.

The optimization preserves all 100,000 source rows and their value fingerprint, but changes granule boundaries and the resulting copy-block boundaries.

Measured copy-block ranges:

Block 28:
  Before optimization: IDs 45155–46820 (1,666 rows)
  After optimization:  IDs 45164–46830 (1,667 rows)

Block 29:
  Before optimization: IDs 46821–48486
  After optimization:  IDs 46831–48496

The first attempt commits blocks 1–28, covering IDs 0–46820, before failing.

On retry, blocks 1–28 cover IDs 0–46830, but receive the same deduplication identities. ClickHouse skips them as duplicates. The first newly committed block starts at ID 46831.

The retry reports success, but Target contains only 99,990 rows. IDs 46821–46830 are missing. No duplicate IDs are present.

Trace logs confirm that block 28, internally source-number-27, retains identical deduplication IDs despite changing from 1,666 to 1,667 rows. The retry logs:

“All rows are deduplicated ... skipping the part commit.”

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?

Reproduced repeatedly on 26.3.16.10001.altinitystable.

Other versions, including upstream ClickHouse builds, have not been tested.

### How to reproduce

The attached SQL script contains the complete reproduction, including every copy setting. Execute it section by section because the first copy deliberately throws an exception.

1. Create Source:

```sql
CREATE TABLE Source
(
    Id UInt64,
    Version UInt64,
    Payload String
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY Id
SETTINGS index_granularity_bytes = 262144;
```

2. Create Target with a constraint that interrupts the first copy:

```sql
CREATE TABLE Target
(
    Id UInt64,
    Version UInt64,
    Payload String,
    CONSTRAINT interrupt_copy CHECK Id < 50000
)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY Id
SETTINGS non_replicated_deduplication_window = 10000;
```

3. Populate Source with 100,000 rows in four separate batches. Execute this statement with offsets 0, 25000, 50000, and 75000:

```sql
INSERT INTO Source
SELECT
    number % 100000 AS Id,
    intDiv(number, 100000) + 1 AS Version,
    concat(
        toString(Id), ':', toString(Version), ':',
        repeat('x', 32 + cityHash64(Id) % 512)
    ) AS Payload
FROM numbers(0, 25000)
SETTINGS async_insert = 0;
```

4. Finalize Source:

```sql
OPTIMIZE TABLE Source FINAL
SETTINGS
    alter_sync = 2,
    optimize_skip_merged_partitions = 0,
    optimize_throw_if_noop = 1;
```

5. Execute the INSERT … SELECT from the attached reproduction script.

Both copy attempts use identical SQL and settings, including:

```sql
async_insert = 0,
deduplicate_insert = 'enable',
deduplicate_insert_select = 'force_enable',
max_threads = 1,
max_block_size = 1000,
min_insert_block_size_rows = 0,
min_insert_block_size_bytes = 0,
optimize_read_in_order = 1,
insert_deduplication_token = 'optimize-replay:partition:all'
```

The query copies Id, Version, and Payload from Source into Target, filtering _partition_id = 'all' and using ORDER BY ALL.

The first attempt throws the constraint exception after committing 46,821 rows, IDs 0–46820.

6. Execute the same OPTIMIZE TABLE Source FINAL again.

The active source part changes from all_1_4_1 to all_1_4_2. The source row count and value fingerprint remain unchanged.

7. Remove the constraint:

```sql
ALTER TABLE Target DROP CONSTRAINT interrupt_copy
SETTINGS alter_sync = 2;
```

8. Retry the identical copy statement, including the same token and settings.

9. Check Target:

```sql
SELECT count(), uniqExact(Id) FROM Target;
-- 99990, 99990

SELECT Id
FROM
(
    SELECT Id FROM Source
    EXCEPT ALL
    SELECT Id FROM Target
)
ORDER BY Id;
-- IDs 46821 through 46830 are missing.
```

Control experiment: omitting only the second optimization produces 100,000 destination rows, zero missing rows, and zero duplicates.

### Expected behavior

The retry should copy all 100,000 source rows exactly once, or explicitly report that safe retry deduplication cannot be guaranteed.

It should not report success while silently omitting rows that were never committed.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

_No response_

### Related issues and pull requests

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

text:
Iceberg `OPTIMIZE` sums all live files into `added-records`: `count()` inflated

### Describe what's wrong

- After `OPTIMIZE` on an Iceberg table, trivial `count()` returns more rows than a full scan.
- Trigger: two consecutive appends plus a position delete, e.g. INSERT 2 rows, INSERT 1 row, DELETE 1 row, then `OPTIMIZE`.
- Trivial `count()` should return 2 but returns 3, while the full scan correctly returns 2.
- The wrong `total-records` is persisted in metadata, so `system.tables.total_rows` and every later trivial count stay wrong until the next rewrite.

Root cause: In Compaction.cpp:1117-1126 `writeMetadataFiles` sums `new_records_count` over every live file of the snapshot (`snapshot_id_to_data_files`) and passes it as `added_records`. `setSnapshotTotals` (MetadataGenerator.cpp:91) then adds it to the rewritten parent's `total-records`, so totals accumulate (1 + 2 = 3).

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `IcebergMetadata::optimize` (IcebergMetadata.cpp:622) -> `compactIcebergTable` -> `writeMetadataFiles` (Compaction.cpp:1117-1126) -> `MetadataGenerator::generateNextMetadata` -> `setSnapshotTotals` (MetadataGenerator.cpp:91,100). The trivial count reads `total-records` back in `IcebergMetadata::totalRows` (IcebergMetadata.cpp:1751).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp:1117`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2a49505f2c31cc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp#L1117) — `total_records_count` = rows of every live file of the snapshot, not the rows it added
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp:1126`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2a49505f2c31cc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp#L1126) — passed as `added_records` to `generateNextMetadata`
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp:297`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2a49505f2c31cc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/Compaction.cpp#L297) — `snapshot_id_to_data_files` collects every file listed by the snapshot's manifests
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/MetadataGenerator.cpp:91`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/2a49505f2c31cc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/DataLakes/Iceberg/MetadataGenerator.cpp#L91) — `total-records` = parent total + `added_records`

Impact: Silent wrong `count()` on an Iceberg table after `OPTIMIZE` (`allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction = 1`, open-source builds). Any history with two consecutive append snapshots and at least one position delete hits it: with N appends the reported total is the sum of all prefix totals. `added-records`/`total-records` in the snapshot summaries are wrong for every reader of the metadata.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master` (`dcccc2b5920c`); not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Requires `allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1`, `mutations_sync = 2` and `allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction = 1`; if the parent snapshot is delete-only the bug does not show.

```bash
# - no-fasttest: requires `IcebergLocal` (USE_AVRO build option)

# Trivial count() must match a full scan after OPTIMIZE of a table with two consecutive appends and a DELETE.

TABLE="t_default_${RANDOM}"
TABLE_PATH="/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/${TABLE}/"

trap 'rm -rf "${TABLE_PATH}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT

clickhouse-client --query "CREATE TABLE ${TABLE} (x Int64) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('${TABLE_PATH}', 'Parquet')"
clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --query "INSERT INTO ${TABLE} VALUES (1), (2)"
clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --query "INSERT INTO ${TABLE} VALUES (3)"
clickhouse-client --allow_insert_into_iceberg=1 --mutations_sync=2 --query "ALTER TABLE ${TABLE} DELETE WHERE x = 1"
clickhouse-client --allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction=1 --query "OPTIMIZE TABLE ${TABLE}"

clickhouse-client --query "SELECT count() FROM ${TABLE} SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 1"
clickhouse-client --query "SELECT count() FROM ${TABLE} SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0"

clickhouse-client --query "DROP TABLE ${TABLE} SYNC"
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`dcccc2b5920c`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

Trivial `count()` after `OPTIMIZE` returns 2, matching the full scan.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2
2
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

Trivial `count()` returns 3 because the snapshot's `total-records` counts the parent's rows twice.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`dcccc2b5920c`):

```
3
2
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Pass a real delta: the rows of the files the snapshot added (files not present in its parent), or `total(snapshot) - total(rewritten parent)`. Make the accumulator 64-bit while there: `Int32 total_records_count` truncates once a snapshot holds more than 2^31 rows.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- `Int32 total_records_count` (Compaction.cpp:1117) also truncates the per-snapshot sum of `UInt64` row counts past 2^31 rows, same lines.
- Not introduced by #116941: the same summation and parent accumulation are in v26.3.9.8-lts and v26.8.9.10-lts. #116941 only lets `OPTIMIZE` through on more tables; its own new mixed-format test has the append, append, delete shape and checks rows with a full scan, so it does not see the wrong count.
- A test merged into the suite needs the `IS_CLOUD` handling used by `04513`/`04815`: on the Cloud build `OPTIMIZE` does not run this code and reports an exception instead.

Found during automated review of [PR #116941](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116941); the bug predates that PR (it reproduces on the master build just before it merged), so the introducing change is not identified yet. Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr116941_001`
