Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`dcccc2b5920c`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

Trivial `count()` after `OPTIMIZE` returns 2, matching the full scan.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
2
2
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

Trivial `count()` returns 3 because the snapshot's `total-records` counts the parent's rows twice.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`dcccc2b5920c`):

```
3
2
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Pass a real delta: the rows of the files the snapshot added (files not present in its parent), or `total(snapshot) - total(rewritten parent)`. Make the accumulator 64-bit while there: `Int32 total_records_count` truncates once a snapshot holds more than 2^31 rows.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- `Int32 total_records_count` (Compaction.cpp:1117) also truncates the per-snapshot sum of `UInt64` row counts past 2^31 rows, same lines.
- Not introduced by #116941: the same summation and parent accumulation are in v26.3.9.8-lts and v26.8.9.10-lts. #116941 only lets `OPTIMIZE` through on more tables; its own new mixed-format test has the append, append, delete shape and checks rows with a full scan, so it does not see the wrong count.
- A test merged into the suite needs the `IS_CLOUD` handling used by `04513`/`04815`: on the Cloud build `OPTIMIZE` does not run this code and reports an exception instead.

Found during automated review of [PR #116941](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/116941); the bug predates that PR (it reproduces on the master build just before it merged), so the introducing change is not identified yet. Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr116941_001`

text:
Full-sort guard misses UNION ALL/ARRAY JOIN/JOIN, causing 7-24% slowdown

### Describe what's wrong

- A small MergeTree read feeding an unbounded ORDER BY through UNION ALL, ARRAY JOIN or a JOIN probe side gets spread over more streams.
- Trigger: ORDER BY with no LIMIT where the read reaches the sort through one of these steps instead of directly.
- Expected is the read keeps its default stream count like a direct sort.
- Actual is extra streams feed a single-thread final merge, 7-24% slower; results stay correct; master only, introduced by #128178, unreleased.

Root cause: The walker in disableSpreadingSmallReadUnderFullSorting (optimizeReadInOrder.cpp:2042) only treats ExpressionStep/FilterStep as transparent, so it stops at UnionStep, ArrayJoinStep or JoinStep and leaves allow_spreading_small_read true, letting spreadMarkRangesAmongStreams raise num_streams.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `optimizeTreeSecondPass` (optimizeTree.cpp:1001) -> `disableSpreadingSmallReadUnderFullSorting` (optimizeReadInOrder.cpp:2034) walks down from the `SortingStep` only through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` (2042-2044). `UnionStep`, `ArrayJoinStep` and `JoinStep` end the walk, `allow_spreading_small_read` stays `true`, and `spreadMarkRangesAmongStreams` (ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:2000-2016) raises `num_streams`.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeReadInOrder.cpp:2042`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/f6573305cb0198/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeReadInOrder.cpp#L2042) — walker passes only ExpressionStep/FilterStep
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:2000`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/f6573305cb0198/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp#L2000) — spreading branch gated by allow_spreading_small_read
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/Optimizations.h:323`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/f6573305cb0198/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/Optimizations.h#L323) — guard contract: a small read below a full sort keeps its default stream count

Impact: Unbounded `ORDER BY` over `UNION ALL` of small `MergeTree` reads, over `ARRAY JOIN`, or over a `JOIN` probe side, on reads below about `max_threads` x 24 marks with `max_threads` 3..16, runs 7-24% slower than before #128178. This is the regression the guard was added to prevent (PR description: `sort_low_cardinality` was 17% slower). Results are correct; master only.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

No — only `master` (`509fb3681976`). The bug starts with #128178 (merged as `f1737bc6d5be`), which is in no release yet, so a release build (and ClickHouse Fiddle) still passes.

### How to reproduce

Use the EXPLAIN PIPELINE counts of MergeTreeSelect streams (3 vs 4 at max_threads=4) in 05457_merge_tree_small_read_streams.sql to see the regression.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/e599eb0d-5019-45fc-800e-e8f8481f2913)

```sql
-- Test: a small read that reaches a full sort without LIMIT through UNION ALL or ARRAY JOIN keeps its default stream count.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_small_read_sort;
CREATE TABLE t_small_read_sort (p UInt8, k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY p ORDER BY k
SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192, index_granularity_bytes = '10Mi';
INSERT INTO t_small_read_sort SELECT 0, number FROM numbers(26 * 8192);
INSERT INTO t_small_read_sort SELECT 1, number FROM numbers(26 * 8192);
OPTIMIZE TABLE t_small_read_sort FINAL;

SET max_threads = 4, max_threads_min_free_memory_per_thread = 0;
SET merge_tree_read_split_ranges_into_intersecting_and_non_intersecting_injection_probability = 0;
SET use_columns_cache = 0, enable_parallel_replicas = 0;

SELECT 'direct', trimBoth(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT k FROM t_small_read_sort ORDER BY k % 7) WHERE explain ILIKE '%MergeTreeSelect%';
SELECT 'union_all', trimBoth(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT k FROM (SELECT k FROM t_small_read_sort UNION ALL SELECT k FROM t_small_read_sort) ORDER BY k % 7) WHERE explain ILIKE '%MergeTreeSelect%';
SELECT 'array_join', trimBoth(explain) FROM (EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT k, x FROM t_small_read_sort ARRAY JOIN [1, 2] AS x ORDER BY k % 7) WHERE explain ILIKE '%MergeTreeSelect%';

DROP TABLE t_small_read_sort;
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`509fb3681976`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

A small read below a full ORDER BY without LIMIT keeps its default stream count regardless of intervening UNION ALL, ARRAY JOIN, or JOIN steps.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
direct	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 3 0 → 1
union_all	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 3 0 → 1
union_all	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 3 0 → 1
array_join	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 3 0 → 1
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The guard only recognizes ExpressionStep/FilterStep as pass-through, so reads behind UNION ALL, ARRAY JOIN or a JOIN probe side still get spread across more streams, slowing those queries 7-24%.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`509fb3681976`):

```
direct	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 3 0 → 1
union_all	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 4 0 → 1
union_all	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 4 0 → 1
array_join	MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPool, algorithm: Thread) × 4 0 → 1
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Let the walker pass every step that keeps its input streams unmerged: `ArrayJoinStep`, each child of a `UnionStep`, and the left (probe) input of `JoinStep`. Trade-off: for `JOIN` the probe side loses read parallelism; the measured net effect of spreading there is still negative (+7-15%). Put the `UNION ALL`/`ARRAY JOIN` cases into `05457_merge_tree_small_read_streams.sql` next to the existing direct-sort case rather than a new file.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- A full sort whose `LIMIT` is at least the data size also spreads, because the guard tests `getLimit() != 0`: `ORDER BY lc_col, uint_col LIMIT 100000000` on 2M rows went 378 -> 414 ms (+9.5%, n=25) at `max_threads = 16`. Same mechanism, different predicate; the suggested fix does not cover it.
- Other stream-preserving parents (e.g. `ReadFromMerge` for `Merge` tables) were not checked.

Introduced by [PR #128178](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128178), found during its automated review: the reproducer passes on the master build just before it merged and fails on the build with it. Severity P3 · Finding `h_pr128178_001`

cc @groeneai @alexey-milovidov (from #128178)


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Resolved by: #128284
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1024-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

text:
Array-join filter ignored in join estimate, wrong side picked for hash build

### Describe what's wrong

- A filter on array-joined elements is dropped when estimating row counts for join reordering.
- Triggered by joining a table to an `ARRAY JOIN`/`arrayJoin` subquery that filters elements, subquery on the right.
- The estimator reports input x 100 as a known row count instead of marking it unknown.
- Causes the hash join to build from the much larger table, with ~21x peak memory and ~9x time.

Root cause: In `RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375` the array-join branch passes `nullptr` instead of `filter` and ignores `ArrayJoinStep::hasElementFilter`, so it returns the unfiltered `input x 100` as a known estimate at :377, which `swap_on_sizes` in `optimizeJoin.cpp:1269` uses to flip the join order.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `addChildQueryGraph` (optimizeJoin.cpp:650) → `estimateReadRowsCount` → the new array-join branch at RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375 calls the child with `nullptr` instead of `filter` and never checks `ArrayJoinStep::hasElementFilter` (ArrayJoinStep.h:46; `tryFuseFilterIntoArrayJoin` fuses element-only filters by default, fuseFilterIntoArrayJoin.cpp:82), then returns `input x 100` at :377 as a known estimate → `swap_on_sizes` (optimizeJoin.cpp:1269-1272) sees `lhs < rhs` and flips the join.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp#L375) — array-join branch passes nullptr instead of `filter`; element filter of `ArrayJoinStep` not consulted
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:377`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp#L377) — unfiltered input estimate multiplied by `array_join_rows_multiplier` and returned as known
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeJoin.cpp:1269`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeJoin.cpp#L1269) — `swap_on_sizes` swaps the hash join when both estimates are known and lhs < rhs
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ArrayJoinStep.h:46`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ArrayJoinStep.h#L46) — `hasElementFilter` exists but the estimator ignores it

Impact: A table joined to an `ARRAY JOIN`/`arrayJoin` subquery that filters the elements, with the subquery on the right, now builds the hash table from the left table whenever left rows < 100x the subquery's input rows. Repro: 5,000,000 vs 11 build rows, 21x peak memory, ~9x time, on every run. Results are correct. Master only (not in 26.10).

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

No — only `master` (`4e3df38e874c`). The bug starts with #126491 (merged as `4e3df38e874c`), which is in no release yet, so a release build (and ClickHouse Fiddle) still passes.

### How to reproduce

Reproduces reliably with `big` (5M rows) joined to a filtered `ARRAY JOIN` subquery over `events` (100k rows, 11 output rows); results stay correct, only performance and memory regress.

[▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/9834a71d-e876-447d-bfed-54e31cf27940)

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```sql
-- Random settings limits: query_plan_optimize_join_order_randomize=(0, 0); query_plan_optimize_join_order_limit=(1, None)

-- A hash join compares the sides by their row estimates, and an array join input is estimated
-- as 100 rows per row of its input.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_l;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_s;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_r;
SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0, join_algorithm = 'hash', query_plan_join_swap_table = 'auto';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_l;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_s;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_r;

CREATE TABLE aj_l (id UInt64, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';
CREATE TABLE aj_s (id UInt64, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';
CREATE TABLE aj_r (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';

INSERT INTO aj_l SELECT number, range(number, number + 20) FROM numbers(100);
INSERT INTO aj_s SELECT number, [number, number + 1] FROM numbers(5);
INSERT INTO aj_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000);

-- Each line counts the plans whose join reads `aj_r` first (`s` is the build side) and those reading `s` first.

SELECT 'arrayJoin, empty input', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'lowered arrayJoin, empty input, LEFT JOIN', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s LEFT JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, empty input', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE id > 1000) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

-- 5 input rows are estimated as 500 rows, fewer than the 1000 rows of `aj_r`.
SELECT 'lowered arrayJoin, 5 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_s) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

-- 100 input rows are estimated as 10000 rows (2000 in fact), more than the 1000 rows of `aj_r`.
SELECT 'arrayJoin, 100 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, 100 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s LEFT JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;
SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_s) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;
SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;

-- A filter on the array-joined elements leaves 6 rows in `s`; the estimate of its input must not make `aj_r` the build side.
SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, element filter', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM aj_r INNER JOIN (SELECT id FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE k = 5) AS s ON aj_r.id = s.id
    SETTINGS query_plan_fuse_filter_into_array_join = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, filter step', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM aj_r INNER JOIN (SELECT id FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE k = 5) AS s ON aj_r.id = s.id
    SETTINGS query_plan_fuse_filter_into_array_join = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

DROP TABLE aj_l;
DROP TABLE aj_s;
DROP TABLE aj_r;
```

</details>

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`4e3df38e874c`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

An unaccounted filter on array-joined elements should make the row estimate unknown, as every other branch of `estimateReadRowsCount` does, preserving the written join order.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
arrayJoin, empty input	1	0
lowered arrayJoin, empty input, LEFT JOIN	1	0
ARRAY JOIN, empty input	1	0
lowered arrayJoin, 5 rows	1	0
arrayJoin, 100 rows	0	1
ARRAY JOIN, 100 rows	0	1
0
10
2000
ARRAY JOIN, element filter	1	0
ARRAY JOIN, filter step	1	0
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The estimate stays known and inflated, so `swap_on_sizes` swaps the build side and the join builds the hash table from the large table instead of the filtered small side.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`4e3df38e874c`):

```
arrayJoin, empty input	1	0
lowered arrayJoin, empty input, LEFT JOIN	1	0
ARRAY JOIN, empty input	1	0
lowered arrayJoin, 5 rows	1	0
arrayJoin, 100 rows	0	1
ARRAY JOIN, 100 rows	0	1
0
10
2000
ARRAY JOIN, element filter	0	1
ARRAY JOIN, filter step	0	1
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

In the array-join branch, handle an unaccounted filter like the sibling branches: when `filter` is non-null or `array_join_step->hasElementFilter()`, return `estimated_rows = {}` (imprecise) unless the input estimate is exactly 0. #126491's case keeps working: its `WHERE id > 1000` sits below the array join (verified in EXPLAIN), so the proven-empty 0 still propagates. title: Array-join filter ignored in join estimate, wrong side picked for hash build
body:
### Describe what's wrong

- A filter on array-joined elements is dropped when estimating row counts for join reordering.
- Triggered by joining a table to an `ARRAY JOIN`/`arrayJoin` subquery that filters elements, subquery on the right.
- The estimator reports input x 100 as a known row count instead of marking it unknown.
- Causes the hash join to build from the much larger table, with ~21x peak memory and ~9x time.

Root cause: In `RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375` the array-join branch passes `nullptr` instead of `filter` and ignores `ArrayJoinStep::hasElementFilter`, so it returns the unfiltered `input x 100` as a known estimate at :377, which `swap_on_sizes` in `optimizeJoin.cpp:1269` uses to flip the join order.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `addChildQueryGraph` (optimizeJoin.cpp:650) → `estimateReadRowsCount` → the new array-join branch at RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375 calls the child with `nullptr` instead of `filter` and never checks `ArrayJoinStep::hasElementFilter` (ArrayJoinStep.h:46; `tryFuseFilterIntoArrayJoin` fuses element-only filters by default, fuseFilterIntoArrayJoin.cpp:82), then returns `input x 100` at :377 as a known estimate → `swap_on_sizes` (optimizeJoin.cpp:1269-1272) sees `lhs < rhs` and flips the join.

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:375`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp#L375) — array-join branch passes nullptr instead of `filter`; element filter of `ArrayJoinStep` not consulted
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp:377`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/RelationStatisticsEstimator.cpp#L377) — unfiltered input estimate multiplied by `array_join_rows_multiplier` and returned as known
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeJoin.cpp:1269`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeJoin.cpp#L1269) — `swap_on_sizes` swaps the hash join when both estimates are known and lhs < rhs
- [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ArrayJoinStep.h:46`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/717cb8ba64a8a3/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ArrayJoinStep.h#L46) — `hasElementFilter` exists but the estimator ignores it

Impact: A table joined to an `ARRAY JOIN`/`arrayJoin` subquery that filters the elements, with the subquery on the right, now builds the hash table from the left table whenever left rows < 100x the subquery's input rows. Repro: 5,000,000 vs 11 build rows, 21x peak memory, ~9x time, on every run. Results are correct. Master only (not in 26.10).

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

No — only `master` (`4e3df38e874c`). The bug starts with #126491 (merged as `4e3df38e874c`), which is in no release yet, so a release build (and ClickHouse Fiddle) still passes.

### How to reproduce

Reproduces reliably with `big` (5M rows) joined to a filtered `ARRAY JOIN` subquery over `events` (100k rows, 11 output rows); results stay correct, only performance and memory regress.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```sql
-- Random settings limits: query_plan_optimize_join_order_randomize=(0, 0); query_plan_optimize_join_order_limit=(1, None)

-- A hash join compares the sides by their row estimates, and an array join input is estimated
-- as 100 rows per row of its input.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_l;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_s;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_r;
SET enable_parallel_replicas = 0, join_algorithm = 'hash', query_plan_join_swap_table = 'auto';

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_l;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_s;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS aj_r;

CREATE TABLE aj_l (id UInt64, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';
CREATE TABLE aj_s (id UInt64, arr Array(UInt64)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';
CREATE TABLE aj_r (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS auto_statistics_types = '';

INSERT INTO aj_l SELECT number, range(number, number + 20) FROM numbers(100);
INSERT INTO aj_s SELECT number, [number, number + 1] FROM numbers(5);
INSERT INTO aj_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000);

-- Each line counts the plans whose join reads `aj_r` first (`s` is the build side) and those reading `s` first.

SELECT 'arrayJoin, empty input', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'lowered arrayJoin, empty input, LEFT JOIN', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s LEFT JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, empty input', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE id > 1000) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

-- 5 input rows are estimated as 500 rows, fewer than the 1000 rows of `aj_r`.
SELECT 'lowered arrayJoin, 5 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_s) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

-- 100 input rows are estimated as 10000 rows (2000 in fact), more than the 1000 rows of `aj_r`.
SELECT 'arrayJoin, 100 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k
    SETTINGS query_plan_lower_array_join_function = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, 100 rows', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_l WHERE id > 1000) AS s LEFT JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;
SELECT count() FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(arr) AS k FROM aj_s) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;
SELECT count() FROM (SELECT k FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k) AS s INNER JOIN aj_r ON aj_r.id = s.k;

-- A filter on the array-joined elements leaves 6 rows in `s`; the estimate of its input must not make `aj_r` the build side.

FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM aj_r INNER JOIN (SELECT id FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE k = 5) AS s ON aj_r.id = s.id
    SETTINGS query_plan_fuse_filter_into_array_join = 1)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

SELECT 'ARRAY JOIN, filter step', countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: aj_r%'), countIf(explain ILIKE '%Join: s%')
FROM (EXPLAIN actions = 1, keep_logical_steps = 1
    SELECT count() FROM aj_r INNER JOIN (SELECT id FROM aj_l ARRAY JOIN arr AS k WHERE k = 5) AS s ON aj_r.id = s.id
    SETTINGS query_plan_fuse_filter_into_array_join = 0)
WHERE explain ILIKE '%Join:%';

DROP TABLE aj_l;
DROP TABLE aj_s;
DROP TABLE aj_r;
```

text: REST Catalog: CREATE TABLE Fails Due to Invalid S3 Metadata URI (Missing URI Scheme) ### Describe what's wrong The Iceberg REST Catalog with S3-like storage expects the table location to include s3:// scheme when creating table. Because CH sends a location without scheme prefix, the create table request fails with an `Invalid S3 URI` error. I investigated the issue and noticed that the `location` parameter is being set to `/{namespace}/{table}/` when sending a POST request to `/v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}` to create a table. Since `/ns1/t/` does not include the required S3 URI scheme, the REST Catalog cannot recognize it as a valid storage location when using S3 as the underlying storage. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce First, deploy the services given docker-compose file attached (REST service with an s3-like storage ) ```sql SET allow_database_iceberg = 1; SET allow_experimental_insert_into_iceberg = 1; CREATE DATABASE demo ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('http://127.0.0.1:8181/v1', 'admin', 'password') SETTINGS catalog_type = 'rest', storage_endpoint = 'http://minio:9000', warehouse = 'warehouse'; CREATE TABLE demo.`ns.t` (id Int64, v Int64); INSERT INTO demo.`ns.t` VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30); ``` ### Expected behavior Table is expected to be created with no error, instead, an error returns from Rest Catalog API. ### Error message and/or stacktrace [error.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34181441/error.log) ### Related issues and pull requests Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115652 ### Additional context _No response_ ### Version info - Resolved by: #128636 - Merged into: `26.11.1.1193-master` (included in `26.11` and later)

text:
`rowNumberInAllBlocks()` resets per chunk in S3/file `PARTITION BY` after #92844

## Summary

Using `rowNumberInAllBlocks()` directly in the `PARTITION BY` expression of `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` (also reproducible with `file(...)`) no longer yields a continuous counter across chunks. On 26.8, the partition-key calculation appears to reconstruct the stateful function for every chunk, resetting its counter to zero.

This is a **user-visible behavior regression** from 25.8: an export that previously split 625 million rows into 13 objects (12 × 50 million rows and one × 25 million rows) now writes a single large object with the same query and data. With other chunk sizes it can silently produce *more* files of incorrect sizes instead.

The apparent cause is #92844, merged January 5, 2026: [avoid caching the partition key for non-deterministic functions](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/92844) (implementation commit [`b9942df`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commit/b9942dfed0958d0b63cf82fed939fbeba79be2ed)).

## Versions

- **Reproduced as broken:** `26.8.34.13` (`SELECT version()`; Docker image `clickhouse/clickhouse-server@sha256:8b28eb09479c36c4533eec7a6268917d04ba3a6fd90e3f4205f70e761b6d7779`).
- **Previously worked:** our production export on 25.8. The `v25.8.33.6-lts` implementation did not conditionally discard non-deterministic partition-key actions.
- **Also potentially affected:** `v26.3.60.2-lts` contains the same relevant `hasNonDeterministic()` code path; I have not separately confirmed the reproducer on that version.

## Minimal reproduction (no S3 credentials required)

Run in a clean `user_files` directory, or use a fresh filename prefix so files from previous runs do not affect the readback.

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION file('bad_{_partition_id}.parquet', 'Parquet')
PARTITION BY intDiv(rowNumberInAllBlocks(), 1000)
SELECT number
FROM numbers(5000)
SETTINGS
    max_block_size = 1000,
    max_insert_threads = 1,
    engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1;

SELECT _file, count() AS rows
FROM file('bad_*.parquet', 'Parquet')
GROUP BY _file
ORDER BY _file;
```

### Expected (25.8 behavior)

Five files, `bad_0.parquet` through `bad_4.parquet`, each containing 1,000 rows. The expectation here is based on the previously observed cross-chunk behavior, not a claim that the docs explicitly guarantee partition-key function-instance lifetime.

### Actual (observed on 26.8.34.13)

```text
bad_0.parquet    5000
```

All rows use partition 0: for each chunk, the counter appears to restart in the range `0..999`, so `intDiv(..., 1000)` remains zero.

This is not limited to a single large file. With a MergeTree source of 200,000 rows and a target of 50,000 rows per file, we observed **10 files** rather than 4, with row counts:

```text
30000, 30000, 30000, 30000, 24352,
20000, 15536, 10000, 10000, 112
```

The export succeeds but the number and size of objects are wrong.

## Suspected root cause

[`rowNumberInAllBlocks.cpp` at v26.8.34.13-lts](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Functions/rowNumberInAllBlocks.cpp) stores the counter inside a function instance:

```cpp
mutable std::atomic<size_t> rows{0};
```

The function reports `isStateful() == true` and `isDeterministic() == false`.

Following #92844, [`IPartitionStrategy.cpp` at v26.8.34.13-lts](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Storages/IPartitionStrategy.cpp) caches partition-key expression actions only if `!actions->getActionsDAG().hasNonDeterministic()`. Otherwise, `getCachedOrBuildActions()` rebuilds the actions when `computePartitionKey()` runs for each chunk. This appears to create a fresh `FunctionRowNumberInAllBlocks` instance—and therefore a fresh zero counter—for each chunk.

Before #92844, `WildcardPartitionStrategy` and `HiveStylePartitionStrategy` constructed and retained these expression actions instead.

**Why this is not simply a request to revert #92844:** the PR addressed a real issue with non-deterministic keys (including `now64()` evaluated across separate inserts). Its regression test is under `tests/integration/test_s3_non_deterministic_partition_by/`, and tests that behavior, but it does not cover stateful counters across chunks within a single insert. The PR has a changelog entry, but neither that entry nor the test calls out this behavior change for stateful expressions.

The old behavior may have been an incidental consequence of action caching rather than a formally supported guarantee. Nevertheless, existing exports depended on it, and the change silently changes their output layout.

## Workaround verified on 26.8.34.13

Evaluate `rowNumberInAllBlocks()` as an output column of the `SELECT` and partition by that column rather than calling it directly inside `PARTITION BY`:

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION file('fix_{_partition_id}.parquet', 'Parquet')
PARTITION BY intDiv(rn, 1000)
SELECT
    number AS id,
    rowNumberInAllBlocks() AS rn
FROM numbers(5000)
SETTINGS
    max_block_size = 1000,
    max_insert_threads = 1,
    engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1;

SELECT _file, count() AS rows
FROM file('fix_*.parquet', 'Parquet')
GROUP BY _file
ORDER BY _file;
```

Reported verification on 26.8.34.13: `fix_0.parquet` through `fix_4.parquet`, each with 1,000 rows. Also tested on a parallel `numbers_mt` insert: 330,000 rows, `max_insert_threads = 8`, bucket size 50,000 → 7 files (6 × 50,000 plus 30,000), with 330,000 distinct IDs and no missing or duplicate IDs.

The same pattern can be used with `s3(...)` and `PARTITION BY intDiv(rn, 50000000)`, using the source query's real columns. **Caveat:** with the wildcard partition strategy, the helper column `rn` is included in the exported Parquet schema. S3 also supports Hive partitioning and a `partition_columns_in_data_file` argument, but that alternative is not part of the verified workaround above.

## Questions

1. Is resetting stateful functions for every partition-key chunk an intended contract change, or an unintended consequence of #92844?
2. Can partition-key evaluation preserve a stateful function instance **within one INSERT** without reintroducing the original non-deterministic-key bug **across INSERTs**? A regression test should cover both the `now64()` scenario and `rowNumberInAllBlocks()` spanning multiple chunks.
3. If the old behavior will not be supported, could the limitation and a reliable alternative be documented explicitly? The current failure is silent and can materially alter exported object layout.

Native splitting by output row count or object size would avoid depending on a stateful partition expression, but that is a separate feature request from this regression.

### Version info
- Resolved by: #128217
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1574-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

Its regression test is under `tests/integration/test_s3_non_deterministic_partition_by/`, and tests that behavior, but it does not cover stateful counters across chunks within a single insert. The PR has a changelog entry, but neither that entry nor the test calls out this behavior change for stateful expressions.

The old behavior may have been an incidental consequence of action caching rather than a formally supported guarantee. Nevertheless, existing exports depended on it, and the change silently changes their output layout.

## Workaround verified on 26.8.34.13

Evaluate `rowNumberInAllBlocks()` as an output column of the `SELECT` and partition by that column rather than calling it directly inside `PARTITION BY`:

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION file('fix_{_partition_id}.parquet', 'Parquet')
PARTITION BY intDiv(rn, 1000)
SELECT
    number AS id,
    rowNumberInAllBlocks() AS rn
FROM numbers(5000)
SETTINGS
    max_block_size = 1000,
    max_insert_threads = 1,
    engine_file_truncate_on_insert = 1;

SELECT _file, count() AS rows
FROM file('fix_*.parquet', 'Parquet')
GROUP BY _file
ORDER BY _file;
```

Reported verification on 26.8.34.13: `fix_0.parquet` through `fix_4.parquet`, each with 1,000 rows. Also tested on a parallel `numbers_mt` insert: 330,000 rows, `max_insert_threads = 8`, bucket size 50,000 → 7 files (6 × 50,000 plus 30,000), with 330,000 distinct IDs and no missing or duplicate IDs.

The same pattern can be used with `s3(...)` and `PARTITION BY intDiv(rn, 50000000)`, using the source query's real columns. **Caveat:** with the wildcard partition strategy, the helper column `rn` is included in the exported Parquet schema. S3 also supports Hive partitioning and a `partition_columns_in_data_file` argument, but that alternative is not part of the verified workaround above.

## Questions

1. Is resetting stateful functions for every partition-key chunk an intended contract change, or an unintended consequence of #92844?
2. Can partition-key evaluation preserve a stateful function instance **within one INSERT** without reintroducing the original non-deterministic-key bug **across INSERTs**? A regression test should cover both the `now64()` scenario and `rowNumberInAllBlocks()` spanning multiple chunks.
3. If the old behavior will not be supported, could the limitation and a reliable alternative be documented explicitly? The current failure is silent and can materially alter exported object layout.

Native splitting by output row count or object size would avoid depending on a stateful partition expression, but that is a separate feature request from this regression.

Queries on S3 cache unecessarily enqueues part check on TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED exception

### Company or project name

_No response_

### Describe the unexpected behaviour

Concurrent queries of the same part that reads through a s3 filesystem cache may lead to necessary part checks if the queries throw a TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED exception like when max_execution_time is set.

When a query waiting for part download hits max_execution_time while reading a part from S3 through the filesystem cache, the error is not treated as retryable and ClickHouse will enqueues a part integrity check on the part despite the part itself not being corrupt. This leads to redundant part checks on parts in S3.

If a generated output is preferred:

`CancellationChecker` kills the query with `CancelReason::TIMEOUT`. The read thread is still inside `MergeTreeReaderWide::readRows`. Two S3 cache paths then call `QueryStatus::throwIfKilled`:
- `FileSegment::wait` does this while the read is blocked on another thread downloading the same cache segment. It checks about once a second.
- `S3::Client::doRequest` does this after a failed `GetObject`, before retrying. `CurrentThread::checkIfNotCancelled` calls `throwIfKilled`.
`throwIfKilled` throws `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED`. The catch in `readRows` calls `reportBroken` for any exception that `isRetryableException` rejects. `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` is not in that list (`NETWORK_ERROR`, `SOCKET_TIMEOUT`, and `ABORTED` are). `reportBrokenPart` then calls `enqueuePartForCheck` for an active part on ReplicatedMergeTree.

26.8.34.13

2. concurrently try to read that part with queries having max_execution_timeout shorter than the time it takes to load the part

text:
`DataLakeCatalog` can't read tables stored on HDFS: `Unsupported storage type: hdfs://`

### Company or project name

IMC Trading

### Describe what's wrong

A DataLakeCatalog database fails on every table whose location uses the `hdfs://` scheme. Reading the same table directly with `icebergHDFS()` works.

All catalog types get the storage type from `DataLake::tryParseStorageTypeFromString` in `src/Databases/DataLake/ICatalog.cpp`. That function lowercases the scheme, capitalises the first letter, and looks the result up in `StorageType` with `magic_enum::enum_cast`. So `hdfs` becomes `Hdfs`, which doesn't match the enum value `HDFS`, and the function then throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

`file`, `s3a`, `oss`, `gs` and `abfss` all have explicit mappings. `hdfs` has none.

Changing the configuration doesn't work around it. The `storage_type_str` override in `TableMetadata::getStorageType()` uses the same parser, so a value of `HDFS` also becomes `Hdfs`.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

Version: 26.10.3.7
Interface: HTTP and `clickhouse-local`, both affected
Setup: an Iceberg REST catalog whose warehouse is on HDFS, so table locations look like `hdfs://<nameservice>/warehouse/...`. HDFS access is configured with Kerberos (`<hdfs>` block and `LIBHDFS3_CONF`) and works.

```sql
SET allow_database_iceberg = 1;

CREATE DATABASE lake
ENGINE = DataLakeCatalog('https://<rest-catalog-host>/')
SETTINGS catalog_type = 'rest', warehouse = '<warehouse>';

-- Fails:
SELECT count() FROM lake.`<namespace>.<table>`;

-- The same table read directly works, so HDFS and Kerberos are fine:
SELECT count() FROM icebergHDFS('hdfs://<nameservice>/warehouse/<namespace>/<table>');
```

### Expected behavior

`hdfs://` locations resolve to `StorageType::HDFS`, and the table reads the same way it does through `icebergHDFS()`.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

```
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Unsupported storage type: hdfs://. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
```

### Related issues and pull requests

- Fix: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112468. It maps `hdfs` to `StorageType::HDFS` and adds a gtest.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126172 also edits location parsing in `ICatalog.cpp`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84125 reported the same error for `gs://`. It was fixed by adding a scheme mapping, the same kind of fix needed here.


### Additional context

The bug affects every `DataLakeCatalog` catalog type (REST, Glue, Hive, Unity), because they all share the same parsing code. Today the only workarounds are to define an `IcebergHDFS` table or call `icebergHDFS()` for each table, which means giving up catalog discovery.

### Version info
- Resolved by: #112468
- Merged into: `26.11.1.1338-master` (included in `26.11` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

```sql
SELECT count() FROM lake.`<namespace>.<table>`;

-- The same table read directly works, so HDFS and Kerberos are fine:
SELECT count() FROM icebergHDFS('hdfs://<nameservice>/warehouse/<namespace>/<table>');
```

### Expected behavior

`hdfs://` locations resolve to `StorageType::HDFS`, and the table reads the same way it does through `icebergHDFS()`.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

```
Code: 48. DB::Exception: Unsupported storage type: hdfs://. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
```

### Related issues and pull requests

- Fix: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112468. It maps `hdfs` to `StorageType::HDFS` and adds a gtest.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126172 also edits location parsing in `ICatalog.cpp`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84125 reported the same error for `gs://`. It was fixed by adding a scheme mapping, the same kind of fix needed here.


### Additional context

The bug affects every `DataLakeCatalog` catalog type (REST, Glue, Hive, Unity), because they all share the same parsing code. Today the only workarounds are to define an `IcebergHDFS` table or call `icebergHDFS()` for each table, which means giving up catalog discovery.

text:
Failed merge does not stop its other in-flight S3 reads

A background merge or mutation can have several S3 reads in flight at the same time. For example, a vertical merge prefetches the next column from every source part ([`vertical_merge_remote_filesystem_prefetch`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp#L2110)).

When one read fails, for example because it exhausts its S3 retries, the merge fails. The other in-flight reads do not stop. They keep retrying to their own budget, and the task is destroyed only after the slowest of them ends. With default settings one `GetObject` retries 500 times with backoff up to 5 s, so one read can hold the task for about 41 minutes.

### Current behavior

1. The exception reaches `MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor::routine`. It calls `cancel` on the task, then destroys the task ([code](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeBackgroundExecutor.cpp#L520-L543)).
2. [`MergeTask::cancel`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTask.cpp#L2954-L2969) and [`MutateTask::cancel`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/Storages/MergeTree/MutateTask.cpp#L4331-L4338) cancel only the pipeline. This is cooperative. A read inside the S3 retry loop does not see it.
3. Nothing sets `MergeListElement::is_cancelled`. The thread group cancellation predicate reads this flag, so `ThreadStatus::isQueryCanceled` stays `false` and [`Client::RetryStrategy::ShouldRetry`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/IO/S3/Client.cpp#L114) keeps retrying.
4. The task destructor waits for each in-flight prefetch in [`AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::resetPrefetch`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/d350a633d54015ae4a6f44592309b07974a6d019/src/Disks/IO/AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer.cpp#L463). The executor then logs `Destroying background task took {} milliseconds`. A `DROP TABLE` of this table waits for the same task.

### Expected behavior

When a merge or mutation fails, its other in-flight reads stop at their next retry check. The task is destroyed within one retry backoff.

### Proposed fix

Set `is_cancelled` on the merge list entry at the start of `MergeTask::cancel` and `MutateTask::cancel`. The executor calls `cancel` on every failure path before it destroys the task. The merge and mutation predicates already read this flag. https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113939 also makes `ReadBufferFromS3::processException` throw on cancellation, so build this fix on top of it.

For the test, extend `test_merge_cancel_s3_read` from that PR. Do not add a new integration test module. Make one read of a merge fail, and check that the other in-flight reads stop.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113939
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/127402

text:
COUNT(DISTINCT) with GROUP BY: skip rows that repeat the previous row's group and value (ClickBench q9 −19%, q10 −16% on Graviton3)

### Describe the situation
COUNT(DISTINCT x) with GROUP BY inserts every row into its group's uniqExact set, even when the row has the same group and value as the previous row, which is common in sorted data. The patch drops such rows before inserting and inserts the rest in batches of 256 rows.

Hot latency, median of 3 runs per round; 7 paired fresh-server rounds, 95% CI; ClickBench hits, 4-core Graviton3.

| Query | Master 8d5702d8 | Patched | Ratio [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| q9 `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 777 ms | 629 ms | 0.813 [0.801, 0.825] |
| q10 `RegionID, SUM, COUNT, AVG, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 977 ms | 821 ms | 0.841 [0.823, 0.859] |
| q9 / q10 with `max_threads = 16` | 826 / 1019 ms | 673 / 871 ms | 0.815 [0.809, 0.821] / 0.855 [0.848, 0.862] |
| `EventDate, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 722 ms | 569 ms | 0.780 [0.761, 0.799] |
| `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase)` (String) | 1420 ms | 1010 ms | 0.692 [0.638, 0.751] |
| `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT WatchID)` (values never repeat) | 2031 ms | 2018 ms | 0.996 [0.985, 1.006] |
| Small sets: `CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID)` / `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT OS)` | 207 / 314 ms | 196 / 304 ms | 0.949 [0.925, 0.973] / 0.966 [0.954, 0.979] |
| q11 / q12 / q14 | 250 / 306 / 750 ms | 243 / 296 / 754 ms | 0.975 [0.961, 0.990] / 0.978 [0.954, 1.002] / 1.005 [0.989, 1.021] |
| q5 (no GROUP BY) / q16 (`GROUP BY UserID`), paths not changed | 228 / 283 ms | 229 / 283 ms | 1.022 [0.978, 1.068] / 0.999 [0.991, 1.007] |
| 4 clients × 4 runs, total wall, q9 / q10 (2 rounds) | 14.6 / 17.8 s | 11.7 / 14.8 s | 0.806 / 0.833 |
| Cold q9 / q10, data pages dropped, median of 8 pairs | 1746 / 1979 ms | 1722 / 1959 ms | unchanged |

Results are identical in every run, and peak memory is unchanged (q9 856 / 856 MiB, q10 795 / 793 MiB). On x86 (Xeon 6975P-C, ThinLTO builds), @groeneai measured q9 0.786 [0.753, 0.820] and q10 0.803 [0.783, 0.824] with `max_threads = 4`, with no slower control ([comment](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6452077614)).

@Algunenano, this is the separate issue you asked for in [#124126](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6494223566). Unlike the patch rejected there, this one uses no software prefetch.

<details><summary>Why rows repeat and why skipping them is faster</summary>

`hits` is sorted by `CounterID, EventDate, UserID`, so 78% of its rows have the same `(RegionID, UserID)` as the previous row. The grouped path (`IAggregateFunctionDataHelper::addBatch`) inserts each of them again. Inserting a key that a set already contains never changes the set, and the keyless path already skips such rows with its last-value cache (`Adder::addManyChunked`).

- For numeric arguments the key is the value itself, so collecting the keys is branch-free: every row writes its key and set pointer, and the count advances only when `(place, value)` differs from the previous row. A first version with an ordinary `if (repeated) continue;` made `CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID)` 10% slower: branch misses rose from 110M to 204M over 5 runs, because skipping an insert into a small, cached set saves less than a misprediction costs. The branch-free version stays at 112M.
- For `String` and `IPv6` the key is a 128-bit SipHash of the value, so skipping a row also saves hashing it.
- With the keys of a chunk collected first, the insert loop has no branch on the repeat test, and more cache misses on the large sets overlap. `perf stat` of q9 (5 runs): cycles 39.5G → 32.1G, instructions 61.0G → 58.5G, branch misses 670M → 576M.

</details>

<details><summary>Correctness</summary>

Master and patch give identical output for 153 upstream stateless tests that use `uniqExact` or `count(DISTINCT)` with `GROUP BY` (run with clickhouse-local, where 51 of them stop early in both builds), and for a check suite under six settings (default, `max_threads = 1`, `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 0`, forced two-level aggregation, `max_block_size = 97`, `enable_software_prefetch_in_aggregation = 0`). The suite covers runs, `-If`, `Nullable`, `String`, `FixedString`, `IPv6`, `UUID`, `Int128`, `Decimal`, floats with NaN and ±0, `LowCardinality`, two-level sets, `WITH TOTALS`, `ROLLUP` and `-State`/`-Merge`, and checks the counts against `SELECT DISTINCT` pairs. The patch adds a smaller version as the stateless test `05472_grouped_uniq_exact_repeated_rows`.

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and builds</summary>

Measured on master 8d5702d8 (2026-10-26) and the same commit with the patch: Release builds with clang 21, without LTO. The x86 numbers above are from @groeneai's ThinLTO release builds of the same commits. The base already has the radix-partitioned keyless `uniqExact` and the Robin Hood two-level hash tables (#123552, #127252, #125001). The grouped `uniqExact` insert loop has not changed since 8d5702d8, and the patch applies cleanly to master 6624a338 (2026-10-29).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

ClickBench `hits` (MergeTree, 100M rows, default codecs) on a 4-vCPU Graviton3 (c7g). For each of 7 rounds and each binary (order alternating): start a fresh server, run `SYSTEM STOP MERGES`, then for each query one warm-up and three timed runs with `use_query_condition_cache = 0`, and compare the per-round medians. Ratio = paired geometric mean with a Student-t 95% interval.

```sql
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10; -- q9
SELECT RegionID, SUM(AdvEngineID), COUNT(*) AS c, AVG(ResolutionWidth), COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10; -- q10
SELECT EventDate, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY EventDate ORDER BY EventDate;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT WatchID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY CounterID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT OS) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC, RegionID LIMIT 10;
-- q11, q12, q14, q5 and q16 are the ClickBench queries; the max_threads = 16 rows add SETTINGS max_threads = 16 to q9 and q10.
```

Concurrency: 4 clients each run the query 4 times; total wall time per binary, 2 rounds in alternating order. Cold runs: fresh server, `echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`, re-read the server binary, one run; 8 pairs in ABBA order.

When the page cache is dropped while the server runs, a first run also reads the query's code from disk, and the two builds lay out their code differently: there, q10 was 3.5% slower in median and q9 unchanged. With the binary re-read after the drop, so that only data is cold, both are unchanged.

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A row whose group and value equal the previous row's should not cost a hash-set insert, as in the keyless path. Data without such repeats should run at the same speed.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126 (software prefetch for the same loop, rejected; this issue was requested there)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/124197 (the prefetch patch as a PR, closed)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128029 (the same kind of skip for `count()`-only `GROUP BY` in the adaptive aggregator; a different loop, which does not cover `uniqExact`)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127940 (skips repeated `LowCardinality` values without `GROUP BY` only)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127280 (radix-partitioned keyless `uniqExact`; does not change the `GROUP BY` path)

</details>

### Additional context
The same skip also works for grouped `uniq` (not `uniqCombined`, whose small exact set converts to HyperLogLog on the next insert of any value). That increment and its measurements are in [this comment](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6448909285); it is not part of the patch below.

<details><summary>Patch (master 8d5702d8, applies to 6624a338)</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h b/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
index 97ec574cb1d..32769462ff9 100644
--- a/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
+++ b/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
@@ -561,6 +561,73 @@ private:
     static constexpr bool is_able_to_parallelize_merge = Data::is_able_to_parallelize_merge;
     static constexpr bool is_parallelize_merge_prepare_needed = Data::is_parallelize_merge_prepare_needed;
     static constexpr bool is_uniques_hash_set = detail::IsUniquesHashSet<DataSet>::value;
+    static constexpr bool is_uniq_exact_set = detail::IsUniqExactSet<DataSet>::value;
+
+    /// `uniqExact` over many places (GROUP BY). A row whose place and value repeat those of the previous row is
+    /// skipped: inserting a key that a set already contains never changes it, and such runs are common in data
+    /// sorted by the grouping and argument columns (as in the keyless path, see `Adder::addManyChunked`).
+    /// The keys of a chunk of rows are collected first. For values that are their own keys the collection is
+    /// branch-free, because short runs make a skip branch mispredict more often than a skipped insert into a small
+    /// set saves; for other values (hashed strings) a repeated row also skips its hash.
+    template <bool check_places>
+    void addBatchExact(size_t row_begin, size_t row_end, AggregateDataPtr * places, size_t place_offset,
+        const IColumn ** columns, ssize_t if_argument_pos) const
+    {
+        using Traits = detail::AggregateFunctionUniqTraits<T, ColumnType>;
+        using Key = typename DataSet::value_type;
+        static constexpr auto hint = is_able_to_parallelize_merge ? SetLevelHint::unknown : SetLevelHint::singleLevel;
+        static constexpr bool value_is_key = std::is_same_v<std::decay_t<decltype(Traits::hashExact(T{}))>, T>;
+        static constexpr size_t chunk_size = 256;
+
+        const char8_t * flags = nullptr;
+        if (if_argument_pos >= 0)
+            flags = assert_cast<const ColumnUInt8 &>(*columns[if_argument_pos]).getData().data();
+        const IColumn & column = *columns[0];
+
+        std::array<Key, chunk_size> keys; // NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init,hicpp-member-init) - only the first `count` entries are read
+        std::array<DataSet *, chunk_size> sets; // NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init,hicpp-member-init)
+        AggregateDataPtr last_place = nullptr;
+        T last_value{};
+
+        size_t row = row_begin;
+        while (row < row_end)
+        {
+            const size_t chunk_end = row + std::min(chunk_size, row_end - row);
+            size_t count = 0;
+            for (; row < chunk_end; ++row)
+            {
+                if constexpr (check_places)
+                {
+                    if (!places[row])
+                        continue;
+                }
+                if (flags && !flags[row])
+                    continue;
+
+                AggregateDataPtr place = places[row] + place_offset;
+                const auto value = Traits::value(column, row);
+                if constexpr (value_is_key)
+                {
+                    const bool repeated = (place == last_place) & bitEquals(value, last_value);
+                    keys[count] = value;
+                    sets[count] = &this->data(place).set;
+                    count += !repeated;
+                }
+                else
+                {
+                    if (place == last_place && bitEquals(value, last_value))
+                        continue;
+                    keys[count] = Traits::hashExact(value);
+                    sets[count++] = &this->data(place).set;
+                }
+                last_place = place;
+                last_value = value;
+            }
+
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
+                sets[i]->template insert<const Key &, hint>(keys[i]);
+        }
+    }
 
 public:
     explicit AggregateFunctionUniq(const DataTypes & argument_types_)
@@ -616,6 +683,8 @@ public:
                 [&](size_t row) { return DataSet::fullHash(Traits::hash(Traits::value(*columns[0], row))); },
                 [&](AggregateDataPtr place) { return &this->data(place).set; });
         }
+        else if constexpr (is_uniq_exact_set)
+            addBatchExact</* check_places = */ true>(row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, if_argument_pos);
         else
             IAggregateFunctionDataHelper<Data, AggregateFunctionUniq<T, ColumnType, Data>>::addBatch(
                 row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, arena, if_argument_pos);
@@ -626,6 +695,8 @@ public:
     {
         if constexpr (std::is_same_v<Data, AggregateFunctionUniqUniquesHashSetData>)
             addBatch(row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, arena, if_argument_pos);
+        else if constexpr (is_uniq_exact_set)
+            addBatchExact</* check_places = */ false>(row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, if_argument_pos);
         else
             /// Unlike its addBatch, the base's non-null variant skips the per-row places[] test.
             IAggregateFunctionDataHelper<Data, AggregateFunctionUniq<T, ColumnType, Data>>::addBatchWithNonNullPlaces(

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+-- Grouped uniqExact skips a row that repeats the place and value of the previous row. Results must not change.
+
+DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_grouped_uniq_exact;
+CREATE TABLE t_grouped_uniq_exact (g UInt32, x UInt64, s String, f Float64, n Nullable(UInt64), c UInt8, ip IPv6)
+ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple();
+
+-- Runs of repeated (g, x) pairs, interleaved groups, floats with NaN and signed zeros, NULLs.
+INSERT INTO t_grouped_uniq_exact SELECT
+    intDiv(number, 7) % 13,
+    if(number < 300000, intDiv(number, 3) % 120000, number),
+    toString(intDiv(number, 5) % 50000),
+    multiIf(number % 11 = 0, nan, number % 11 = 1, -0., number % 11 = 2, 0., toFloat64(intDiv(number, 2) % 1000) / 7),
+    if(number % 5 = 0, NULL, intDiv(number, 2) % 70000),
+    number % 4 = 0,
+    toIPv6(IPv4NumToString(toUInt32(intDiv(number, 3) % 30000)))
+FROM numbers(500000);
+
+SELECT g, uniqExact(x), uniqExact(s), uniqExact(f), uniqExact(n), uniqExactIf(x, c), uniqExact(ip), count(DISTINCT x)
+FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g;
+
+-- Sets that convert to two-level (150000 keys per group, more than the 100000 threshold).
+SELECT x % 2 AS k, uniqExact(x), uniqExact(s) FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY k ORDER BY k;
+
+-- Small blocks, several threads and two-level aggregation give the same results.
+SELECT g, uniqExact(x), uniqExact(s), uniqExact(f) FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g
+SETTINGS max_block_size = 97, max_threads = 3;
+SELECT g, uniqExact(x), uniqExactIf(s, c) FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g
+SETTINGS group_by_two_level_threshold = 1, group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes = 1;
+
+-- The same counts from distinct pairs.
+SELECT (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, uniqExact(x) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g))
+     = (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, toUInt64(count()) AS u FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g, x FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact) GROUP BY g ORDER BY g));
+SELECT (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, uniqExact(s) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g))
+     = (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, toUInt64(count()) AS u FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g, s FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact) GROUP BY g ORDER BY g));
+SELECT (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, uniqExact(n) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g))
+     = (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, toUInt64(count()) AS u FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g, n FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact WHERE n IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY g ORDER BY g));
+SELECT (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, uniqExactIf(x, c) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g))
+     = (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, toUInt64(count()) AS u FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g, x FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact WHERE c) GROUP BY g ORDER BY g));
+SELECT (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, uniqExact(ip) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g ORDER BY g))
+     = (SELECT groupArray((g, u)) FROM (SELECT g, toUInt64(count()) AS u FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g, ip FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact) GROUP BY g ORDER BY g));
+-- The keyless path agrees with the grouped path.
+SELECT (SELECT uniqExact(f) FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact WHERE g = 5) = (SELECT u FROM (SELECT g, uniqExact(f) AS u FROM t_grouped_uniq_exact GROUP BY g) WHERE g = 5);
+
+DROP TABLE t_grouped_uniq_exact;
```

@groeneai could you take a look? If the analysis and patch hold up, feel free to open a PR if it fits.

</details>

title: COUNT(DISTINCT) with GROUP BY: skip rows that repeat the previous row's group and value (ClickBench q9 −19%, q10 −16% on Graviton3)
body:
### Describe the situation
COUNT(DISTINCT x) with GROUP BY inserts every row into its group's uniqExact set, even when the row has the same group and value as the previous row, which is common in sorted data. The patch drops such rows before inserting and inserts the rest in batches of 256 rows.

Hot latency, median of 3 runs per round; 7 paired fresh-server rounds, 95% CI; ClickBench hits, 4-core Graviton3.

| Query | Master 8d5702d8 | Patched | Ratio [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| q9 `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 777 ms | 629 ms | 0.813 [0.801, 0.825] |
| q10 `RegionID, SUM, COUNT, AVG, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 977 ms | 821 ms | 0.841 [0.823, 0.859] |
| q9 / q10 with `max_threads = 16` | 826 / 1019 ms | 673 / 871 ms | 0.815 [0.809, 0.821] / 0.855 [0.848, 0.862] |
| `EventDate, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID)` | 722 ms | 569 ms | 0.780 [0.761, 0.799] |
| `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase)` (String) | 1420 ms | 1010 ms | 0.692 [0.638, 0.751] |
| `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT WatchID)` (values never repeat) | 2031 ms | 2018 ms | 0.996 [0.985, 1.006] |
| Small sets: `CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID)` / `RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT OS)` | 207 / 314 ms | 196 / 304 ms | 0.949 [0.925, 0.973] / 0.966 [0.954, 0.979] |
| q11 / q12 / q14 | 250 / 306 / 750 ms | 243 / 296 / 754 ms | 0.975 [0.961, 0.990] / 0.978 [0.954, 1.002] / 1.005 [0.989, 1.021] |
| q5 (no GROUP BY) / q16 (`GROUP BY UserID`), paths not changed | 228 / 283 ms | 229 / 283 ms | 1.022 [0.978, 1.068] / 0.999 [0.991, 1.007] |
| 4 clients × 4 runs, total wall, q9 / q10 (2 rounds) | 14.6 / 17.8 s | 11.7 / 14.8 s | 0.806 / 0.833 |
| Cold q9 / q10, data pages dropped, median of 8 pairs | 1746 / 1979 ms | 1722 / 1959 ms | unchanged |

Results are identical in every run, and peak memory is unchanged (q9 856 / 856 MiB, q10 795 / 793 MiB). On x86 (Xeon 6975P-C, ThinLTO builds), @groeneai measured q9 0.786 [0.753, 0.820] and q10 0.803 [0.783, 0.824] with `max_threads = 4`, with no slower control ([comment](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6452077614)).

@Algunenano, this is the separate issue you asked for in [#124126](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6494223566). Unlike the patch rejected there, this one uses no software prefetch.

<details><summary>Why rows repeat and why skipping them is faster</summary>

`hits` is sorted by `CounterID, EventDate, UserID`, so 78% of its rows have the same `(RegionID, UserID)` as the previous row. The grouped path (`IAggregateFunctionDataHelper::addBatch`) inserts each of them again. Inserting a key that a set already contains never changes the set, and the keyless path already skips such rows with its last-value cache (`Adder::addManyChunked`).

- For numeric arguments the key is the value itself, so collecting the keys is branch-free: every row writes its key and set pointer, and the count advances only when `(place, value)` differs from the previous row. A first version with an ordinary `if (repeated) continue;` made `CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID)` 10% slower: branch misses rose from 110M to 204M over 5 runs, because skipping an insert into a small, cached set saves less than a misprediction costs. The branch-free version stays at 112M.
- For `String` and `IPv6` the key is a 128-bit SipHash of the value, so skipping a row also saves hashing it.
- With the keys of a chunk collected first, the insert loop has no branch on the repeat test, and more cache misses on the large sets overlap. `perf stat` of q9 (5 runs): cycles 39.5G → 32.1G, instructions 61.0G → 58.5G, branch misses 670M → 576M.

</details>

<details><summary>Correctness</summary>

Master and patch give identical output for 153 upstream stateless tests that use `uniqExact` or `count(DISTINCT)` with `GROUP BY` (run with clickhouse-local, where 51 of them stop early in both builds), and for a check suite under six settings (default, `max_threads = 1`, `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 0`, forced two-level aggregation, `max_block_size = 97`, `enable_software_prefetch_in_aggregation = 0`). The suite covers runs, `-If`, `Nullable`, `String`, `FixedString`, `IPv6`, `UUID`, `Int128`, `Decimal`, floats with NaN and ±0, `LowCardinality`, two-level sets, `WITH TOTALS`, `ROLLUP` and `-State`/`-Merge`, and checks the counts against `SELECT DISTINCT` pairs. The patch adds a smaller version as the stateless test `05472_grouped_uniq_exact_repeated_rows`.

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?
<details><summary>Tested versions and builds</summary>

Measured on master 8d5702d8 (2026-10-26) and the same commit with the patch: Release builds with clang 21, without LTO. The x86 numbers above are from @groeneai's ThinLTO release builds of the same commits. The base already has the radix-partitioned keyless `uniqExact` and the Robin Hood two-level hash tables (#123552, #127252, #125001). The grouped `uniqExact` insert loop has not changed since 8d5702d8, and the patch applies cleanly to master 6624a338 (2026-10-29).

</details>

### How to reproduce
<details><summary>Data, queries and measurement procedure</summary>

ClickBench `hits` (MergeTree, 100M rows, default codecs) on a 4-vCPU Graviton3 (c7g). For each of 7 rounds and each binary (order alternating): start a fresh server, run `SYSTEM STOP MERGES`, then for each query one warm-up and three timed runs with `use_query_condition_cache = 0`, and compare the per-round medians. Ratio = paired geometric mean with a Student-t 95% interval.

```sql
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10; -- q9
SELECT RegionID, SUM(AdvEngineID), COUNT(*) AS c, AVG(ResolutionWidth), COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY c DESC LIMIT 10; -- q10
SELECT EventDate, COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY EventDate ORDER BY EventDate;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT WatchID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT CounterID, COUNT(DISTINCT RegionID) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY CounterID ORDER BY u DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT RegionID, COUNT(DISTINCT OS) AS u FROM hits GROUP BY RegionID ORDER BY u DESC, RegionID LIMIT 10;
-- q11, q12, q14, q5 and q16 are the ClickBench queries; the max_threads = 16 rows add SETTINGS max_threads = 16 to q9 and q10.
```

Concurrency: 4 clients each run the query 4 times; total wall time per binary, 2 rounds in alternating order. Cold runs: fresh server, `echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`, re-read the server binary, one run; 8 pairs in ABBA order.

When the page cache is dropped while the server runs, a first run also reads the query's code from disk, and the two builds lay out their code differently: there, q10 was 3.5% slower in median and q9 unchanged. With the binary re-read after the drop, so that only data is cold, both are unchanged.

</details>

### Expected performance
<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A row whose group and value equal the previous row's should not cost a hash-set insert, as in the keyless path. Data without such repeats should run at the same speed.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests
<details><summary>Related work</summary>

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126 (software prefetch for the same loop, rejected; this issue was requested there)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/124197 (the prefetch patch as a PR, closed)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/128029 (the same kind of skip for `count()`-only `GROUP BY` in the adaptive aggregator; a different loop, which does not cover `uniqExact`)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127940 (skips repeated `LowCardinality` values without `GROUP BY` only)
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/127280 (radix-partitioned keyless `uniqExact`; does not change the `GROUP BY` path)

</details>

### Additional context
The same skip also works for grouped `uniq` (not `uniqCombined`, whose small exact set converts to HyperLogLog on the next insert of any value). That increment and its measurements are in [this comment](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/124126#issuecomment-6448909285); it is not part of the patch below.

<details><summary>Patch (master 8d5702d8, applies to 6624a338)</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h b/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
index 97ec574cb1d..32769462ff9 100644
--- a/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
+++ b/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionUniq.h
@@ -561,6 +561,73 @@ private:
     static constexpr bool is_able_to_parallelize_merge = Data::is_able_to_parallelize_merge;
     static constexpr bool is_parallelize_merge_prepare_needed = Data::is_parallelize_merge_prepare_needed;
     static constexpr bool is_uniques_hash_set = detail::IsUniquesHashSet<DataSet>::value;
+    static constexpr bool is_uniq_exact_set = detail::IsUniqExactSet<DataSet>::value;
+
+    /// `uniqExact` over many places (GROUP BY). A row whose place and value repeat those of the previous row is
+    /// skipped: inserting a key that a set already contains never changes it, and such runs are common in data
+    /// sorted by the grouping and argument columns (as in the keyless path, see `Adder::addManyChunked`).
+    /// The keys of a chunk of rows are collected first. For values that are their own keys the collection is
+    /// branch-free, because short runs make a skip branch mispredict more often than a skipped insert into a small
+    /// set saves; for other values (hashed strings) a repeated row also skips its hash.
+    template <bool check_places>
+    void addBatchExact(size_t row_begin, size_t row_end, AggregateDataPtr * places, size_t place_offset,
+        const IColumn ** columns, ssize_t if_argument_pos) const
+    {
+        using Traits = detail::AggregateFunctionUniqTraits<T, ColumnType>;
+        using Key = typename DataSet::value_type;
+        static constexpr auto hint = is_able_to_parallelize_merge ? SetLevelHint::unknown : SetLevelHint::singleLevel;
+        static constexpr bool value_is_key = std::is_same_v<std::decay_t<decltype(Traits::hashExact(T{}))>, T>;
+        static constexpr size_t chunk_size = 256;
+
+        const char8_t * flags = nullptr;
+        if (if_argument_pos >= 0)
+            flags = assert_cast<const ColumnUInt8 &>(*columns[if_argument_pos]).getData().data();
+        const IColumn & column = *columns[0];
+
+        std::array<Key, chunk_size> keys; // NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init,hicpp-member-init) - only the first `count` entries are read
+        std::array<DataSet *, chunk_size> sets; // NOLINT(cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init,hicpp-member-init)
+        AggregateDataPtr last_place = nullptr;
+        T last_value{};
+
+        size_t row = row_begin;
+        while (row < row_end)
+        {
+            const size_t chunk_end = row + std::min(chunk_size, row_end - row);
+            size_t count = 0;
+            for (; row < chunk_end; ++row)
+            {
+                if constexpr (check_places)
+                {
+                    if (!places[row])
+                        continue;
+                }
+                if (flags && !flags[row])
+                    continue;
+
+                AggregateDataPtr place = places[row] + place_offset;
+                const auto value = Traits::value(column, row);
+                if constexpr (value_is_key)
+                {
+                    const bool repeated = (place == last_place) & bitEquals(value, last_value);
+                    keys[count] = value;
+                    sets[count] = &this->data(place).set;
+                    count += !repeated;
+                }
+                else
+                {
+                    if (place == last_place && bitEquals(value, last_value))
+                        continue;
+                    keys[count] = Traits::hashExact(value);
+                    sets[count++] = &this->data(place).set;
+                }
+                last_place = place;
+                last_value = value;
+            }
+
+            for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
+                sets[i]->template insert<const Key &, hint>(keys[i]);
+        }
+    }
 
 public:
     explicit AggregateFunctionUniq(const DataTypes & argument_types_)
@@ -616,6 +683,8 @@ public:
                 [&](size_t row) { return DataSet::fullHash(Traits::hash(Traits::value(*columns[0], row))); },
                 [&](AggregateDataPtr place) { return &this->data(place).set; });
         }
+        else if constexpr (is_uniq_exact_set)
+            addBatchExact</* check_places = */ true>(row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, if_argument_pos);
         else
             IAggregateFunctionDataHelper<Data, AggregateFunctionUniq<T, ColumnType, Data>>::addBatch(
                 row_begin, row_end, places, place_offset, columns, arena, if_argument_pos);
@@ -626,6 +695,8 @@ public:
     {

+        else if constexpr (is_uniq_exact_set)
```

text:
AsynchronousMetrics logs "Cannot read from file .../cpu.max, errno: 19" every second after systemd disables the cgroup cpu controller

### Company or project name




### Describe what's wrong

`AsynchronousMetrics` opens the cgroup v2 `cpu.max` file once at startup (`openCgroupv2MetricFile("cpu.max", cgroupcpu_max)` in `src/Common/AsynchronousMetrics.cpp`) and re-reads it via `rewind()` through the same descriptor on every update. If systemd later disables the `cpu` controller for the parent slice, the kernel removes `cpu.max`, the kept descriptor starts returning `ENODEV`, and the server logs an error every second until restart:

```
<Error> void DB::AsynchronousMetrics::update(TimePoint, bool): Code: 74. DB::ErrnoException: Cannot read from file /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max: , errno: 19, strerror: No such device
```

`/proc/<pid>/fd` of the server shows the descriptor pointing to a deleted file:

```
/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max (deleted)
```

On Debian 12, systemd enables the `cpu` controller only while some unit needs it. By default that is `user@.service` (`Delegate=pids memory cpu`), which exists only while a user is logged in. So the error appears whenever the server is (re)started from an SSH session and the session is then closed — e.g. after a manual `systemctl restart clickhouse-server` or a package upgrade. When the server starts at boot (nobody logged in, `cpu.max` absent), the error does not appear.

The same happens with `clickhouse-keeper`.


### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes

### How to reproduce

ClickHouse version: 26.10.3.7 (official build, `v26.10.3.7-stable`, git hash `0a1e24c6`), deb package from `packages.clickhouse.com/deb stable main`. I did not run v26.10.2.103 itself, but the relevant code is the same: `src/Common/AsynchronousMetrics.cpp` is unchanged between `v26.10.2.103-stable` (c6428ebc) and the current `26.10` branch head (8365cb6a, already 26.10.3); none of the 29 commits in between touch AsynchronousMetrics or cgroup code.

1. Debian 12 (systemd 252, kernel 6.1, cgroup v2 unified hierarchy), ClickHouse installed from the official deb package, no CPU settings in the unit.
2. Log in via SSH as root (this starts `user@0.service`, systemd enables `cpu` in `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control`, `/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max` appears).
3. `systemctl restart clickhouse-server`
4. Log out, make sure no other user sessions exist.
5. `cpu` disappears from `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control`, `system.slice/cpu.max` is removed, and `clickhouse-server.err.log` gets the error above once per second (~86k lines per day).

The server should not keep failing on a cgroup file that has disappeared. For example: on `ENODEV`/`ENOENT` close the descriptor and re-discover the file on the next update (or treat the limit as "max"), and log it at most once.

Currently the `catch (...)` around the `cpu.max` read only calls `tryLogCurrentException` and keeps the stale descriptor, while the neighbouring `/proc/uptime` block reopens its file in `catch`.

### Error message and/or stacktrace

Code: 74. DB::ErrnoException: Cannot read from file /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max: , errno: 19, strerror: No such device

### Related issues and pull requests

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103968
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/69833

### Additional context

Workaround: make systemd keep the `cpu` controller enabled for the service, e.g. a drop-in with the default weight:

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/clickhouse-server.service.d/cgroup-cpu.conf
[Service]
CPUWeight=100
```

title: AsynchronousMetrics logs "Cannot read from file .../cpu.max, errno: 19" every second after systemd disables the cgroup cpu controller
body:
### Company or project name




### Describe what's wrong

`AsynchronousMetrics` opens the cgroup v2 `cpu.max` file once at startup (`openCgroupv2MetricFile("cpu.max", cgroupcpu_max)` in `src/Common/AsynchronousMetrics.cpp`) and re-reads it via `rewind()` through the same descriptor on every update.
```
<Error> void DB::AsynchronousMetrics::update(TimePoint, bool): Code: 74. DB::ErrnoException: Cannot read from file /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max: , errno: 19, strerror: No such device
```

`/proc/<pid>/fd` of the server shows the descriptor pointing to a deleted file:

```
/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cpu.max (deleted)
```

So the error appears whenever the server is (re)started from an SSH session and the session is then closed — e.g. after a manual `systemctl restart clickhouse-server` or a package upgrade.
